About Fundraise Up

We’re Fundraise Up - a global fundraising platform built to make donating to nonprofits fast, seamless, and accessible to all. Every month, our technology powers tens of millions of dollars in donations across the globe. We focus on innovation that directly impacts results: faster load times, higher conversion rates, global payment support, and accessibility-first design.

Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading nonprofits, including UNICEF, the Alzheimer’s Association, and a wide range of global NGOs. With a 4.9/5 rating across top software review platforms, we’re recognized not just for our impact - but for the quality of the product we deliver.

A Truly Global Product

We operate in the enterprise segment, serving nonprofit organizations across North America, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Europe.

We’re building alarge and complex product ecosystemthat serves nonprofits, donors, and partners around the world. The platform includes a moderncheckout experience and customizable widgets(each a standalone SPA),donor, organization, and partner portals,admin tools, and several internal apps.

The Team

We are a distributed team of 160+ product professionals. Our team members are mainly based across Spain, Poland, Portugal, Georgia, Armenia, Serbia, Turkey, and Cyprus.

Despite our scale, we operate like a focused team - where every task matters and every voice is heard. We value thoughtful collaboration, strong engineering practices, and a product mindset. You’ll be joining a team where quality, mentorship, and mutual respect come first.

About the Role

Gift Cart is one of Fundraise Up's fastest-growing giving surfaces — it lets donors support multiple causes in a single checkout, giving nonprofits a new way to present their programmes and deepen donor engagement beyond a standard donation form. It's already live and scaling across organisations running everything from humanitarian aid to symbolic animal adoptions.

We're looking for a Product Manager to own Gift Cart end-to-end: strategy, discovery, and delivery. You'll shape the roadmap, drive adoption, and grow the metrics that matter — average order value, multi-designation rate, and reliability — while safeguarding the payment and ledger correctness, risk posture, and operability that a financial product demands. This is a full-lifecycle role: you'll go from strategic thinking to engineering-ready specs to launch, working closely with engineering, risk, and design along the way.

If you enjoy owning a product from "why does this matter" through to "it's live and working," this is built for that.

What You’ll Own

  • Define the Gift Cart strategy and translate it into a roadmap — with clear priorities and reasoning behind every decision.
  • Communicate with customers and CSMs regularly, and analyze data together with the analytics team — to find growth opportunities and make informed decisions.
  • Write specifications that engineers can build from — with detailed requirements and edge cases covered.
  • Take features from idea to launch, working closely with design and engineering at every step.
  • Track product health and growth: conversion, average gift size, error rates — and understand what's driving them.
  • Prepare CSMs and Sales for every launch so they're always in context ahead of time.
  • Keep stakeholders aligned — on priorities, timelines, and changes in plans.

Requirements

  • Experience owning a product area end-to-end — you take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.
  • Ability to build a strategy and roadmap for 12–24 months — and clearly explain the reasoning behind your decisions.
  • Data-driven: you analyze funnels, understand the numbers, and know where to look for growth opportunities.
  • You write specifications engineers can build from — clear, with edge cases covered and no open questions left.
  • Systems thinker: you see the product as a whole, understand dependencies, and anticipate the impact of decisions.
  • Strong UX sensibility: you know what makes an experience good and can advocate for it with your team.
  • Comfortable working across functions — design, engineering, analytics, and business stakeholders.

Nice To Have

  • Experience in e-commerce or products with multi-step checkout flows.
  • Experience working with nonprofits, donors, or in the fundraising industry.
  • Experience with payment flows or financial products.

Working model

  • High ownership and direct collaboration with dedicated Engineering TL, Engineers, Designer, Analyst and CSM, Sales teams.
  • We use AI to accelerate analysis, specs, and communication — with clear assumptions and validation.

At Fundraise Up, AI is a default tool — not an experimental one

We expect every team member to actively use AI in their day-to-day work, identify where AI can change the shape of problems in their function, and grow their fluency as the tools evolve. You should already be using AI meaningfully in your work and understand where it adds value and how it can improve the way you operate.

Why work with us

  • A strong, collaborative product team that owns what it builds
  • Clear product vision and access to real customer feedback from global nonprofit leaders
  • Flat structure: no politics, just great work with great people
  • Transparent company culture-we share how we’re growing, where revenue comes from, and what’s next
  • Long-term focus: we offer equity options and value sustained, meaningful contribution

Compensation

  • The compensation range for this role is €5,600 - €6,100 gross.
  • Final compensation will be determined based on relevant experience, skills, qualifications, alignment with the role’s requirements and location.

Benefits

OVERVIEW

Reporting to the VP, Data Management & Program Delivery, the Director, Transition & Integration is accountable for the strategic planning and execution of select large‑scale, complex transitions across the enterprise, including enterprise transformation and strategic capability projects and a critical internal initiative to inhouse services. This role serves as the single point of accountability for end‑to‑end integration success, ensuring continuity of services, sequenced change, risk mitigation, and clear leadership communication throughout all phases of transition.

The Director operates as a central orchestrator, coordinating cross‑functional workstreams, proactively managing dependencies and pressure points, and ensuring that change is introduced in a disciplined, sustainable manner without compromising operational performance or service levels.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead and own the integration and transition roadmap of our select, large-scale initiatives across all phases (plan, mobilize, execute, stabilize).
  • Serve as the single point of accountability for overall transition and integration outcomes.
  • Coordinate cross‑functional workstreams on these initiatives to ensure alignment, readiness, and timely decision‑making.
  • Ensure integration milestones, success measures, and stabilization criteria are clearly defined and tracked by horizon.
  • Act as the enterprise focal point for these initiatives through transition coordination, enabling visibility across the organization.
  • Proactively monitor pressure points and emerging risks across technology, operations, people, and vendors as they relate to the implementation of these initiatives.
  • Surface issues early, escalate decisively, and drive resolution before risks become service disruptions.
  • Maintain a cohesive view of risks, issues, and dependencies across concurrent initiatives in-line with standard organizational risk management protocols.
  • Plan resource demands adequately to avoid parallel constraints and/or concurrent resource demands.
  • Balance the delivery timelines of these initiatives with operational capacity to protect performance, safety, and morale.
  • Partner with business and operational leaders to manage change saturation and ensure realistic execution plans-based timeline constraints.
  • Partner with operational, business and technology leaders to define and monitor continuity plans during transition periods.
  • Ensure service levels, customer outcomes, and regulatory obligations are maintained throughout integration of these initiatives
  • Track transition performance metrics and lead corrective actions where continuity is at risk and establish mitigation strategies to address, resolve or reduce risk profile.
  • Align leadership messaging to ensure clarity, consistency, and confidence throughout the change management lifecycle.
  • Reduce uncertainty by ensuring stakeholders understand what is changing, when, and why.
  • Enable leaders with clear transition narratives, decision points, and risk awareness.
  • Establish and operate effective transition governance structures.
  • Enable timely, informed decisions by synthesizing complex inputs into clear options and trade‑offs.
  • Ensure accountability across workstreams and remove barriers to progress.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Management, Operations, Engineering, or a related discipline required
  • Master’s degree (MBA, MPA, or equivalent) preferred
  • Formal training or certification in program management, change management, or integration methodologies (e.g., PMP, PgMP, Prosci, SAFe, ITIL) considered an asset

Experience

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in enterprise transformation, integration, transition management, or large‑scale program leadership
  • Proven experience leading complex, cross‑functional transitions involving operations, technology, people, and vendors
  • Demonstrated accountability for end‑to‑end integration programs, including roadmap ownership, governance, and stabilization
  • Experience managing concurrent, high‑impact initiatives while maintaining operational continuity
  • Strong background working with executive leadership to enable timely decisions and align messaging
  • Experience in regulated, national, or mission‑critical environments preferred
  • Exposure to in‑housing, operating model shifts, or service delivery transformations is a strong asset

Knowledge/Competencies/Skills

  • Enterprise transition and integration management across complex, multi‑workstream initiatives
  • End‑to‑end ownership of integration roadmaps, milestones, and stabilization outcomes
  • Strong systems thinking with the ability to anticipate downstream operational, technical, and people impacts
  • Advanced risk, issue, and dependency management, with proactive escalation and mitigation
  • Change sequencing and capacity management to prevent operational overload and protect performance
  • Operational readiness assessment and service continuity planning during periods of significant change
  • Governance design and execution, including clear decision rights, escalation paths, and accountability
  • Ability to synthesize complex information into clear options, trade‑offs, and executive recommendations
  • Strong executive presence with the ability to influence and align leaders without direct authority
  • Clear, disciplined communication that reduces uncertainty and aligns leadership messaging
  • Proven ability to coordinate cross‑functional teams across Operations, Technology, HR, Finance, and Vendors
  • Performance monitoring and use of metrics to track transition health and integration success
  • High tolerance for ambiguity with calm, decisive leadership under pressure
  • Results‑oriented mindset with strong accountability for enterprise outcomes
  • Strong organizational awareness and judgment in navigating complex stakeholder environments

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • All CM employees work 40 hours per week, remotely from a Canadian home office environment.
  • This is a remote position with a flexible work schedule and periods of uneven workflow. May require periods of extended working hours to meet deadlines during peak business cycle.

  • A track record of directly owning pipeline or revenue growth outcomes — not just supporting them. You’ve held the number and you know what it takes to hit it.
  • Strong experimentation instincts: you make fast, data-informed decisions about what to scale, optimize, or kill.
  • You think like a growth architect first. Systems, automations, and tooling are levers you pull — not the job itself.
  • Energized by ambiguity and a bias toward action in lean, high-ownership environments.

Technical Aptitude

  • Ability to visualize how data flows through a complex GTM system and spot where it leaks.
  • Hands-on experience designing and building automation workflows across GTM systems, with strong fluency in APIs, integrations, and workflow orchestration tools.
  • Deep familiarity with CRMs (Salesforce/HubSpot) and the surrounding GTM ecosystem — marketing automation, SDR tooling, enrichment platforms, CS platforms, and more.
  • AI-native fluency: you’ve deployed agentic workflows in a GTM context with demonstrable impact, and you use AI daily to move faster without sacrificing quality.

GTM Context & Curiosity

  • You’ve done some of these GTM jobs before, or spent serious time understanding their day-to-day goals and challenges. You build for the rep, not just the system.
  • First-principles problem solver: you ask “Why is this process broken at the root?” not “How do we fix this tool?”
  • Strong systems thinking — connecting channels, lifecycle stages, messaging, and GTM motions into a cohesive growth strategy.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate between business and technical stakeholders.
  • Obsessive learner with a track record of teaching yourself new technologies before they become obvious.

Required Skills

  • 5+ years of experience in GTM Operations, RevOps, Sales/Marketing Systems, Growth, or Automation Engineering.
  • Proven experience designing and building automation workflows across GTM systems.
  • Hands-on experience with AI-powered technologies, agents, or autonomous GTM systems.
  • Strong technical fluency, including experience with Salesforce, APIs, integrations, and workflow orchestration tools.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate between business and technical stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.

Preferred Skills

  • SQL proficiency for self-serve data analysis, debugging, and validation.
  • Hands-on experience with HubSpot, Salesforce, Qualified, RB2B, Clay, or similar enrichment and analytics platforms.
  • Experience building internal tools or lightweight UIs to unify data across systems.
  • Background in B2B SaaS.

Our Values

As a Founding hire of this function, you will embody our core values:

  • Confident Humility: We lean into our strengths but “know what we don’t know.” You’ll bring bold ideas to the Senior Leadership Team while viewing asking for help as a sign of strength.
  • Mission-Driven Ownership: You take responsibility for anything that affects the OTS mission, even if it’s “not in your job description.”
  • Compassionate Candor: Direct communication is the fastest way to find solutions. You’ll give and receive honest feedback to help our GTM engine scale.
  • Teamwork: We are all rowing in the same canoe. There is no such thing as “somebody else’s problem.”Grit: Building something great is hard. You embrace the uncertainty of bold goals with passion and perseverance.
  • Kaizen: You believe that getting 1% better every day compounds into massive outcomes.

About On The Stage

On The Stage (OTS) started in the arts — and we’ve never left. What began as a platform built for theatre makers has grown into the ticketing, marketing, and fundraising engine powering the full spectrum of live entertainment: from K–12 drama programs and community theatres to professional performing arts organizations, comedy clubs, music venues, multi-venue entertainment complexes, immersive experiences, and location-based entertainment.

Founded by Tony and Olivier Award-winning Broadway producer Hunter Arnold alongside Silicon Valley tech veterans, we were built from the inside out — by people who came from the arts and understood what was missing. That origin shapes everything: the language we use, the problems we prioritize, and the conviction that every live entertainment producer — non-profit or commercial, a school drama teacher or a West End producer — deserves access to the same infrastructure that powers Broadway.

Today, OTS serves thousands of organizations across the US — non-profits and commercial producers alike. Our all-in-one platform delivers Broadway-caliber infrastructure: ticketing with mobile-first checkout, a native CRM, automated marketing, a full fundraising suite, in-checkout revenue accelerators, and real-time reporting — all sharing a single patron record. Whether the goal is filling seats, cultivating donors, or maximizing revenue per transaction, every feature serves one mission: helping live entertainment organizations endure, expand, and prosper.

We believe in power without complexity — intuitive enough for a solo educator to launch in minutes, sophisticated enough to power the most complex commercial productions. OTS is at a pivotal growth stage, and the GTM infrastructure we build today will directly shape how we reach and serve the next wave of live entertainment organizations. This role sits at the center of that.

For more information, visit: www.OnTheStage.com

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

On The Stage (OTS) is at an inflection point. As our Founding GTM Engineer, you won’t just maintain systems — you’ll be the architect of how we generate pipeline, expand accounts, and compound growth across the business. You'll partner closely with our GTM Operations Manager, who will own the reliability and architecture of the systems you build on, and together you'll ensure OTS operates with a single version of the truth from top-of-funnel through revenue

This is a growth ownership role first. The right person owns outcomes — pipeline generated, upgrades driven, adoption accelerated — and builds the systems and automations that make those outcomes repeatable and scalable. If you can own growth at this level, the efficiency and enablement work comes naturally. The reverse is not true, and we’re not hiring for the reverse.

This is a strategic, high-visibility role reporting directly to the SVP of CS & Business Operations, with direct exposure to the Senior Leadership Team.

Director of Product Commercialization is a new role at Halo Collar. This person will be responsible for bringing new products and services to market, owning the end-to-end process from product development through post-launch review. You will coordinate cross-functional teams and external vendors, and build the go-to-market strategies and operational infrastructure that make launches successful.

Reporting to the VP, Marketing Operations, you will serve as the connective tissue between Brand, Merchandising, Planning, Product Development, Operations, Mobile App, and Marketing. This is an opportunity to join a high-growth brand at a pivotal moment in its operational transformation, building the systems this function needs largely from scratch.

Responsibilities

Cross-Functional Orchestration

  • Serve as the central coordination point across internal teams and external partners, including Engineering, Product Development, Brand, Marketing, Packaging, Operations, Supply Chain, Retail, Legal, Planning, and overseas manufacturing partners
  • Build trusted working relationships across every function, with the discipline to keep a large, distributed team aligned across time zones, technical disciplines, and competing priorities
  • Balance decisiveness with judgment on when to decide independently versus escalate, align, or bring others into the decision
  • Translate technical engineering constraints into business and marketing impacts, and vice versa
  • Lead regular cross-functional syncs and deliver structured status updates to the team and leadership

Portfolio and Program Visibility

  • Manage a concurrent portfolio of product tracks at different stages — new products, line extensions, product changes, and accessories — each with distinct timelines and dependencies
  • Own portfolio-level visibility in Asana, maintaining initiative-level status
  • Deliver structured status reporting on a regular cadence covering where each track stands, what is at risk, and what decisions are needed

Product Development Coordination

  • Own the sample and approval review calendar for every active product track: shipping schedule, reviewers, go/no-go criteria, and what happens when samples fail
  • Understand hardware development stage gates well enough to hold the line on what must be true before downstream marketing and GTM gates can open
  • Serve alongside Operations as liaison to overseas manufacturing partners on production milestones, tooling schedules, quality control checkpoints, and packaging timelines
  • Coordinate firmware scope and app readiness as parallel launch dependencies with the digital product team, so software tracks are gated and visible alongside hardware milestones

Launch Planning and Execution

  • Own end-to-end GTM execution for every new product launch, from product development through retail shelf placement, acquisition marketing, and post-launch review
  • Build and maintain cross-functional launch plans with clear milestones, work stream owners, and handoffs
  • Manage dual-channel launches where DTC/eCommerce and retail timelines run in parallel
  • Work with Retail to define retail readiness as a distinct deliverable: planogram specs, sell-in packets, retailer-specific packaging compliance, and submission timelines
  • Build the master launch timeline across teams and vendor partners, surfacing risk before it reaches the critical path
  • Run post-launch retrospectives and feed learnings into future launch planning

Change Control and Regulatory Compliance

  • Own the change control process post style-freeze: define what triggers a formal change request, who approves it, and what the downstream impact assessment covers - protecting Packaging, Retail, Marketing, and Operations from late disruption
  • Maintain visibility into certification requirements, including whether a design or supplier change requires new certification or falls under an existing approval
  • Ensure no launch ships without confirmed regulatory clearance, and own the escalation path when certification timelines are at risk
  • Build organizational discipline around change control over time, reducing the frequency and cost of post-freeze changes across the portfolio

Launch Cost Visibility

  • Maintain a current per-SKU cost model for every launch — material, tooling amortization, freight, duties, and fulfillment fees against margin targets — and keep it current through every design or supplier change
  • Partner with Planning and Operations to flag margin risk before launch decisions are made


Required Qualifications

  • 7-10 years of cross-functional product launch or commercialization experience, with a track record of bringing physical or hardware/software products to market at speed across multiple departments simultaneously
  • Comfortable in a growth-phase scaling environment where systems are being built alongside the business, including sequencing early wins to create momentum for harder changes
  • Experience owning launch timelines across engineering, supply chain, and go-to-market concurrently
  • Consumer hardware, pet tech, wearables, or connected device background strongly preferred; understands what makes a hardware-software-subscription product fundamentally different from a pure software launch
  • Retail channel experience with PetSmart, Amazon, and specialty retail programs, including lead times, compliance requirements, submission processes, and the difference between DTC and retail launch calendars
  • Willingness to work across multiple time zones, including overseas (Asia)
  • Enough regulatory literacy to manage certification timelines as a launch risk, including recognizing when a supplier or design change triggers new certification
  • Strong program management instincts: plans that hold, and clear judgment on when to push versus when to pause
  • Able to get clear answers from engineers, creatives, ops managers, and retail buyers in the same week
  • Proficiency in Asana and Jira, or a comparable project management platform, with experience maintaining initiative-level visibility for a full leadership team

Preferred Qualifications

  • Background spanning both a startup scaling phase and a more established operational environment, with experience building process rather than just inheriting it
  • Experience coordinating with contract manufacturers and 3PL fulfillment partners on launch timing and inventory readiness
  • Familiarity with supplier changes, ECNs, and BOM revisions interact with assembly timelines


Perks of the Pack

  • Company-paid Long-Term Disability
  • 401k with Company Match
  • Paid Time Off
  • Free Halo gear + Product Testing Opportunities
  • Work remotely from anywhere in the U.S.

POSITION TITLE:Infrastructure and Database Team Lead

Supervised by:IT Operations Manager

Supervises: Database Team members, Infrastructure Team members, Solution Analyst(s)

FLSA Status: Exempt / Full-Time

POSITION SUMMARY. MediQuant helps more than 250 health systems and hospital networks retire, secure, and modernize their legacy healthcare data. As Infrastructure & Database Team Lead, you’ll own the infrastructure, systems, and standards that make it possible.

The Infrastructure & Database Team Lead owns the availability, reliability, security, and performance of MediQuant infrastructure, cloud, and database environments — both the systems that run MediQuant business and the platforms that power services for its healthcare clients. This role leads a combined technical team, sets standards across both domains, and partners closely with the IT Operations Manager on roadmap, budget, and compliance priorities.

JOB DUTIES and ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS. A qualified individual must be able to perform these essential functions of the job as listed, with or without accommodation.

  1. Infrastructure, Cloud & Database Operations
    1. Owns day-to-day operations, performance monitoring, and configuration of MediQuant’s infrastructure, cloud, and database environments — both internal and client-facing.
    2. Owns the Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BCDR) process, documentation, and testing across infrastructure and database systems.
    3. Leads incident, problem, and change management for escalated infrastructure and database issues through to resolution; documents root cause and resolution in knowledge base articles.
    4. Develops and maintains the infrastructure and database services roadmap in partnership with the IT Operations Manager.
    5. Monitors service levels and communicates proactively with internal stakeholders and clients on status, risk, and incidents, operating within the SLAs/OLAs negotiated by the IT Operations Manager.
    6. Ensures the team maintains on-call/escalation coverage, escalating unresolved gaps to the IT Operations Manager.
  2. Compliance & Data Security
    1. Owns execution of HIPAA and HITRUST CSF compliance controls for infrastructure and database systems, including evidence collection supporting MediQuant’s HITRUST r2 certification. The IT Operations Manager holds operational compliance accountability; the Information Security Manager holds final compliance program ownership and audit sign-off.
    2. Ensures data integrity, access controls, and secure handling of Confidential Data and PHI across all systems under this role’s oversight.
    3. Partners with Security/Compliance leadership on audit readiness, risk assessments, and remediation tracking.
  3. Project & Portfolio Governance
    1. Scopes, sequences, and manages a portfolio of infrastructure and database projects: resourcing, milestone tracking, cost/benefit analysis, and risk management.
    2. Assembles project teams, assigns responsibilities, and coordinates with the PMO/project management function on schedule and dependencies.
    3. Independently verifies the actual state of systems, projects, and initiatives owned by this role, rather than relying solely on team- or vendor-reported status.
    4. Proactively escalates risk, slippage, or emerging issues to the IT Operations Manager in advance of impact, with a recommended course of action.
    5. Prepare status reports for upper management.
  4. Vendor & Budget Management
    1. Leads technical evaluation of infrastructure and database vendors and tooling (e.g., cloud provider technical support, database platform vendors) and recommends vendor selection and RFP/NDA/MSA terms on the technical side; the IT Operations Manager approves contractor and tooling spend within budget.
    2. Provides budget input (actual-vs-planned technology spend for infrastructure and database systems) to the IT Operations Manager, who consolidates it into budget requests to the Director, IT.
    3. Monitors Azure resource utilization and spend, recommending rightsizing or reserved-capacity opportunities to control cloud cost.
  5. Team Leadership & Performance Management
    1. Builds 30-60-90-day onboarding plans and conducts onboarding one-on-ones for new hires; provides input for their early (90-day) performance review.
    2. Holds regular one-on-ones and conducts performance reviews at agreed intervals (90-day, semi-annual, annual) against competency standards set by Technology Leadership; the IT Operations Manager holds final accountability for ratings, salary discussions, and issuance.
    3. Builds a day-to-day learning environment; identifies and nominates staff for training, coursework, and certifications. The IT Operations Manager approves and funds training and certification investment.
    4. Manages timekeeping and leave administration for direct reports, including approval of timecards, PTO, and schedule adjustments to maintain operational coverage and payroll accuracy.
    5. Interviews and evaluates candidates and recommends hire/no-hire decisions, partnering with Human Resources throughout; the IT Operations Manager holds final hiring sign-off.
    6. Recommends performance ratings and Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs) to the IT Operations Manager for sign-off, and implements approved PIPs and other approved personnel actions.
  6. Team Resourcing & Succession
    1. Owns daily task, shift, and queue allocation to meet coverage and delivery commitments for the team.
    2. Identifies and closes cross-training and skill-gap coverage needs within the team.
    3. Translates IT Operations Manager-set team goals into day-to-day priorities and assignments.
    4. Provides input on intra-team staffing and FTE allocation; the IT Operations Manager owns final allocation decisions.
    5. Recommends succession candidates and escalates staffing or resourcing risk to the IT Operations Manager.
  7. Documentation & Knowledge Management
    1. Ensures documentation and knowledge articles for infrastructure and database processes, releases, and recurring incidents are created and maintained, feeding into the IT Operations Manager’s broader IT documentation and leadership reporting.
    2. Leads the team in developing training materials and onboarding documentation for automated deployment and support processes.

QUALIFICATIONS

Competencies:

  • Critical Thinking
  • Technical Acumen — Infrastructure & Database
  • Professionalism and Composure
  • Documentation Skills
  • Interpersonal and Communication Skills
  • Flexibility and Self-Motivation
  • Team Leadership and Coaching

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field; equivalent work experience will be considered in lieu of degree.
  • 3+ years of progressive infrastructure/cloud experience with Microsoft technologies (Azure, Windows Server, Microsoft 365), or 3+ years of hands-on SQL Server database administration experience — with working fluency in the other domain.
  • 1+ years of experience mentoring, informally leading, or coordinating technical staff or project delivery.
  • Experience owning BCDR, incident management, or change management in a regulated environment.
  • Hands-on administration experience in Azure infrastructure, Windows Server, and Microsoft 365 (identity, endpoint management, Exchange Online) and/or SQL Server database administration (backup/recovery, performance tuning, high-availability configuration).

Additional Eligibility Qualifications:

  • Microsoft certifications such as Azure Administrator Associate, Azure Database Administrator Associate, Windows Server Hybrid Administrator Associate, or Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert.
  • Experience supporting healthcare or other highly regulated clients.

Work Environment. Employees may work from our corporate headquarters or work from home. Employees may at times be required to travel to headquarters for meetings or company events. Remote workers will be provided with a company laptop and are responsible for maintaining access to high-speed internet.

Physical Demands.While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to sit for long periods of time, stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

Position Type and Expected Hours of Work.This is a full-time position, and the hours of work and days are typically Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Some flexibility in hours is allowed, but the employee must be available during the “core” work hours of 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Occasional evening and weekend work may be required as job duties demand.

Travel. Incumbent may occasionally experience some out-of-the-area and overnight travel.

Work Authorization. In compliance with Federal employment laws, MediQuant will verify the identity and employment authorization of each person hired. MediQuant participates in the Federal E-Verify program.

Security Clearance.Must be able to pass all security clearances mandated by various government contracts as well as client hospital/healthcare security requirements. Any employee working on government projects will be required to successfully pass a government background check and receive a Common Access Card (CAC). Additionally, the applicant must be a U.S. citizen and will be subject to a Public Trust security background investigation and must meet requirements to obtain a Department of Defense (DOD) network account.

AAP/EEO Statement.MediQuant, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer.

Compliance. Employees shall comply with all MediQuant policies, state and federal laws, regulations, and contractual obligations when accessing MediQuant or client Confidential Data, Confidential Information, and Information Assets.

Other Duties.Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time.

Care Access is working to make the future of health better for all. How This Role Makes a Difference

Central Clinical Services enables decentralized and hybrid clinical trials by providing staff who virtually support patients and sites. The RA is accountable for study delivery at the patient level and is expected to support the patient experience, data management, and other study administrative tasks with a quality-first approach. jobs.excerpt: Senior Substation Constructability & Quality Review SpecialistLeidos is seeking an experienced field operations professional to support engineering quality reviews and constructability reviews for high-voltage and EHV substation design packages.
jobs.description:
Senior Substation Constructability & Quality Review Specialist

Leidos is seeking an experienced field operations professional to support engineering quality reviews and constructability reviews for high-voltage and EHV substation design packages. This role is ideal for someone who has spent their career in the field — leading crews, maintaining equipment, and troubleshooting live systems — and now wants to bring that hands-on judgment to the front end of project design, catching issues before they become costly problems in the field. This position sits within our EPC Solutions group, part of the Power Delivery Solutions division, supporting consulting and EPC delivery for investor-owned and public utility clients nationwide.

What You'll Do:

Design & Constructability Review

  • Perform constructability reviews of substation physical and P&C design packages, identifying field-impractical details, sequencing conflicts, and access/clearance issues before construction.
  • Review designs for accessibility, equipment clearances, installation requirements, maintenance access, equipment removal/replacement, vehicle and crane access, cable installation, temporary facilities, and construction means and methods.
  • Conduct quality reviews of engineering drawing deliverables (one-lines, physical layouts, panel schedules, wiring diagrams, grounding, etc.) to flag errors, omissions, and conflicts based on real-world installation and maintenance experience.
  • Identify design conditions that could create unnecessary field labor, rework, difficult installation, operational constraints, safety concerns, or long-term maintenance challenges.
  • Identify design features that may create unnecessary operational complexity or maintenance burden.
  • Review bills of materials for completeness, accuracy, and alignment with actual field installation needs.
  • Review construction sequencing plans and construction schedules for feasibility, identifying gaps between the design intent and how the work will actually be built and energized.

Brownfield & Energized Substation Work

  • Provide field-informed recommendations for brownfield construction where work must occur adjacent to or within existing energized substations.
  • Draw on extensive brownfield substation experience — phased construction, equipment replacement, temporary configurations, and constrained outages — to inform design and planning decisions.
  • Support outage planning and evaluate proposed solutions to unforeseen construction conditions in live or partially energized environments.

Field Support & Knowledge Transfer

  • Provide technical field support during construction, outages, commissioning, and energization when required.
  • Assist project teams in resolving field questions and evaluating proposed solutions to unforeseen construction conditions.
  • Provide lessons learned from field failures, equipment maintenance, emergency repairs, and troubleshooting activities to improve engineering designs.
  • Participate in site walks, constructability reviews, pre-construction meetings, and outage planning meetings.
  • Flag design elements likely to cause safety, maintenance, or operational challenges once the substation is in service.

Collaboration & Mentorship

  • Participate in design review meetings and job-site visits, serving as the “voice of the field” alongside engineering staff.
  • Coordinate with project engineers, project managers, and construction teams to resolve identified issues.
  • Document review findings, comments, and recommendations in a clear, trackable format.
  • Mentor junior staff on practical field considerations in design and construction planning.

What Sets You Apart (Background Requirements):

  • 10+ years of hands-on experience in substation or transmission operations, construction, or maintenance — e.g., leading construction crews, performing equipment maintenance, or troubleshooting during outages.
  • No engineering degree required; equivalent field experience and demonstrated technical judgment substitute for formal education.
  • Experience at 138 kV, 230 kV, 345 kV, 500 kV, or higher voltage levels.
  • Experience leading construction or maintenance crews in energized substations.
  • Extensive brownfield substation experience involving phased construction, equipment replacement, temporary configurations, and constrained outages.

jobs.excerpt: Gcore WAAP protects customer web applications and APIs against DDoS, bots, and application-layer attacks at CDN edge scale.
jobs.description:
Gcore WAAP protects customer web applications and APIs against DDoS, bots, and application-layer attacks at CDN edge scale. We are building out a proactive, managed-support offering for enterprise customers, and we need a SOC Analyst to run the day-to-day security operations: watch traffic and alerts, triage false positives, prepare customer-facing threat reports, and escalate real impact to the right team. You will work alongside our Threat Researchers, taking the operational load off them so they can focus on deep analysis. You do not need to be a threat-hunting expert.

You need to be reliable, observant, comfortable in logs and dashboards, and able to tell an attack from legitimate traffic - and know when to escalate.

What You Will Do

  • Monitor WAAP and DDoS activity across customer accounts - dashboards, alerts, and traffic patterns - and recognize when something needs attention.
  • Triage false positives: review traffic flagged by security policies, confirm or dismiss, and keep noise down for customers (this is a large, daily part of the job).
  • Prepare reports: weekly threat summaries per customer and post-incident DDoS reports, in clear customer-facing English.
  • Alert and escalate: when an attack is impacting a customer, signal the engineering team or Support with the right context - e.g. a customer needs to be tagged or a policy adjusted - and follow the escalation runbook.
  • Support customer onboarding: apply standard security configuration based on the customer's profile (resource type, traffic volume, legitimate-traffic exclusions) following playbooks.
  • Follow the reaction-time SLA - our commitment to customers is speed of reaction and clear post-incident reporting, not a prevention guarantee.
  • Contribute to and maintain runbooks so responses are consistent and repeatable.

What We are Looking For

  • Understanding of web security fundamentals: WAF, DDoS, bots, OWASP Top 10.
  • Solid basics in HTTP, TCP/IP, TLS.
  • Comfortable analyzing logs and reading dashboards; can spot anomalies in traffic.
  • Able to distinguish malicious from legitimate traffic and reason about false positives.
  • Clear written English for customer-facing reports.
  • Reliable, detail-oriented, and calm under incident pressure.
  • Willingness to work in a shift/on-call rotation.

Nice to Have

  • Prior SOC L1/L2 or related experience.
  • Basic query/scripting: SQL-like log queries, regex, a bit of Python.
  • Familiarity with CDN/WAF platforms (Cloudflare, Akamai, Imperva, F5, Radware).
  • Exposure to SIEM / alerting tooling and PagerDuty-style on-call.
  • Security certifications (e.g. CompTIA Security+) - a plus, not a requirement.

Explicitly NOT Required

  • Deep threat research, exploit development, malware reverse-engineering. That work stays with our Threat Researchers - this role feeds them clean, triaged signal and takes the routine off their plate.

Why This Role Matters

You become the first line of Gcore WAAP's managed security operations - the person who keeps customers informed and protected day to day, and who lets our specialists focus on the hard problems. High visibility, direct customer impact, and a clear path to grow into threat research or detection engineering.

Benefits

At Gcore, we want you to do your best work and enjoy the journey. Our benefits are designed to support your growth, well-being, and life beyond work:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Flexible working hours and hybrid or remote options, depending on your role
  • Work from anywhere in the world for up to 45 days per year
  • Private medical insurance for you and your family*
  • Extra paid vacation and sick leave days*
  • Support for life’s important moments and celebrations
  • Language courses to help you connect and grow
  • Modern, welcoming offices with snacks, drinks, and entertainment*
  • Team sports and social activities*

*Benefits may vary depending on your location.

Equal Opportunity Employer

We provide equal opportunity to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, disability, or any other legally protected characteristics.

This position is available only under an employment (labor) agreement.

The world’s digital experiences run on something invisible: the infrastructure and software that keep them fast, reliable, and secure. At Gcore, you’ll help design and deliver that foundation for an AI-driven world.

We’re a global provider of infrastructure and software solutions for AI, cloud, network, and security, powering everything from real-time communication and streaming to enterprise AI and secure web applications. With 210+ edge locations, 50+ cloud regions, and thousands of GPUs, your work here can reach users and businesses across the globe.

You’ll collaborate with leading technology partners such as Intel, NVIDIA, Dell, and Equinix, and work on platforms that power digital products used around the world. Our vision is simple: to connect the world to AI, anywhere, anytime.

jobs.description:
GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026.

Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

Location: Remote, with a requirement to overlap with an East Africa timezone by at least 3 hours. We can only employ people in certain places at the moment, so it's worth checking our current list of eligible countries to see if yours is included. If you're based elsewhere, it's not an automatic no, but do flag it early with your recruiter. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time.

About this role

GD moves cash directly into the hands of people living in poverty, often in contexts with limited infrastructure and oversight. Protecting that cash from fraud — whether attempted by external bad actors, field staff, or recipients — is core to our mission and to donor trust. Internal Audit is GD's second line of defense against fraud, and this role sits at the center of it.

We're looking for a Data Analyst who can turn raw operational, payments, and enrollment data into a clear picture of where fraud risk is emerging across our programs, translate those patterns into recommendations that change how projects are designed, and partner with our Product team to build the tools that help us catch fraud earlier and more reliably. You'll move fluidly between deep analysis, clear storytelling to stakeholders who aren't data specialists, and hands-on collaboration with engineers and product managers.

This role sits within Internal Audit but has a dotted reporting line to the Director of Data in order to ensure we meet the organisational technical quality bar and standardise analytical and engineering practises and ways of working across the organisation. Internal Audit owns fraud-risk questions, indicator definitions, investigative analysis, and interpretation, while the central Data team owns shared data infrastructure, production pipelines, governed data models, and platform standards. The analyst bridges the two: contributing domain requirements, validation, and quality assurance, and ensuring this work aligns with organization-wide analytical and engineering practices.

You are as comfortable in a spreadsheet or SQL console as you are in a room with country program leads explaining why a trend matters and what to do about it. You default to evidence over instinct, but you know that a good insight is only useful if someone acts on it.

What you'll do

  • Analyze fraud risk trends: Mine enrollment, payment, survey, and field-operations data to identify patterns, anomalies, and emerging fraud typologies (e.g., duplicate enrollments, collusion, identity fraud, diversion of funds) across GD's programs and geographies.
  • Design and oversee fraud-risk indicators: Build, validate, and maintain recurring monitoring in partnership with central data and operational control owners.
  • Identify data quality issues in data currently collected by Internal Audit, and help design and implement process improvements to resolve them.
  • Embed data-driven thinking into IA design: Identify fraud-related decisions where GiveDirectly should be more data-driven, and incorporate this into Internal Audit process design.
  • Translate findings into action: Package analysis into clear, credible briefs and presentations for country teams, operations leadership, and senior management, with concrete recommendations for reducing fraud risk.
  • Support fraud investigations: Provide data pulls, quantify exposure, and help reconstruct events for specific cases — ensuring analysis is reproducible and audit-ready, with documented queries, data lineage, assumptions, exclusions, and QA checks.
  • Partner with Product and Central Data on fraud-detection tooling: Translate validated risk signals into product requirements, contribute domain expertise and acceptance criteria, and test whether controls operate as intended — while maintaining clear ownership and independence boundaries.
  • Partner with Data Engineering on upstream data quality and pipeline improvements, while owning the downstream analytical layer.
  • Strengthen methodology over time: Back-test risk indicators against investigated cases, monitor precision, coverage, and false-positive rates, and refine based on outcomes and emerging risks.
  • Communicate uncertainty honestly: Distinguish confirmed fraud from suspicious-but-unconfirmed patterns, helping stakeholders make decisions without overstating findings.

What you'll bring

  • 4+ years of experience in data analysis, audit, risk, or a related analytical role; experience in internal audit, fraud/forensics, or a nonprofit/development context is a plus but not required.
  • Strong SQL skills and comfort working directly in large, sometimes messy operational datasets (Salesforce data, payments data, survey data).
  • Experience using Python for reproducible analysis, automation, record linkage, anomaly investigation, or data-quality testing is strongly preferred.
  • Familiarity with analytical notebooks, version control, and documenting analysis so it can be reviewed and reproduced by others is a plus.
  • Experience with visualization tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau, Power BI) and/or Python/R for analysis.
  • Demonstrated ability to turn ambiguous, exploratory analysis into a clear, defensible narrative for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience or strong interest in working cross-functionally with product and engineering teams to translate analytical needs into product requirements.
  • Sound judgment on evidence quality: knowing the difference between a real signal and noise, and communicating that distinction transparently.
  • High integrity and discretion — this role will have visibility into sensitive information about staff, recipients, and active investigations.
  • Alignment with GiveDirectly's values, including prioritizing recipient wellbeing above all else.

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income.

  • Bonus at Target Performance: 10% (~$10,707, with potential for upside. For reference, with the organization’s current performance multiplier, this amount would be $12,527 in 2025)
  • Estimated Total Compensation at Target: $117,777

This role is fully remote, so if you are not based in the US, UK or Kenya, we will share an estimated salary benchmark for the country you are based in during the hiring process.

Why work at GiveDirectly?

At GiveDirectly, we work to ensure that you have everything you need to excel in your role and on your team, including:

Working at GiveDirectly

Reporting to a passionate and driven Product Director, this is an incredible opportunity for an experienced product manager who owns hard problems end to end and is technically fluent enough to earn engineering's confidence, shape platform and API decisions, and get hands-on to de-risk an idea.

  • Fluency with modern AI tooling as part of your working practice.

Location: Remote

About STERRY

At STERRY, we help ambitious brands scale through data-driven marketing strategies that deliver measurable results. Over the years, we've helped clients generate more than $100 million in trackable online revenue across crowdfunding, e-commerce, and growth-focused campaigns. We're currently supporting the growth of a logistics technology platform and are looking for a sharp, ambitious, and commercially minded Marketing Director to help scale the business globally.

The Role
This is a unique opportunity for someone who enjoys owning both strategy and execution. As Marketing Director, you'll bridge the gap between B2B supply chain marketing and technology platform growth, building and optimizing the marketing engine that attracts, converts, and retains 3PL partners and platform users worldwide.

Working directly with the CEO and collaborating with cross-functional teams, you'll be responsible for everything from high-level growth planning and market expansion initiatives to campaign execution, outreach strategy, funnel optimization, and performance analysis. We're looking for someone who understands the logistics landscape, knows how to market a B2B platform or marketplace, and enjoys rolling up their sleeves to make things happen.

Key Responsibilities
Marketing Strategy & Growth
  • Own and execute the company's global marketing strategy, including brand positioning, demand generation, content marketing, SEO, paid media, email marketing, and product marketing.
  • Develop and optimize inbound and outbound marketing funnels that drive qualified 3PL partnerships and platform sign-ups.
  • Build scalable lead generation systems and nurturing programs across email, LinkedIn, and other acquisition channels.
  • Develop compelling messaging and positioning that resonates with 3PL providers, e-commerce merchants, and supply chain stakeholders.
  • Partner closely with the CEO to align marketing initiatives with business objectives, market expansion plans, and strategic partnerships.
  • Continuously evaluate growth opportunities, customer acquisition strategies, and market trends to support business growth.
3PL Research, Outreach & Partnership Development
  • Identify, research, and evaluate potential 3PL partners across global markets based on capabilities, geographic coverage, and strategic fit.
  • Build and maintain a structured database of prospective partners, including service offerings, contact information, engagement history, and partnership status.
  • Execute outreach campaigns through email, LinkedIn, and other channels to introduce the platform and generate partnership opportunities.
  • Conduct initial qualification and discovery conversations to assess partnership potential and business fit.
  • Prepare prospect profiles, competitive analyses, service gap assessments, and recommended engagement strategies.
  • Manage ongoing follow-up and relationship-building efforts throughout the partnership pipeline.
  • Monitor and respond to inbound partnership inquiries, emails, and direct messages in a timely and professional manner.
  • Support and oversee social media activities related to partner engagement and brand visibility.
  • Manage and mentor team members and virtual assistants responsible for 3PL sourcing and outreach initiatives.
Analytics, Platform Performance & Market Intelligence
  • Monitor website traffic, user behavior, order flows, conversion rates, and user journeys to identify growth opportunities and areas for optimization.
  • Track and report on key performance indicators including MQLs, sign-ups, conversion rates, customer acquisition costs (CAC), lifetime value (LTV), and campaign performance.
  • Analyze acquisition channels, user engagement metrics, and conversion paths to improve platform performance.
  • Review order activity and operational trends, escalating issues and identifying opportunities for process improvements.
  • Prepare weekly and monthly reports highlighting growth performance, outreach effectiveness, partnership pipeline status, and strategic recommendations.
  • Conduct ongoing competitor analysis and monitor logistics industry trends, pricing changes, market developments, and emerging opportunities.
Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Lead and mentor a growing cross-functional team supporting marketing, outreach, research, design, development, and growth initiatives.
  • Directly oversee the 3PL Searching & Outreach team, ensuring sourcing pipelines, outreach efforts, and engagement targets are achieved.
  • Collaborate with design, development, operations, and data teams to improve customer experience and optimize growth initiatives.
  • Establish clear goals, reporting structures, workflows, and performance expectations across the team.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and data-driven decision-making.
Executive Partnership & Operational Support
  • Serve as a strategic partner to the CEO on growth initiatives, partnership development, and market expansion opportunities.
  • Coordinate projects across multiple stakeholders, ensuring priorities remain aligned and execution stays on track.
  • Conduct ad hoc market research, competitive analysis, and business intelligence projects to support strategic decision-making.
  • Assist with scheduling, communications, meeting preparation, and executive follow-ups related to key initiatives.
  • Support meeting documentation, action-item tracking, and project coordination.
  • Coordinate travel arrangements and logistics for partnership meetings, conferences, and industry events when required.
Team Structure This role will directly lead and collaborate with:
  • 3PL Searching Lead
  • 3PL Searching Assistant
What We're Looking For:

Logistics & 3PL Industry Expertise You have hands-on experience within the logistics, freight forwarding, fulfillment, supply chain, shipping, or 3PL technology ecosystem. You understand how logistics providers operate, the challenges they face, and how purchasing and partnership decisions are made.

Strategic Yet Hands-On You can confidently move between quarterly growth planning and day-to-day execution. Whether it's refining a go-to-market strategy, reviewing campaign performance, writing outreach messaging, or optimizing conversion funnels, you're comfortable owning the details.

Data-Driven Decision Maker You don't just look at traffic reports—you understand user behavior, conversion paths, acquisition performance, and growth metrics. You know how to turn data into actionable recommendations and work effectively with developers and technical teams to improve outcomes.

Strong Communicator & Relationship Builder You can confidently present performance updates and market insights to executive leadership while maintaining clear communication with partners, prospects, and internal teams. You build trust quickly and represent the company professionally across global markets.

Qualifications
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business Administration, or Communications, or related field is a plus— but what truly matters is what you can build. A standout portfolio or equivalent hands-on experience is just as valued.
  • 6–8+ years of experience in marketing, growth, business development, partnerships, or related leadership roles.
  • Proven success within a 3PL, logistics, freight forwarding, B2B supply chain technology, marketplace, or related environment.
  • Strong understanding of both inbound and outbound lead generation strategies.
  • Experience designing and executing outreach and nurturing sequences across email, LinkedIn, and other channels.
  • Deep understanding of global logistics markets, industry dynamics, pricing structures, and competitive landscapes.
  • Experience managing cross-functional teams and driving business growth initiatives.
  • Strong analytical skills with experience using modern marketing and analytics platforms.
  • Familiarity with Google Analytics, Hotjar, CRM systems, automation tools, and reporting platforms.
  • Shopify and broader e-commerce ecosystem experience is highly preferred.
  • Strong project management, stakeholder management, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to thrive in a remote, fast-paced, and growth-oriented environment
Why Join STERRY?

This is an opportunity to play a key role in building and scaling a growing global platform while working directly with leadership. You'll have the autonomy to shape strategy, influence business decisions, build meaningful partnerships, and create measurable impact within an industry undergoing rapid transformation.

Job Title: Legacy System Export Developer (PeopleSoft/EBS)Job Category: Information TechnologyTime Type: Full timeMinimum Clearance Required to Start: NoneEmployee Type: RegularPercentage of Travel Required: Up to 10%Type of Travel: Continental US* * *

The Opportunity:

CACI is seeking an experienced Senior Consultant with deep PeopleSoft HRMS and Oracle E‑Business Suite (EBS) HCM expertise to support a large federal HCM modernization initiative. You will play a key role in migrating federal civilian employee records from legacy HR platforms into Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM—supporting multiple agencies and delivering enterprise‑grade data conversion solutions.

This is an opportunity to influence a high‑visibility modernization program, solve complex data challenges, and directly contribute to transforming federal HR operations.

Work Location & Travel:

This role is primarily remote with up to 10% travel for agency migration activities.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop SQL and PL/SQL extraction programs to export employee data from PeopleSoft HRMS and Oracle EBS HCM, including demographics, job history, positions, compensation, and benefits.

  • Analyze agency‑specific configurations and customizations to produce detailed data mapping documents aligned to Oracle Fusion HCM HDL formats.

  • Build PeopleSoft Application Designer and Application Engine routines to support repeatable extract processes for mock migrations and production cutover.

  • Design and implement Oracle EBS HCM concurrent programs and extraction packages ensuring complete HR, payroll, and benefits data export.

  • Create SQR reports and validation queries to ensure extraction accuracy, completeness, and EHRI compliance.

  • Conduct data profiling to evaluate data quality, identify gaps, and determine custom handling requirements.

  • Maintain PeopleSoft and EBS legacy environments used for extraction development (schema refreshes, access, performance tuning).

  • Collaborate with agency system administrators to understand customizations, integrations, and data dependencies impacting extraction sequencing.

  • Execute reconciliation processes comparing legacy system data with extraction outputs to ensure zero data loss.

  • Document extraction processes, agency‑specific mappings, and known data issues following SAFe Agile artifact standards.

  • Support agency cutover events by running final extracts, validating outputs, and troubleshooting issues under tight deadlines.

  • Apply established best practices to resolve technical challenges and contribute knowledge to team repositories.

  • Communicate clearly with project stakeholders, participate in Agile ceremonies, and support coordinated delivery across workstreams.

Required:

  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance (U.S. Citizenship required).

  • Bachelor’s degree and 5 years of related experience (additional experience may substitute for degree).

  • 3+ years hands‑on experience with PeopleSoft HRMS (Application Designer, Application Engine, PeopleCode, SQR) and/or Oracle EBS HCM (concurrent programs, PL/SQL packages, HR tables).

  • Strong SQL/PL‑SQL skills with experience writing complex queries against large HR datasets (100K+ records).

  • Solid knowledge of HR data domains (employee demographics, job history, positions, compensation, benefits).

  • Experience in data validation, profiling, and data quality assessment.

  • Familiarity with Agile/SAFe and iterative migration processes.

Desired:

  • Expertise with PeopleTools 8.5x, Component Interface, Integration Broker.

  • Oracle DBA (OCP) certification.

  • Experience with EHRI data standards and federal personnel data reporting.

  • Hands‑on experience with Oracle Fusion HDL and HSDL formats.

  • Knowledge of federal HR data elements (NOA codes, SF‑50 data, position classification).

  • Experience supporting large‑scale migrations (500K+ records) across multiple legacy systems.

  • Familiarity with Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).

This position is contingent on funding and may not be filled immediately. However, this position is representative of positions within CACI that are consistently available. Individuals who apply may also be considered for other positions at CACI.

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

An environment of trust.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

Pay Range:

There are a host of factors that can influence final salary including, but not limited to, geographic location, Federal Government contract labor categories and contract wage rates, relevant prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education, and certifications. Our employees value the flexibility at CACI that allows them to balance quality work and their personal lives. We offer competitive compensation, benefits and learning and development opportunities. At CACI, you will receive comprehensive benefits such as; healthcare, wellness, financial, retirement, family support, continuing education, and time off benefits.

$75,200-$158,100

jobs.title: Director of Product Management -Product Platform
jobs.excerpt: CaptivateIQ is transforming the way companies plan, manage, and optimize the models that run their business.
jobs.description:
CaptivateIQ is transforming the way companies plan, manage, and optimize the models that run their business. We started by revolutionizing incentive compensation management, expanded into sales planning, and are building a unified, AI-native platform for the most critical models an enterprise runs. Recognized by industry analysts like Forrester and G2 and backed by top-tier investors including Sequoia, ICONIQ, Accel, Sapphire Ventures, and Workday Ventures, we power high-growth innovators like Figma, Stripe, and Snowflake alongside global enterprises such as Netflix, Mastercard, and Boston Scientific.

Join a talented, fast-growing team committed to solving some of the most complex and impactful problems in enterprise modeling — at platform scale.

About the Role

CaptivateIQ is looking for a Director of Product Management to lead the strategy and execution of our Product Platform — the shared foundation that every CaptivateIQ application is built on. This is the connective tissue of the company: the layers that turn a set of products into a single, AI-native system.

It is where data becomes connected and queryable, where workflows orchestrate long-running human-and-agent processes, where reporting turns models into decisions, where identity and entitlements govern who can do what, where state is versioned and audited, and where the AI and agent platform gives every product a consistent, agent-accessible surface.

This role owns one of CaptivateIQ’s highest-leverage areas. A single great primitive shipped here compounds across every product. It demands a leader who is hands-on, deeply curious about the systems beneath the surface, and capable of balancing rigorous platform thinking with decisive product execution.

Job Location

Remote - US & Canada

What You'll Own

    The Product Platform spans the shared layers and cross-cutting capabilities that sit between our applications and our infrastructure. Concretely, this scope includes:

  • AI & Agent Platform. The agent SDK, MCP server (the single inbound surface for tool calls across the platform), agent portal for authoring and observability, eval framework and runner, and the shared chat/agent UI primitives every product embeds. This vertical spans the full stack — every layer must be API-first and agent-accessible.

  • Data Platform. Bi-directional data connectors (ingest from HRIS, CRM, and more; egress to warehouse and BI), and the ETL / ingestion and transformation layer that takes raw third-party data through to clean, typed, queryable objects.

  • Workflows & Reporting. Long-running orchestration with human-in-the-loop approvals (payout processing, plan rollout, period close), and in-house reporting and analytics built natively on platform objects and modeling outputs.

  • Identity. Authentication and SSO, policies and permissions (RBAC, scoping enforced at every layer boundary), entitlements that drive feature gating, billing, org settings, and user preferences.

  • State Platform. State as a first-class primitive — the versioning and state-transition machine every change flows through — plus the sandbox (branchable, isolated workspaces for staging changes safely) and audit (a record of every state transition for review and compliance) built on top of it.

    • Your job is everything that makes our customer-facing applications interoperable, governable, and agent-ready.

Responsibilities

  • Own the Product Platform strategy and roadmap. Define how CaptivateIQ’s shared layers — data, workflows, reporting, identity, state, and the AI/agent platform — evolve to make every product faster to build and every model more connected.

  • Make the platform an accelerant, not a tax. A platform team succeeds only when product teams move faster because of it. Build primitives teams reach for by default, and retire the temptation to invent parallel versions.

  • Champion interface-first, agent-ready design. Every platform surface must be designed API-first with well-defined schemas and documentation, with human UX built on top. Agents are only as reliable as the APIs and data structures they operate on — your layers are that substrate.

  • Model hands-on product leadership. Stay close to the details. Immerse yourself in customer workflows, data models, agent behavior, and technical constraints. Reason from system dynamics, not surface requirements.

  • Scale enterprise readiness. Deliver the governance, auditability, access control, sandboxing, performance, and reliability that enterprises operating at scale depend on — and that make AI-generated logic trustworthy and governable.

  • Develop system thinkers. Coach PMs to think holistically across components and personas, reason about trade-offs, and make clear, structured decisions grounded in how the whole platform behaves.

  • Drive measurable impact. Connect platform work to company-level outcomes — development velocity, API-first coverage, cross-model data flows, reduction in fragmentation — and ensure alignment through clarity, not control.

What You’ll Bring

  • 4+ years leading product managers, with a track record of shaping complex, multi-tenant systems.

  • Accountable to achieving business, platform, and organizational outcomes by creating clarity, enabling systems of good decision-making, and multiplying impact

  • Deep experience with platform or infrastructure products — data platforms, APIs and developer platforms, workflow/orchestration engines, identity and access, or similar foundational layers where correctness, scale, and usability intersect.

  • Demonstrated ability to build reusable primitives and abstractions that serve multiple products, teams, and external builders.

  • Strong API-first instincts — you think in interfaces, schemas, and contracts before screens.

  • Fluency with and genuine curiosity about the AI/agent stack: MCP, agent tooling, evals, context management, and how orchestration around a model — not just the model — drives differentiated value.

  • Strong cross-functional instincts — able to bring together Engineering, Design, Sales, and CX around shared context and goals.

  • A coaching mindset; you invest in developing people’s judgment, not just their execution.

  • Clear, structured thinking — you simplify complexity without losing nuance.

  • Passion for creating environments where product teams do their best, most thoughtful work.

How We Think About Leadership

  • As a platform leader, your impact is leverage: the primitives you ship and the standards you set determine how fast every other team can move. You help teams understand the “why” behind what they’re building, connect their local work to the bigger picture, and cultivate a culture where ownership is shared, curiosity is encouraged, and collaboration is the default.

  • You hold a high bar for quality velocity over raw velocity — AI-accelerated development amplifies whatever you build, so architecture, testing, and reliability are force multipliers, not overhead.

Benefits

  • Comprehensive Healthcare: 100% coverage for medical, dental, and vision for all FTEs, with roughly 75% coverage for dependents.
  • Flexible Time Off: Flexible vacation days plus quarterly mental health days to ensure you have the space to recharge.
  • Annual Stipends: Dedicated funds for your professional development and caretaking needs.
  • Work Anniversary Bonuses: Annual bonuses to celebrate your milestones and contributions to the CaptivateIQ team that grow as your tenure does.
  • Retirement Savings (US-Only): A 401(k) plan to help you invest in and secure your future.
  • Premium Tools: The latest Apple hardware to empower you to do your best work.
  • Inclusive Community: Active Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that celebrate shared identities and support our DEI goals by fostering an environment where diverse talent thrives.

Notice to Prospective Candidates

  • Only emails from @captivateiq.com should be trusted.
  • We are aware of active recruitment scams using the CaptivateIQ name, in which individuals pose as our recruiters and post fake remote job openings and make fake job offers on the Internet. Please note, we will never do the following:Attempt to correspond with a candidate using a free web-based account, such as an email address that ends in @gmail.com, @yahoo.com, @hotmail.com, etc.
  • Make an offer of employment without conducting multiple rounds of interviews face-to-face using secure video-conferencing technology.
  • Ask candidates to cash checks to buy equipment on behalf of CaptivateIQ.
  • Ask candidates to make a payment in order to be considered for a position.
  • Make early requests for candidates' personal information such as date of birth, passport details, credit card numbers, bank details and social security number, etc.
  • Please note that we’ll only ask for more sensitive personal information in connection with background checks after an offer is made.
  • Participate in an on-call rotation to provide after-hours support, ensuring timely resolution of critical issues and maintaining system uptime.
CaptivateIQ participates in E-Verify, web-based system that allows enrolled employers to confirm the eligibility of their employees to work in the United States.

ABOUT GENERATION:

At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives. We are a global nonprofit organization that supports adults to achieve economic mobility through employment. Generation trains and places adult learners of all ages into careers that are otherwise inaccessible, working in partnership with governments, employers, and other system actors. Launched in 2015, Generation comprises a global hub (Generation You Employed, or GYE) and a network of in-country affiliates. When learners join Generation, 91% are unemployed, of which nearly half are long-term unemployed. Three months after completing our program, graduates have a 78% job placement rate, rising to 88% within six months. Of our employed graduates, 79% are hired by repeat employers who have previously hired Generation graduates, and 89% are in jobs directly related to the profession for which we have trained them. Employed graduates immediately earn an average of 3-4X their previous earnings. Two to five years after graduation, 77% of our alumni from upper-middle income countries continue to meet their daily financial needs and 63% can save for the future.
