jobs.description:
Description

Nebius Academy is an educational platform that helps business professionals and organizations navigate the era of AI-driven transformation. We create specialized courses that teach practitioners how to apply AI tools strategically in real-world business workflows — across sales, marketing, learning & development, and organizational management.

Our programs are designed for working professionals who need to act on AI, not just understand it. We focus on practical adoption, measurable impact, and the kind of judgment that comes from experience — helping individuals and teams lead change, not react to it.

Our mission is to equip business professionals with the knowledge and frameworks to make smart AI decisions, drive adoption across their organizations, and become leaders in the new era of work.

Who are we looking for?

We are building a talent pool of experienced business professionals, consultants, and transformation leaders for ongoing roles as Instructors, Authors, and Subject Matter Experts across our AI for Business & Transformation program.

Our courses cover: AI for Smart Work, AI for Sales, AI for L&D, AI for Marketing, and AI for Teachers.

We recruit across three experience levels:

Junior Specialists (Instructors / Technical Trainers / Automation Specialists) bring 1–3 years of hands-on experience with AI tools or digital transformation initiatives. They explain AI concepts clearly, without technical jargon, and are comfortable teaching non-technical audiences.

Middle Experts (Authors / Automation Consultants / Automation Engineers) have 3–6 years of experience implementing AI in real organizations. They work with business examples and case studies, and can explain the reasoning behind technology choices — including build vs. buy decisions and AI governance basics.

Senior SMEs (AI Consultants / Automation Architects / Technology Strategists) bring 6+ years of experience working with business leaders and C-level stakeholders. They speak to ROI, digital transformation strategy, AI governance, and organizational change management.

What sets our experts apart is the ability to translate real-world AI experience into learning that sticks — for audiences who are already senior, already busy, and already skeptical of hype.

These are Talent Pool positions — we continuously review applications and build our roster of experts. There may not be an immediate opening at the time you apply, but strong candidates will be added to our talent pool and contacted as relevant opportunities arise.

You can join us on a part-time basis (10–15 hours per week) as an instructor leading live sessions, a course author creating learning materials, or a subject matter expert supporting curriculum development.

Apply now — we review applications on an ongoing basis. Our selection process is fully asynchronous and designed to respect your time:

  1. Application Review — we evaluate your profile against our current needs
  2. Async Video Interview — a short self-recorded interview (10–15 minutes max)
  3. Test Assignment — approximately 1 hour to complete
  4. Talent Pool — finalists are added to our active roster of vetted experts
  5. Hiring Manager Call — once a relevant position opens, we invite you to a live interview with our team
  6. Offer — we extend an offer for a relevant position upon successful completion of the process

Please submit your resume in English.

What you will do

Available Roles

We are building a talent pool of Instructors, Authors, and Subject Matter Experts for our AI for Business & Transformation programs. We hire on an ongoing basis across the following specializations:

Most in demand: AI for Smart Work, AI for Sales, AI for Marketing, AI for L&D, AI for Teachers

Also relevant: other business functions and organizational transformation domains

Depending on your expertise, you may:

  • Deliver live workshops and training sessions
  • Create educational content, assessments, and project-based learning materials
  • Design practical exercises, guides, prompts, and reference resources
  • Help define curriculum structure, learning objectives, and competency frameworks
  • Review content for technical accuracy and industry relevance
  • Share insights on AI tools, workflows, and emerging trends
  • Collaborate with instructional designers and curriculum teams to continuously improve learning outcomes
  • Support program updates based on learner feedback and market needs

Areas of involvement

  • Instructor — leads live sessions, workshops, and learner interactions.
  • Author — creates course content, lessons, assessments, and projects.
  • Subject Matter Expert — shapes curriculum strategy, competency frameworks, and program direction.

⌛ All roles are part-time: 10–15 hours per week.

Requirements

  • 1+ years of experience implementing AI tools or contributing to digital transformation initiatives in business environments
  • Hands-on experience with AI tools relevant to business workflows, such as ChatGPT, Copilot for M365, Make, Zapier, Notion AI, or similar
  • Practical understanding of AI use cases across business functions such as sales, marketing, L&D, operations, or related areas
  • Ability to explain AI concepts clearly, using practical business examples and actionable use cases for non-technical audiences
  • Strong ability to share knowledge through consulting, training, content creation, coaching, mentoring, or facilitation
  • Ability to work independently with strong ownership and minimal supervision
  • Availability to collaborate within European time zones
  • Ability to dedicate approximately 10–15 hours per week
  • Fluent English (written and spoken); Russian or Spanish is a strong plus
  • Background in business consulting, corporate training, professional coaching, digital transformation, or knowledge-sharing is a plus

Nice-to-have

  • 6+ years of experience working with business leaders, senior managers, or C-level stakeholders on AI adoption, digital transformation, or organizational change initiatives
  • Ability to evaluate real-world AI applications in business contexts and distinguish practical, high-ROI approaches from hype
  • Experience creating competency maps, maturity frameworks, skill decompositions, or curriculum structures
  • Familiarity with AI governance, build-vs-buy decisions, and change management principles
  • Ability to review learning content and provide structured feedback

What we can offer you

  • The opportunity to teach while maintaining your primary job: Share your expertise without leaving your current role.
  • Competitive hourly rate of $40-$150 USD for flexible part-time collaboration with significant impact and an amazing team!
  • Remote cooperation with a schedule convenient for both you and the team: We don't focus on micromanagement.
  • Cross-cultural experience: Become part of an international team and connect with professional developers from diverse backgrounds.
  • Meaningful impact: Share your knowledge and help experienced engineers advance their skills in AI-assisted development.
  • Participation in innovative projects: Contribute to shaping the future of programming education and AI adoption.
  • Professional growth: Receive feedback and develop your skills as a technical educator and thought leader.

jobs.description:
Highlights:

Location: Spain

Language: Fluent in Russian and English (C1+)

About Fundraise Up

We’re Fundraise Up - a global fundraising platform built to make donating to nonprofits fast, seamless, and accessible to all. Every month, our technology powers tens of millions of dollars in donations across the globe. We focus on innovation that directly impacts results: faster load times, higher conversion rates, global payment support, and accessibility-first design.

Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading nonprofits, including UNICEF, the Alzheimer’s Association, and a wide range of global NGOs. With a 4.9/5 rating across top software review platforms, we’re recognized not just for our impact - but for the quality of the product we deliver.

A Truly Global Product

We operate in the enterprise segment, serving nonprofit organizations across North America, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Europe.

We’re building a large and complex product ecosystem that serves nonprofits, donors, and partners around the world. The platform includes a modern checkout experience and customizable widgets (each a standalone SPA), donor, organization, and partner portals, admin tools, and several internal apps.

The Team

We are a distributed team of 160+ product professionals. Our team members are mainly based across Spain, Poland, Portugal, Georgia, Armenia, Serbia, Turkey, and Cyprus.

Despite our scale, we operate like a focused team - where every task matters and every voice is heard. We value thoughtful collaboration, strong engineering practices, and a product mindset. You’ll be joining a team where quality, mentorship, and mutual respect come first.

About In-Person Giving at Fundraise Up

In-Person Giving brings the quality and connected data of Fundraise Up’s online donation experience into physical fundraising moments.

The product begins with Tap to Donate and Giving Station: staff-led and self-service experiences that let nonprofits accept contactless donations at events, in public spaces, and through other offline workflows. Every transaction should connect to the same campaigns, donor records, reporting, CRM integrations, and operational controls used across Fundraise Up.

The next product direction is Events & Commerce. It includes ticket sales, check-in, merchandise and food purchases, symbolic purchases, auctions, paddle raises, and additional donations before and during an event. These capabilities must work as one connected fundraising system rather than another isolated event tool.

About the Role

We are hiring a Product Manager to own Events & Commerce within the broader In-Person Giving product line.

This is a hands-on software product role covering discovery, definition, delivery, launch, and iteration. You will turn a large category into a focused product direction grounded in customer workflows, live usage, and commercial evidence.

You will work closely with the PM responsible for the broader In-Person Giving area so that event commerce builds on the same payment, campaign, donor-data, reporting, mobile, and operational foundations as Tap to Donate and Giving Station. You will also partner with the Peer-to-Peer team where ticketing and event capabilities should be shared rather than rebuilt separately.

This is not an event-planning, sales, or internal project-coordination role.

What You’ll Own

Define the product direction

  • Turn customer research, market evidence, and business context into a clear Events & Commerce product thesis and sequenced roadmap.
  • Choose a focused target segment and event scenario rather than trying to replace every event platform at once.
  • Decide which capabilities belong in the shared In-Person Giving foundation and which require an Events-specific model.
  • Make explicit decisions about what Fundraise Up should build, integrate, partner on, or deliberately exclude.
  • Keep assumptions, success metrics, scope, risks, and product decisions visible.

Lead discovery and product definition

  • Work directly with nonprofit fundraising teams, event operators, finance teams, volunteers, attendees, donors, design partners, and internal GTM teams.
  • Map the complete workflow before, during, and after an event—including purchase, donation, check-in, fulfillment, reconciliation, reporting, and follow-up.
  • Validate decisions through interviews, workflow observation, prototypes, and live product usage.
  • Separate true adoption blockers from feature requests and expectations created by incumbent event platforms.
  • Shape problems such as ticket sales, QR-based check-in, guest management, commerce catalogues, FMV and receipts, on-site purchases, auctions, paddle raises, refunds, attribution, reporting, and integrations. These are examples—not a pre-committed feature checklist.

Shape and deliver the product

  • Own the product from problem definition through requirements, delivery, launch, and iteration.
  • Write clear requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases, state transitions, and decision records.
  • Make day-to-day scope and trade-off decisions with Engineering, Design, Analytics, Research, QA, and GTM partners.
  • Design for real event conditions: staff and volunteer operators, self-service flows, mobile devices, optional hardware, unreliable connectivity, high-volume moments, and operational recovery.
  • Ensure that event capabilities reuse Fundraise Up’s existing payments, campaign, donor, reporting, CRM, and identity infrastructure wherever possible.
  • Keep delivery predictable by surfacing dependencies, risks, and unresolved decisions early.

Launch, learn, and drive outcomes

  • Launch through EAPs with clear entry criteria, target workflows, success measures, readiness requirements, and out-of-scope areas.
  • Understand whether organizations can configure and run the target event workflows without heavy manual work or disconnected tools.
  • Measure whether attendees can purchase, check in, donate, and receive the right confirmation or receipt through a clear experience.
  • Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, CSM, Support, Finance, Legal, and Operations on positioning, commitments, enablement, and launch readiness.
  • Connect product evidence to activation, adoption, event completion, GPV, expansion, pipeline, retention, and operational cost.
  • Turn evidence into explicit recommendations: iterate, expand, change direction, partner, or stop.

Work AI-native

  • Use AI for research synthesis, workflow analysis, prototyping, specification quality, data exploration, and operational automation.
  • Build testable artifacts quickly without outsourcing product judgment.

Requirements

  • 4–7 years of Product Management or Product Ownership experience in a software product company.
  • End-to-end ownership of a customer-facing product area with Engineering and Design.
  • Strong judgment in reducing a large problem space to a focused release and explaining the trade-offs.
  • Experience turning customer evidence and product data into decisions.
  • Clear written communication across requirements, edge cases, metrics, and decision records.
  • Ability to work with transactional, multi-actor workflows involving permissions, states, money, and data relationships.
  • High ownership and independence, with fluent written and spoken English.

Strong plus

  • Experience with ticketing, event technology, commerce, POS, payments, marketplaces, registration, auctions, or other transaction-heavy products.
  • Experience with mobile applications, contactless payments, physical devices, or hardware-enabled workflows.
  • Experience with B2B SaaS, fundraising, nonprofits, or other operationally complex customer environments.
  • Experience launching a new product area through beta or EAP.
  • Knowledge of CRM integrations, financial reconciliation, reporting, transaction attribution, analytics, or SQL.
  • Practical use of AI for research, prototyping, analysis, or product operations.

This Role May Not Be a Fit If

  • You are looking for an event-planning or internal project-management role rather than software product ownership.
  • You prefer to receive a fully defined roadmap and requirements instead of helping determine what should be built.
  • You want to work only on strategy and avoid specifications, QA, delivery details, or post-launch iteration.
  • You treat every customer request as a roadmap commitment.
  • You need stable scope and certainty before moving forward.
  • You measure progress mainly by features shipped rather than customer and business outcomes.

Why work with us

  • Build a new product direction from research through live customer use.
  • Work in a large, proven fundraising category with clear customer demand and meaningful commercial potential.
  • Shape ticketing and event commerce as part of a broader fundraising platform rather than an isolated event tool.
  • Work with real nonprofit customers, rich product evidence, and experienced cross-functional partners.
  • Join a small team where product managers have meaningful ownership and direct access to Product leadership.
  • Help define an AI-native approach to product management in practice.
  • Build technology that helps nonprofits engage more supporters and raise more money for their missions.

Compensation

  • The compensation range for this role is €5,600 - €6,100 gross.
  • Final compensation will be determined based on relevant experience, skills, qualifications, alignment with the role’s requirements and location.

Benefits

  • Private medical insurance for the employee and their family
  • 23 paid vacation days per year
  • 11 paid public holidays per year
  • 5 company-paid sick leave days
  • English learning courses
  • Relevant professional education
  • Gym or swimming pool
  • Home Office Setup Assistance: the company offers assistance with purchasing furniture (office chair, office desk, monitor) and other items to create a comfortable workspace
  • Co-working
  • Remote working

**Please note: All official correspondence from Fundraise Up will exclusively originate from the @fundraiseup.com domain. Exercise caution and ensure the authenticity of emails claiming to be from our company.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law in the countries where we operate.

The Opportunity:

Join a mission‑driven team supporting the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC)—the agency that protects America’s bank depositors and helps maintain stability in the nation’s financial system. In this role, you will provide mid‑ to senior‑level acquisition policy expertise that directly supports the FDIC’s Acquisition Services Branch in shaping, strengthening, and modernizing acquisition policies, procedures, and lifecycle processes. If you thrive in fast‑moving environments, enjoy complex policy work, and excel in collaboration across legal, contracting, and technical teams, this opportunity offers both challenge and impact.

Note: This role is remote but requires the selected candidate to reside within the Washington, D.C. Metro Area.


Responsibilities:

As a Policy Analyst you will:
  • Provide mid‑ to senior‑level acquisition policy support with expertise in interpreting and drafting acquisition policy, understanding that the FDIC is not a FAR‑based agency.
  • Provide strategic support for developing, implementing, and maintaining FDIC contract policies and procedures.
  • Collaborate across FDIC teams to ensure alignment with legal and regulatory requirements and promote compliance and efficiency in contract management.
  • Obtain, research, analyze, and present detailed and complex contracting information; track, organize, and communicate procurement data clearly and logically.
  • Develop presentations and data‑enriched reports, offering findings and actionable recommendations.
  • Work effectively and collaboratively with contract specialists, contracting officers, legal personnel, and other teams in a demanding, fast‑evolving environment.
  • Conduct research on Executive Orders, OMB memoranda, and related policy drivers to identify impacts on FDIC acquisition operations and policy.
  • Assist with drafting and reviewing updates to FDIC’s APGM, including integrating interim policy changes and stakeholder inputs.
  • Draft and review acquisition templates, samples, and other documents used across the FDIC user community.
  • Coordinate updates and interactions with acquisition systems such as APS and ASNG.



Qualifications:

Required:

Note: This role is remote but requires the selected candidate to reside within the Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

  • BA or BS degree in a business‑related, management, or legal field
  • At least ten (10) years of direct procurement experience in federal government and/or the private sector
  • At least five (5) of the most recent years must include practical experience creating policy documents, updating existing policies, and developing templates
  • Clearance: Public Trust
  • Proven practical knowledge and excellence applying both non‑FAR‑based regulations and the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), along with other U.S. Government policies
  • Experience working with GSA Schedules, GWACs, and MA‑IDIQs
  • Demonstrated understanding and practical experience with acquisition management principles across the full lifecycle (pre‑award through closeout)
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple contract types for supplies and services (FFP/LOE, T&M, FFP, CPFF, CPIF, CPAF)
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills; ability to work effectively in a team environment
  • Ability to anticipate issues, establish paths to mitigate risk, and manage administrative processes on behalf of management
  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in demanding environments and establish productive relationships at all levels—internal and external
  • Proven ability to set a positive example, resolve misunderstandings proactively, expand working relationships, and influence productive outcomes



Desired:
  • Master’s Degree in a business‑related, management, or legal field
  • Minimum of ten (10) years of direct procurement experience in federal government and/or private sector contract management with focus on policy development and implementation
  • Certification: Certified Procurement Professional (CPP) or similar certification in government procurement practices (e.g., FAC Professional or FAC‑C II or equivalent)
-

What You Can Expect:

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

An environment of trust.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

Pay Range:

There are a host of factors that can influence final salary including, but not limited to, geographic location, Federal Government contract labor categories and contract wage rates, relevant prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education, and certifications. Our employees value the flexibility at CACI that allows them to balance quality work and their personal lives. We offer competitive compensation, benefits and learning and development opportunities. At CACI, you will receive comprehensive benefits such as; healthcare, wellness, financial, retirement, family support, continuing education, and time off benefits.

$95,500-$210,100

jobs.description:
Licensed Insurance Customer Service Representative (P&C) – Remote | U.S. Hours

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours
Location: Outside the United States

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Licensed Insurance Customer Service Representative (P&C) to support a U.S.-based insurance agency with policy servicing, quoting, renewals, and day-to-day customer support.

This is a client-facing insurance role where you’ll communicate directly with policyholders, prospects, carriers, and agency teams. You’ll help customers understand their coverage, process policy requests accurately, prepare quotes, and ensure every interaction is handled professionally and efficiently.

An active U.S. Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance license is required, either resident or non-resident. If additional state licenses are needed for the role, the client will assist with obtaining them.

What You’ll Own

Policy Servicing

  • Handle policy changes, endorsements, renewals, cancellations, and other servicing requests.
  • Respond to policyholder questions accurately and professionally.
  • Review policy information and assist clients with coverage-related questions.
  • Maintain detailed records of customer interactions and policy activities.
  • Ensure servicing requests are completed accurately and within expected timelines.
  • Follow agency procedures and applicable insurance regulations.

Insurance Quoting & Renewals

  • Prepare insurance quotes for new and existing customers.
  • Gather information required to generate accurate quotes.
  • Explain available coverage options and policy details clearly.
  • Follow up with prospects regarding outstanding quotes.
  • Support existing customers throughout the renewal process.
  • Help identify and resolve issues that could delay quotes or renewals.

Customer Service

  • Handle inbound and outbound calls with policyholders and prospects.
  • Respond to customer emails and servicing requests promptly.
  • Build strong relationships through responsive, professional communication.
  • Help resolve customer concerns while maintaining a positive experience.
  • Ensure clients receive clear updates regarding outstanding requests.

Carrier & Agency Coordination

  • Communicate with insurance carriers regarding:
    • Underwriting requirements
    • Policy changes
    • Coverage questions
    • Documentation
    • Renewals
  • Coordinate with producers and other agency team members.
  • Process and organize policy documentation.
  • Maintain accurate records within the agency management system.
  • Follow up with carriers and internal stakeholders until requests are fully resolved.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You hold an active U.S. Property & Casualty insurance license.
  • You have hands-on experience working with P&C insurance policies.
  • You genuinely enjoy helping customers and solving servicing issues.
  • You communicate confidently and professionally by phone and email.
  • You understand the importance of accuracy and compliance in insurance.
  • You can manage multiple customer requests without losing track of details.
  • You’re comfortable working independently in a remote environment.
  • You take ownership of requests from initial contact through resolution.

Required Experience & Skills

Must-Have

  • Active U.S. Property & Casualty (P&C) Insurance License, resident or non-resident.
  • Minimum 1 year of Property & Casualty insurance experience with an insurance agency or carrier.
  • Experience with Personal Lines, Commercial Lines, or both.
  • Experience handling policy servicing, customer inquiries, and insurance documentation.
  • Comfortable handling inbound and outbound calls with policyholders, prospects, and carriers.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Ability to work during U.S. business hours.
  • Reliable high-speed internet and a dedicated home-office setup.
  • Must be located outside the United States.

Nice to Have

  • Experience supporting both Personal and Commercial Lines.
  • Familiarity with major U.S. insurance carriers.
  • Previous experience working remotely for a U.S.-based insurance agency.
  • Experience supporting multiple insurance producers or agency teams.
  • Familiarity with agency management systems such as:
    • Applied Epic
    • AMS360
    • HawkSoft
    • EZLynx
    • QQCatalyst
    • Vertafore
    • Similar insurance platforms

What a Typical Day Looks Like

You’ll start by reviewing new customer inquiries, policy requests, endorsements, renewals, and outstanding follow-ups.

Throughout the day, you may:

  • Respond to policyholder calls and emails.
  • Process endorsements and policy changes.
  • Prepare insurance quotes.
  • Explain coverage and policy information to customers.
  • Follow up on quotes and upcoming renewals.
  • Contact carriers regarding underwriting or servicing requests.
  • Update customer and policy records in the agency management system.
  • Coordinate with producers and other agency team members.
  • Follow outstanding requests through to completion.

In short: you help keep the agency’s customer service and policy operations accurate, responsive, and organized while delivering a strong experience to every client.

What Success Looks Like

  • Fast and accurate handling of policy servicing requests.
  • High-quality customer communication and responsiveness.
  • Accurate quotes, documentation, and agency records.
  • Timely completion of endorsements and renewals.
  • Strong follow-through on customer and carrier requests.
  • Consistent compliance with agency procedures.
  • Positive customer and agency-team feedback.
  • Minimal errors or unresolved servicing requests.

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Work directly within the U.S. insurance industry.
  • Put your existing P&C license and insurance experience to use remotely.
  • Gain exposure to U.S. carriers, producers, and agency operations.
  • Build deeper experience across Personal and/or Commercial Lines.
  • Fully remote opportunity for professionals located outside the United States.
  • Long-term growth opportunities within insurance servicing, account management, and agency operations.

Interview Process

  • Initial Recruiter Screening
  • Client Interview
  • Offer Stage

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. It’s a short, self-recorded video completed on your own time and is the final step that completes your application.

Instead of repeating yourself across multiple screening calls, you get to introduce yourself once and let your story carry forward. Hiring managers can see how you communicate before meeting you, making future interviews more focused and meaningful.

You can record your video as many times as you like before submitting it — only your final submission will be reviewed.

Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation.

Apply Now

If you’re a licensed P&C insurance professional who enjoys customer service, policy servicing, quoting, and helping clients understand their coverage, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply today and bring your U.S. insurance experience to a fully remote client-facing role.

We partner with hospitals, healthcare practices, and individuals to provide personalized, root-cause nutrition care across a wide range of conditions, including metabolic health, digestive disorders, hormonal imbalances, and chronic disease.

Our approach is grounded in prevention, root-cause resolution, and sustainable lifestyle change, supporting patients throughout their health journey. Through a fully virtual, telehealth model, we meet patients where they are, delivering accessible, high-quality care.

  • Credentialing: If you’re not yet in-network, our team fully manages the insurance credentialing process on your behalf, including covering all associated fees and handling the paperwork.

Benefits

  • Flexible Scheduling: Set your availability with the ability to build and adjust your schedule based on your preferences and patient demand
  • Supplement Commissions: Earn 12.5% of MSRP on supplements purchased through Fullscript. Commissions are paid quarterly and can meaningfully increase your overall earnings based on patient engagement.
  • Performance-Based Bonus Opportunities: Earn additional income based on patient retention and face-to-face care time.
  • Paid Time Off (PTO): Accrue 1 hour of PTO for every 12 hours of patient care, supporting flexibility and time away as you work.
  • Discretionary Holiday Break: Office closed between Christmas and New Year’s — guaranteed time off from patient appointments & administrative work
  • Fitness Allowance: Partial reimbursement for gym memberships, fitness classes, or wellness activities
  • Simplex Wellness on Demand: Free access to virtual fitness programs

Time Zone and Schedule:

Our operations and patient base are primarily in Eastern Standard Time (EST). Candidates in Pacific or Mountain time zones have the unique advantage of working standard daytime hours in their local time zone while providing essential evening coverage for our East Coast patients. Please note that administrative support is available from 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM EST, and while live attendance at team meetings is encouraged, recordings will be provided for those unable to join due to time zone differences.

Key Intangible Characteristics of the Ideal Candidate:

Called: A passion for our mission and a sense that this role and company are a strong fit for the blessings of your gifts, talents, passions, and experiences.. Must be mission-motivated with a resolve to overcome obstacles, anchored in a sense of purpose in this work.

Servant Leadership: Nobody is above any task, and we are all here to serve others. Every customer—internal or external—needs help, and the most powerful way to lead will be to serve.

Learning and Adaptive: As a startup with a big mission, new systems, technology, and situational adaptability are expected. This person must have an appetite for learning and skill improvement.

Grit, Resourcefulness & Entrepreneurial Spirit: Not everything will have a pre-planned solution. This person will have to be resourceful in figuring things out, resist feeling overwhelmed, and be willing to roll up their sleeves to make things happen. This person will have to have an open mind and good resolve, whether it’s looping in other people, finding answers online, or seeking best practices.

Organizational Skills: Being or becoming a constant organizational force. It will require a capacity for being open to change, discerning better processes, and prioritizing for improved outcomes.

Chemistry Fit: We have a unique and fun culture—we laugh, press in, work hard, and jump in to figure things out. Fitting into the team chemistry is essential.

High Character: We operate with a high trust culture. Personal values must fuel our work. Integrity, honesty, compassion, reconciliation, and diligence are all things this person must possess to flourish.

Energy & Enthusiasm: This person must bring joy and passion for work to the job. Encouraging and spurring on others on the mission while being self-motivated and positive is essential.

Multitasking: This is not a steady-state or static environment. Workflow will cycle, and interruptions are normal, so this person must be able to juggle and adjust on the fly.

Project Management: While multitasking, this person must be able to keep an eye on deadlines and critical dependencies, working to preserve them or source support proactively.

🌟 Why Dietitians Choose Simplex Health

Because great clinicians deserve great support.

🧾 We Handle Credentialing & Licensing
We cover insurance credentialing costs and reimburse for out-of-state license fees.

🎓 CEU Reimbursement
We invest in your professional growth and continued learning.

💻 Technology Reimbursement
Support for the tools you need to work efficiently and effectively.

💲 Recruitment Thank You Bonus
Bonus for any referrals hired by Simplex Health who stay at least 90 days

📋 Consistent Referrals & Quality Resources
A steady patient flow and high-quality patient-facing materials to support your care.

👥 Helpful Support Team & Quick Response Times
From scheduling to tech help, our support staff makes your day run smoother.

🌿 Approachable Leadership & Collaborative Culture
Leaders who listen, and a clinical community that truly supports one another.

🤝 Opportunities Beyond Patient Care
Get involved with social media, engagement projects, or hosting lunch & learns.

🌎 Broad Range of Clients, Deep Skill Development
Grow your counseling skills and confidence across a variety of cases.

💞 Strong Sense of Community
Even in a virtual environment, you’ll feel connected, encouraged, and supported.

If you’ve ever wished you could combine the freedom of private practice with the camaraderie and stability of a larger organization, this is where you belong.

Apply today and rediscover the joy of patient care without the grind of running a business.

Simplex Health Core Values:

Simplex Health strives to embody the following values and to apply them to every aspect of how we run our business, including how we interact with each other as teammates and leaders. These values also apply to how we interact with and continue to inspire our clients and strategic partners:

We Inspire Each Other
You are an important part of our team and together we make a collective intention to uplift and commit to one another. Through cultivating genuine, transparent, relationships, we create an environment that encourages individuals to dream big, take risks, and be bold. We aim to inspire and commit to everyone we touch. This sense of commitment and care sets the stage for a culture of accountability, where we hold ourselves and each other to the same high standards, taking the ownership necessary for achieving our goals.
Therefore encourage one another and build each other up, just as in fact you are doing.
1 Thessalonians 5:11

We Always Learn and Grow
We at Simplex Health strive to be continual learners and to expand our abilities as people and as an organization. We educate ourselves, remain curious, and use evidence-based research to challenge our current understanding. We see mistakes and failure as great teachers and learning opportunities. When we stay engaged in the world with a growth mindset, it creates the right environment for us to thrive and make a meaningful impact on each other and on the world.
Let the wise hear and increase in learning, and the one who understands obtain guidance.
Proverbs 1:5

We Think Big Picture What we do day in, day out, how we do it, and the decisions we make- shape who we are as a people and as a company. The details are super important, AND should always be guided by our wide perspective and an understanding of how we are impacting each other, our clients, and our business. Before making any major decision, ask yourself:

• Does it help us grow? How?

• Does it answer “how are we different and why should you care?”
• Is what I’m working on duplicatable and transferable (ie can I duplicate it and apply to other situations)? How?
• Does it challenge the status quo?
• Does it inspire?
• Does it tightly align with and advance our mission? How?
• Can it be more humanized and relatable?
• Does it unite us? How?
• Does it solve a problem? How?
Now we see things imperfectly, like puzzling reflections in a mirror, but then we will see everything with perfect clarity. All that I know now is partial and incomplete, but then I will know everything completely, just as God now knows me completely.
I Corinthians 13:12

We Challenge the Status Quo:
We are inquisitive by nature. We are courageous! We are not afraid to go against the grain in our search for truth. We always question conventional wisdom- it’s how Simplex Health started- it’s what we do.
Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will. Romans 12:2

We Cultivate Health and Vitality:
Being alive in a body is an incredible, temporary experience. Even though at times we feel pain and face challenges, our next breath is not guaranteed and is a HUGE gift. We experience EVERYTHING through our bodies, including thoughts, emotions, spirit, and our inspiration. We see health and vitality as the foundation for living a life that is happy, fulfilled, present, and productive.
Dear friend, I pray that you may enjoy good health and that all may go well with you, even as your soul is getting along well.
3 John 1:2

We Embody Integrity:
We communicate with transparency and face conflict head-on. We do this with the understanding that we respect each other and recognize that we are on the same team working toward a unified noble mission with shared goals. We don’t compromise our morals or integrity no matter the context. When challenging scenarios arise, we approach them with honesty and trust that we are all holding the highest intentions, are committed to our values, and are making best efforts.
Do to others as you would have them do to you.
Luke 6:31

We Simplify the Complicated:
We believe that complex problems don’t always require complex solutions. By simplifying the complicated and offering digestible, scalable solutions, we can pay more attention to the things that matter most. Simplicity- it’s the word that inspired our name - we make cultivating health and vitality simple.
Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.
Philippians 4:6

jobs.excerpt: About Flinks Flinks is the embedded finance platform that brings together connectivity, intelligence, and payments — giving businesses the infrastructure they need to build and deliver seamless financial experiences at scale.
jobs.description:
About Flinks

Flinks is the embedded finance platform that brings together connectivity, intelligence, and payments — giving businesses the infrastructure they need to build and deliver seamless financial experiences at scale.

As a leader in Open Finance in Canada, we’ve grown since 2016 into one of North America’s most trusted platforms for financial data access, enrichment, and money movement. We work with innovators across many industries, including lending, fintech, banking, insurance, and wealth management.

Today, our platform connects to 15,000+ financial institutions across North America and powers over 1M monthly connections. We also give our customers unprecedented visibility into 4,500+ real-time financial insights to support smarter decisioning. Companies rely on Flinks to streamline onboarding, verify income, assess credit risk, and power faster payment experiences.

We’re on a mission to drive financial innovation and help businesses build financial experiences that feel effortless, connected, and customer-first. That’s where you come in.

The Role

We're hiring our Senior Data Engineer (Data / ML Platform) to stand up data engineering as a discipline at Flinks. You'll own the data and ML platform that turns models into reliable production services, harden the data models the business runs on and close the seam between our data scientists and the product teams. This is a high-ownership, greenfield-leaning role: much of this foundation is yours to build and own, not inherit.

If you like being the person who makes data and ML production-grade - pipelines, serving, governance, reliability - and you want broad impact across a company's data, this is built for you.

What You'll Do

  • Own and evolve the data platform - the BigQuery warehouse, dbt transformation layers, Airflow / Cloud Composer orchestration and Pub/Sub ingestion that feed every model and metric.
  • Build and operate the ML platform - training pipelines (Kubeflow on Vertex AI), model serving (FastAPI behind Vertex endpoints), CI/CD, containerization and typed contracts. Take operational ownership of model-serving infrastructure so reliability isn't carried by the data scientists alone.
  • Harden and standardize the data models the business depends on - improving schemas, fixing data-quality issues and establishing trustworthy source-of-truth feeds.
  • Establish data governance and observability - bring data that lives outside the warehouse under proper governance and build operational metrics for products that don't yet have them.
  • Standardize how data engineering is done across product lines - patterns, tooling and pipelines other teams can adopt.
  • Partner across data science, backend and product on the producer to consumer contract (models produced by data science, consumed/aggregated downstream, surfaced to clients).

What You'll Work On

You'll help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' financial intelligence products, supporting everything from transaction enrichment and categorization to risk and payments decisioning.

Key areas of focus include:

  • Building scalable data pipelines that process and transform large volumes of financial data.
  • Designing and maintaining reliable datasets, data models, and feature pipelines used by machine learning and product teams.
  • Improving data quality, observability, and operational metrics across our platform and customer-facing products.
  • Developing cost-efficient, high-performance data services and infrastructure that support real-time and batch workloads.
  • Partnering closely with Data Science, Product, and Engineering teams to enable new capabilities and accelerate product delivery.
  • Contributing to the evolution of our data platform architecture as we continue to scale our products, customers, and machine learning capabilities.

Our stack

  • Python, SQL, Bash
  • Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • BigQuery and dbt
  • Airflow (Cloud Composer), Pub/Sub, and Cloud Functions
  • Kubeflow, Vertex AI, MLflow, and FastAPI
  • Docker, Terraform, and Protocol Buffers
  • Azure DevOps
  • Grafana and GCP Logging

You don't need experience with every tool listed above - strong Data Engineering fundamentals and experience building production data platforms matter more than direct experience with our exact stack. SQL is the exception: it's a non-negotiable (see Key Requirements).

Why This Role

  • Greenfield ownership — help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' next generation of data and machine learning products.
  • High leverage impact — your work enables Data Science, Product, Engineering, and Risk teams to move faster with reliable, trusted data.
  • Real-world scale and complexity — work with large volumes of financial data powering products used by banks, fintechs, and financial institutions across North America.
  • Modern cloud-native environment — build on a modern GCP stack using contemporary data, platform, and machine learning tooling.

Key Requirements

  • Experience: 5+ years of hands-on Data Engineering experience designing, building, and operating production data platforms, pipelines, and warehouse solutions in a cloud environment.
  • Data Engineering Expertise: Strong experience with ETL/ELT development, data modeling, schema design, orchestration, data quality, lineage, and warehouse optimization. Experience with BigQuery, dbt, Airflow, or equivalent modern data tooling is highly desirable.
  • Technical Foundation: Expert SQL and strong Python skills, with the ability to build scalable, maintainable, and well-tested data solutions that support both operational and analytical workloads.
  • Cloud Data Platforms: Experience working with modern cloud-native data ecosystems, including data warehouses, event-driven architectures, distributed processing, and platform observability.
  • Operational Excellence: Demonstrated ownership of production systems, including monitoring, reliability, performance tuning, cost optimization, incident response, and ongoing platform improvements.
  • Machine Learning Platform Exposure: Experience supporting machine learning workflows, feature pipelines, model-serving infrastructure, or MLOps environments is an asset, but a strong Data Engineering foundation is the primary requirement.
  • Collaboration: Ability to partner effectively with Data Science, Product, Engineering, and QA teams to deliver trusted, scalable, and well-governed data solutions.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Work Authorization: Must be legally authorized to work in Canada.

Compensation Range

For experienced and qualified hires located in Canada, of senior (IC4) level, the compensation range is between $120,000 to $160,000 CAD annually.

As part of the total rewards package, Flinks offers:

  • Health & Dental coverage as of Day 1
  • Flexible Paid Time Off (FTO)
  • Remote work environment with frequent in-person gatherings and activities.
  • Career development, learning opportunities and growth
  • And more

We are committed to providing accommodations for persons with disabilities. If you require accommodation, we will work with you to meet your needs.

Flinks uses artificial intelligence (AI) during the recruitment process to assist in screening, assessing, or selecting applicants.

À propos de Flinks 🚀

Flinks est une plateforme de finance intégrée qui réunit la connectivité, l’intelligence financière et les paiements, offrant aux entreprises l’infrastructure nécessaire pour concevoir et déployer des expériences financières fluides à grande échelle.

Chef de file de la finance ouverte (Open Finance) au Canada, nous avons connu une croissance soutenue depuis 2016 pour devenir l’une des plateformes les plus fiables en Amérique du Nord en matière d’accès aux données financières, d’enrichissement des données et de mouvement de fonds. Nous collaborons avec des entreprises innovantes dans de nombreux secteurs, notamment le crédit, les technologies financières (fintech), les services bancaires, l’assurance et la gestion de patrimoine.

Aujourd’hui, notre plateforme est connectée à plus de 15 000 institutions financières à travers l’Amérique du Nord et soutient plus d’un million de connexions mensuelles. Nous offrons également à nos clients un accès à plus de 4 500 indicateurs financiers en temps réel afin de favoriser une prise de décision plus éclairée. Les entreprises s’appuient sur Flinks pour simplifier l’intégration de leurs utilisateurs, vérifier les revenus, évaluer le risque de crédit et offrir des expériences de paiement plus rapides.

Notre mission est d’accélérer l’innovation financière et d’aider les entreprises à créer des expériences financières simples, connectées et centrées sur leurs clients. C’est là que vous entrez en jeu.

Le poste

Nous recrutons notre Ingénieur(e) principal(e) en données (Plateforme Données / IA) afin d’établir l’ingénierie des données comme une discipline à part entière chez Flinks. Vous serez responsable de la plateforme de données et d’apprentissage automatique qui transforme les modèles en services de production fiables, renforcerez les modèles de données sur lesquels l’entreprise s’appuie et assurerez la connexion entre nos scientifiques des données et les équipes produit.

Il s’agit d’un rôle à forte autonomie, orienté vers la création de nouvelles fondations : une grande partie de cette infrastructure sera à concevoir, bâtir et faire évoluer par vous, plutôt qu’à hériter d’un environnement existant.

Si vous aimez être la personne qui rend les données et l’IA prêtes pour la production — pipelines, mise en service des modèles, gouvernance, fiabilité — et que vous souhaitez avoir un impact important sur l’ensemble des capacités de données d’une entreprise, ce rôle est fait pour vous.

Ce que vous ferez

  • Assurer la propriété et l’évolution de la plateforme de données — l’entrepôt BigQuery, les couches de transformation dbt, l’orchestration Airflow / Cloud Composer et les mécanismes d’ingestion Pub/Sub qui alimentent chaque modèle et indicateur.
  • Concevoir, exploiter et faire évoluer la plateforme d’apprentissage automatique — pipelines d’entraînement (Kubeflow sur Vertex AI), mise en service des modèles (FastAPI derrière les points de terminaison Vertex), CI/CD, conteneurisation et contrats typés. Assumer la responsabilité opérationnelle de l’infrastructure de mise en production des modèles afin que leur fiabilité ne repose pas uniquement sur les scientifiques des données.
  • Renforcer et standardiser les modèles de données essentiels aux opérations de l’entreprise — amélioration des schémas, correction des problèmes de qualité des données et mise en place de sources de vérité fiables.
  • Mettre en place des pratiques de gouvernance et d’observabilité des données — intégrer sous une gouvernance appropriée les données qui se trouvent à l’extérieur de l’entrepôt et créer des métriques opérationnelles pour les produits qui n’en disposent pas encore.
  • Standardiser les pratiques d’ingénierie des données à travers les différentes lignes de produits — modèles, outils et pipelines pouvant être réutilisés par les autres équipes.
  • Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de science des données, de développement backend et de produit afin de définir et maintenir le contrat entre producteurs et consommateurs de données (modèles produits par la science des données, consommés ou agrégés en aval et exposés aux clients).

Ce sur quoi vous travaillerez

Vous contribuerez à bâtir et à faire évoluer la plateforme de données qui alimente les produits d’intelligence financière de Flinks, soutenant notamment l’enrichissement et la catégorisation des transactions, ainsi que les solutions de gestion du risque et de prise de décision liées aux paiements.

Les principaux domaines d’intervention incluent :

  • Concevoir des pipelines de données évolutifs capables de traiter et de transformer de grands volumes de données financières.
  • Concevoir et maintenir des ensembles de données, modèles de données et pipelines de caractéristiques fiables utilisés par les équipes d’apprentissage automatique et de produit.
  • Améliorer la qualité des données, l’observabilité et les indicateurs opérationnels à travers notre plateforme et nos produits destinés aux clients.
  • Développer des services et infrastructures de données performants et optimisés en coûts afin de soutenir des charges de travail en temps réel et par lots.
  • Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Science des données, Produit et Ingénierie afin de permettre le développement de nouvelles capacités et d’accélérer la livraison de produits.
  • Contribuer à l’évolution de l’architecture de notre plateforme de données alors que nous continuons à faire croître nos produits, notre clientèle et nos capacités d’apprentissage automatique.

Notre environnement technologique

  • Python, SQL, Bash
  • Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • BigQuery et dbt
  • Airflow (Cloud Composer), Pub/Sub et Cloud Functions
  • Kubeflow, Vertex AI, MLflow et FastAPI
  • Docker, Terraform et Protocol Buffers
  • Azure DevOps
  • Grafana et GCP Logging

Vous n’avez pas besoin d’avoir travaillé avec chacun des outils mentionnés ci-dessus. De solides fondations en ingénierie des données et une expérience démontrée dans la conception de plateformes de données en production sont plus importantes qu’une connaissance approfondie de notre pile technologique actuelle. Le SQL constitue toutefois l’exception : il s’agit d’une exigence incontournable (voir les exigences clés).

Pourquoi ce poste?

Responsabilité sur un environnement en construction — contribuez à bâtir et à faire évoluer la plateforme de données qui alimentera la prochaine génération de produits de données et d’intelligence artificielle de Flinks.

Impact à fort levier — votre travail permettra aux équipes Science des données, Produit, Ingénierie et Risque d’avancer plus rapidement grâce à des données fiables et dignes de confiance.

Échelle et complexité réelles — travaillez avec d’importants volumes de données financières alimentant des produits utilisés par des banques, fintechs et institutions financières partout en Amérique du Nord.

Environnement infonuagique moderne — développez des solutions sur une pile technologique GCP moderne utilisant des outils contemporains de données, de plateformes et d’apprentissage automatique.

Exigences essentielles

Expérience :
Plus de 5 ans d’expérience pratique en ingénierie des données, incluant la conception, le développement et l’exploitation de plateformes de données, de pipelines et de solutions d’entreposage de données en environnement infonuagique.

Expertise en ingénierie des données :
Expérience approfondie en développement ETL/ELT, modélisation de données, conception de schémas, orchestration, qualité des données, traçabilité des données (data lineage) et optimisation d’entrepôts de données. Une expérience avec BigQuery, dbt, Airflow ou des outils modernes équivalents est fortement souhaitée.

Fondations techniques :
Excellente maîtrise du SQL et solides compétences en Python, avec la capacité de concevoir des solutions de données évolutives, maintenables et rigoureusement testées, soutenant à la fois les besoins opérationnels et analytiques.

Plateformes de données infonuagiques :
Expérience avec des écosystèmes de données modernes natifs du nuage, incluant les entrepôts de données, les architectures événementielles, le traitement distribué et les pratiques d’observabilité des plateformes.

Excellence opérationnelle :
Expérience démontrée dans la gestion de systèmes en production, notamment en matière de surveillance, de fiabilité, d’optimisation des performances, de contrôle des coûts, de gestion des incidents et d’amélioration continue des plateformes.

Expérience liée aux plateformes d’apprentissage automatique :
Une expérience soutenant des flux de travail d’apprentissage automatique, des pipelines de caractéristiques, des infrastructures de mise en production de modèles ou des environnements MLOps constitue un atout. Toutefois, une solide expertise en ingénierie des données demeure la principale exigence.

Collaboration :
Capacité à collaborer efficacement avec les équipes Science des données, Produit, Ingénierie et Assurance qualité (QA) afin de livrer des solutions de données fiables, évolutives et bien gouvernées.

Formation :
Baccalauréat en informatique, en ingénierie des données, en génie logiciel ou dans un domaine technique connexe, ou expérience pratique équivalente.

Autorisation de travail :
Doit être légalement autorisé(e) à travailler au Canada.

Fourchette salariale

Pour les candidats expérimentés et qualifiés résidant au Canada, au niveau principal (IC4), la fourchette salariale annuelle se situe entre 120 000 $ et 160 000 $ CAD.

Ce que Flinks offre

Dans le cadre de son programme global de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux, Flinks offre notamment :

  • Couverture santé et dentaire dès le premier jour
  • Politique de congés flexibles (FTO)
  • Environnement de travail à distance avec des rencontres et activités en personne régulières
  • Opportunités de développement professionnel, d’apprentissage et de croissance
  • Et bien plus encore

Accessibilité

Flinks s’engage à offrir des mesures d’adaptation aux personnes en situation de handicap. Si vous avez besoin d’un accommodement dans le cadre du processus de recrutement ou d’emploi, nous travaillerons avec vous afin de répondre à vos besoins.

Intelligence artificielle et recrutement

Flinks utilise l’intelligence artificielle (IA) dans le cadre de son processus de recrutement afin d’aider à la présélection, à l’évaluation ou à la sélection des candidats.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts
jobs.excerpt: Who We Are:Fusable is a leader in data-driven solutions for the trucking, agriculture, and construction industries.
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Fusable is a leader in data-driven solutions for the trucking, agriculture, and construction industries. We’re passionate about valuing our associates for their unique skills, ideas, and backgrounds, and we’re committed to building an inclusive, innovative workplace where everyone can thrive.

Your Role as a Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts:

Fusable is seeking a highly consultative, results-driven Strategic Account Executive to lead growth across a portfolio of strategic insurance carrier accounts and prospects. This role combines new business development with enterprise account expansion, focusing on commercial P&C insurers that cover Commercial Trucking.

As a trusted advisor, you will help clients leverage Fusable's portfolio of market-leading data, analytics, SaaS applications, and Data-as-a-Service (DaaS) solutions to solve critical business challenges. You will build executive-level relationships, uncover strategic opportunities, articulate measurable business value, and drive revenue growth through solution-based selling.

This is a senior sales role suited for professionals who thrive in complex enterprise environments, enjoy navigating multi-stakeholder sales cycles, and are passionate about the transformative power of data and analytics.

The position reports to the Sales Director, Strategic Accounts Risk Intelligence

A Day in the Life of a Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts:

Drive New Business Growth

  • Develop and execute strategic territory and account plans to increase market penetration within commercial P&C insurance organizations.
  • Identify, qualify, and pursue new enterprise opportunities within target accounts.
  • Conduct consultative discovery conversations to understand business objectives, pain points, and opportunities for value creation.
  • Position and demonstrate Fusable's solutions through compelling presentations, workshops, webinars, and executive-level business discussions.

Expand and Retain Strategic Accounts

  • Own and grow a portfolio of large enterprise customers by identifying expansion opportunities and increasing solution adoption.
  • Develop long-term account strategies aligned with client business priorities.
  • Conduct executive business reviews and strategic planning sessions that demonstrate ROI, customer value, and account health.
  • Drive customer retention and renewal success through proactive engagement and relationship management.

Lead Complex Sales Cycles

  • Manage opportunities through the entire sales lifecycle, from prospecting through contract execution.
  • Develop business cases and ROI-driven value propositions that align with client objectives.
  • Structure, negotiate, and close licensing, subscription, and enterprise agreements.
  • Maintain accurate forecasting, pipeline management, and CRM discipline.

Collaborate Across the Organization

  • Partner closely with Product Management, Marketing, Sales Engineering, Data Analytics, and Client Success teams.
  • Provide market intelligence and customer feedback that influence product innovation and go-to-market strategies.
  • Champion customer needs internally while helping shape solutions that create competitive differentiation.

What Success Looks Like:

  • Consistent achievement of revenue and growth goals.
  • Expansion of strategic relationships within enterprise insurance organizations.
  • Growth in customer adoption across Fusable's Risk Intelligence portfolio.
  • Strong client retention and renewal performance.
  • Trusted advisor status with executive and operational decision-makers.

What You Need:

  • 7+ years of successful B2B sales experience, including at least 5 years selling SaaS, DaaS, analytics, data, technology, or information services solutions to enterprise organizations.
  • Demonstrated success managing large, complex sales opportunities with multiple stakeholders and long sales cycles.
  • Proven track record of developing executive-level relationships and driving strategic account growth.
  • Experience creating and communicating business value through ROI-based or consultative selling methodologies.
  • Strong presentation, communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience selling into commercial P&C insurance carriers, reinsurers, MGAs, brokers, or related insurance markets.
  • Knowledge of commercial underwriting, risk management, claims, actuarial analysis, fleet, transportation, construction, specialty lines, or inland marine insurance.
  • Experience selling data analytics, predictive modeling, business intelligence, or risk intelligence solutions.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce CRM and modern sales engagement technologies.
  • Bachelor's degree in business, Marketing, Finance, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Someone has to build what makes that catalog possible: the publishing pipeline, the QA process, and a team of three that can run it well without you standing over their shoulder. This isn't a maintenance job. Nobody here has run a catalog at this scale before, so a lot of what you build in the first few months won't have a template to follow — you'd be building the foundation for a 100x scale-up from close to day one, and a year from now, you'll have a genuinely rare story to tell about what you built and when.

We're looking for someone who can lead a small team, own a production calendar, and hold a real quality bar under pressure, who also happens to be technical enough to get hands-on with a CMS when something needs fixing. If building the system behind a company's next stage of growth sounds like the kind of problem you want to solve, please apply.

You'll own our product catalog, our QA process, and the team of three that grows with it. Build the systems now, and a year from now your team is running most of it without you, while you're already onto the next big problem.

Le ou la Chef.fe de Produit traduit la stratégie produit et les priorités de la feuille de route en travaux clairs et réalisables pour les équipes de développement, tout en maximisant la valeur livrée à chaque version et à chaque sprint. Il s’agit d’un rôle tactique axé sur l’exécution : la personne titulaire du poste est responsable du backlog pour un domaine fonctionnel défini, collabore quotidiennement avec les équipes de développement et de conception, et veille à ce que les fonctionnalités développées répondent aux besoins les plus importants des clients et de l’entreprise.

Agissant comme principal point de liaison entre la vision du gestionnaire de produit et l’exécution de l’équipe de développement, le ou la propriétaire de produit combine une solide connaissance du domaine produit à une expérience pratique de la livraison agile. La réussite dans ce rôle repose sur un jugement solide au quotidien et sur la capacité à prendre des décisions éclairées quant aux compromis nécessaires afin de maintenir l’alignement avec la stratégie produit définie par la gestion de produits et les dirigeants de l’entreprise.

Principales responsabilités

  • Assurer la gestion et la priorisation du carnet de produit pour un domaine produit assigné, en rédigeant des user stories clairs ainsi que des critères d’acceptation qui traduisent les thèmes de la feuille de route et les exigences des clients en travaux concrets pour les équipes de développement.
  • Collaborer quotidiennement avec les équipes de développement et de conception tout au long du cycle de développement, notamment lors des activités de raffinement, de planification des sprints, des rencontres quotidiennes, des revues et des rétrospectives. Prendre rapidement des décisions concernant la portée, l’ordre de mise en œuvre et les priorités, et transmettre les compromis de nature stratégique ou financière au gestionnaire de produit ou au directeur, au besoin.
  • Valider que les fonctionnalités livrées répondent aux critères d’acceptation et aux résultats attendus pour les clients ou l’entreprise. Agir comme principal point de contact auprès de l’équipe de développement pour les questions liées aux exigences, à l’intention fonctionnelle et aux priorités.
  • Recueillir et synthétiser les commentaires provenant des équipes des ventes, du succès client, du soutien technique et des clients afin d’alimenter l’évolution du carnet de produit. Soutenir également le gestionnaire de produit dans les activités de recherche de marché, d’analyse concurrentielle et de définition des exigences fonctionnelles.
  • Effectuer le suivi et la production de rapports sur l’avancement des sprints et des versions, la vélocité ainsi que les indicateurs de livraison. Identifier de façon proactive les risques liés à la portée ou aux échéanciers et intégrer les commentaires issus des tests d’acceptation utilisateurs et des programmes bêta aux prochaines itérations du carnet de produit.

Qualifications et expérience

  • Baccalauréat en génie, en administration, en technologie ou dans un domaine connexe, ou expérience équivalente.
  • De 2 à 4 ans d’expérience à titre de chef.fe/responsable de produit, d’analyste d’affaires ou dans un rôle similaire lié à la livraison agile ou à la gestion de produits au sein d’une entreprise de logiciels.
  • Connaissance pratique des méthodologies Agile/Scrum et expérience concrète avec des outils de gestion des carnets de produit et des sprints tels que Jira ou Azure DevOps.
  • Capacité démontrée à traduire une orientation stratégique et les besoins de la clientèle en récits utilisateurs clairs et en critères d’acceptation précis.
  • Expérience de collaboration directe avec des équipes de développement et aisance à mener des discussions techniques portant sur la faisabilité, l’ordre de réalisation et les compromis.
  • Excellentes compétences analytiques et en résolution de problèmes, avec une grande attention aux détails dans la définition des exigences et la validation de la qualité.
  • Bonne compréhension des technologies infonuagiques, SaaS et des plateformes d’entreprise à grande échelle.

Qualifications privilégiées et exigences particulières

  • Expérience dans le domaine des technologies de l’information en santé.
  • Capacité démontrée à exercer un leadership d’influence plutôt que d’autorité.
  • Excellentes habiletés en communication et en organisation, avec un historique démontré de collaboration entre les équipes de développement, de conception et les partenaires d’affaires interfonctionnels.
