jobs.title: 2029 Sales & Relationship Academy - Greenwood Project Scholar Program
jobs.excerpt: About The Greenwood ProjectAt Greenwood Project, we open doors in financial services for undergraduate freshmen.
jobs.description:
About The Greenwood Project
At Greenwood Project, we open doors in financial services for undergraduate freshmen. We give our scholars three things: social capital, the network that comes from knowing people inside the industry. Academic and technical capital, the training the work actually requires. And aspirational capital, the belief that the seat belongs to you.
This is not a workshop series. Scholars commit to twelve months of training, deliver real work on real deadlines, and finish knowing whether this industry is for them. Many go on to internships and full time offers at our partner firms. All of them leave with a network they did not have before.
The Sales & Relationship Academy
This academy trains institutional sales and relationship management. We want to be straight with you about that before you apply. Over twelve months you will learn how financial products work, how to explain them to someone deciding whether to move millions of dollars, and how to build a relationship that outlasts a single transaction.
The training travels further than almost anything else we teach. The ability to prepare, listen, pitch, and hold a room is what every commercial role hires for. But the programming is built around selling to and servicing institutional clients, and that is the work you should want.
What this academy trains
  • Institutional sales. Selling investment products and ideas to large organizations such as pension funds, asset managers, and corporations, rather than to individual consumers. The twelve months are built around this.
  • Relationship management and client coverage. Owning the ongoing relationship with a client, understanding their business, and being the person they call first.
Where that training can take you
  • Capital markets sales. Working with clients on stock and bond issuance, hedging, and market access.
  • Wealth management and private client. Advising individuals and families on how their money is invested. This is the largest employer of client facing talent in the industry and a common first seat.
  • Client service and business development. Supporting existing relationships and opening new ones.
Read that split carefully. The first two are what we teach. The rest are real places scholars land, and this training is the right foundation for them. But if you want a client facing job without learning the products underneath it, this is the wrong academy.

Program Overview
We are recruiting 100 scholars into the Sales & Relationship Academy for the 2029 cohort. Across all three Greenwood academies we will select 325.
You are eligible if you are currently a freshman graduating in 2030. We call this the 2029 cohort because Summer 2029 is the internship you are working toward.
When What happens
  • October 2026 to June 2027 Rolling admissions. Decisions every month. November is the priority round.
  • July 2027 Academy begins.
  • July 2027 to June 2028 Twelve months of training, from the summer after freshman year through your sophomore year.
  • Fall 2028 Junior year internship recruiting season. Greenwood supports you through interviews.
  • Summer 2029 The goal: a 10 week internship with a partner firm, the summer after your junior year.
  • Spring 2030 You graduate.

How rolling admissions works
We review applications and make decisions every month from October 2026 through June 2027. You will hear back within 4 weeks of the round your application lands in. Seats fill as we go, so the earliest rounds have the most of them open. Apply early.
You get one application
You submit one application for this cohort. Not one per academy, and not one per round. Our Talent & Recruitment team may move you to a different academy than the one you selected if your answers point somewhere else, so you do not need to get that choice perfect.
Every application gets one of three outcomes:
  • Accepted. You are in.
  • Deferred. We want to see more before we decide, usually your next term of grades. Your application carries forward automatically and you do not need to submit anything new. You will hear from us about two weeks before the next round of decisions, and again every month until we decide. You will not sit in silence.
  • Declined. Final for this cycle. Because this program only admits freshmen, we cannot reconsider you in a later round.
Deferral is the reason you can apply in an early round without taking a risk. If we are not ready to decide, we hold your application. We will not turn you away for applying before your first semester was finished.
Deadlines in this process are real. Once you apply, we will ask you for things on a schedule: transcripts, forms, sometimes an interview time. If you miss those deadlines, your application is declined rather than delayed. We hold this line because the program itself runs on deadlines, and how you handle ours tells us how you will handle those.
Please read this carefully. Internship placements are not guaranteed. Greenwood trains you, advocates for you, and puts you in front of our partner firms. Those firms make their own hiring decisions. What we guarantee is the preparation, the network, and honest feedback. The offer is something you earn.
What You'll Do
  • Build and deliver client presentations and pitches, then get critiqued on them in front of your peers. Repeatedly, until it stops being frightening.
  • Run relationship management simulations, including the uncomfortable ones: a client who is unhappy, a client who says no, a client who knows more than you do.
  • Learn what you are actually selling. Training on capital markets products, meaning the stocks, bonds, and other instruments companies and investors use, and on what moves their prices.
  • Learn to read a client. Active listening, asking the question behind the question, and figuring out what someone needs when they have not said it clearly.
  • Work with a mentor who does this for a living, and meet professionals at our partner firms.
  • Practice getting told no. Resilience in this job is a technical skill and we treat it like one.
Building AI Fluency
The client facing side of financial services is being rebuilt around AI, though not in the way people fear. Trust is still built between two people. What changed is everything surrounding that conversation. AI assistants built into CRM systems now summarize calls, draft follow ups, update records, and flag which client to contact next. CRM stands for customer relationship management, the system every firm uses to track client relationships. Salespeople who use these tools well spend their time in front of clients. The ones who do not spend it on admin, and it shows in their numbers.
Hands on with real tools. You will not just learn concepts. You will build working skill with the software and AI tools used on the job. Each Greenwood academy trains a different technical toolset, chosen to match the roles that academy actually feeds, so what you build here is specific to client research, pitch development, and relationship management rather than a general overview of finance technology.
What AI cannot do for you: earn a client's trust, read a room, or hold your nerve in a negotiation. Those are the reasons this job still belongs to people, and they are what we will push you on hardest.

What We're Looking For - Ideal Degree Backgrounds

Your major does not decide which academy fits you. Your interest does. Plenty of freshmen have not declared yet, and some schools do not allow it until sophomore year. Neither works against you. Major titles also vary from school to school, so if yours is named differently but covers the same ground, it counts. Tell us what it is called where you are.
Fields of study that line up with this academy
  • Finance
  • Business Administration, Management, or General Business
  • Communications
  • Economics
  • Political Science or Public Policy
  • Psychology or Sociology
  • Any major, if you can communicate well and are willing to learn the products
If you have not declared a major yet
You can apply as undeclared. What we need to see is that you are seriously pointed toward client facing work in financial services, meaning roles where the relationship is the job. Undeclared is not a weaker application. An undeclared student who can show us the following is stronger than a declared student who cannot.
  • Courses you have taken or registered for next term, such as economics, business, communications, or public speaking
  • Clubs and activities that back it up: a sales or pitch competition, debate, student government, a campus job in customer service, or anything where you have had to persuade someone
  • Anything you have taught yourself about markets or financial products
  • A clear answer to why this academy and not the Investment Banking or Fintech Academy
If your major is not on this list
This academy is the most major agnostic of the three, so almost nobody should be ruled out by field of study. What matters is whether you can hold a conversation, handle rejection, and put in the work to learn markets.

Technical skills you will build
You are not expected to arrive with any of these. You are expected to want them.
  • Market awareness, meaning the ability to speak credibly about what is happening in markets and why it matters to a client
  • A working understanding of capital markets and financial instruments, including stocks, bonds, and derivatives at a conceptual level
  • Presentation development and delivery, including the storytelling that makes a deck land
  • CRM systems and disciplined relationship tracking
  • Enough financial analysis to hold your own in a client conversation about numbers
  • Client and market research, so you walk in already knowing their business
  • Working with AI tools for research, drafting, and call follow up
Soft skills and characteristics
Greenwood selects scholars who show grit, resourcefulness, and intellectual curiosity, along with:
  • Strong verbal and written communication
  • Natural relationship building instincts and comfort with people you do not know
  • Confidence in client facing situations and in front of a room
  • Active listening, and the ability to hear what a client actually needs
  • Persuasive communication and early negotiation instincts
  • Resilience. You will be told no more often than yes, and it cannot change how you show up.
  • Adaptability and quick thinking when a conversation goes somewhere you did not plan for

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

What Makes a Strong Sales Academy Candidate:
The strongest candidates genuinely like people and are willing to be told no. That combination is rarer than it sounds. Being outgoing is not the qualification. Plenty of excellent salespeople are quiet. What matters is preparation, listening, and follow through.
What this takes
  • Twelve months, from the summer after freshman year through your sophomore year, on top of a full course load.
  • Roughly 6 to 8 hours per week, with heavier weeks around pitch deadlines.
  • Presenting in front of your peers and industry professionals, and being critiqued directly.
  • Managing your class schedule around program commitments and staying organized without being chased.
Eligibility Requirements
  • Currently enrolled as a freshman (Class of 2030) at an accredited four year institution
  • Minimum 3.2 GPA for standard consideration
  • Students with a GPA between 3.0 and 3.19 may apply with a required personal essay
  • Students below a 3.0 GPA are not eligible for this cycle
  • Your high school transcript, submitted with your application
  • Your first semester or first quarter college transcript, submitted with your application or as soon as grades post if you apply in an early round
  • A demonstrated commitment to excellence, integrity, character, and collaboration
If your GPA falls between 3.0 and 3.19, the essay is not a formality. Tell us what the number does not capture, and be specific about what you changed.
If you apply in an early round before you have a college GPA, we review your high school record first and confirm eligibility once your first term transcript arrives.

What You'll Gain

  • Communication skills that transfer anywhere. The ability to pitch, present, and hold a room is useful in every job you will ever have, including the ones outside finance.
  • Product knowledge. You will understand what you are selling, which separates a credible young salesperson from a scripted one.
  • AI capability most candidates do not have. Working AI tools into client research, outreach, and call follow up is exactly what sales desks are hiring for right now.
  • A real network. One on one coaching, a mentor in the industry, and access to professionals at our partner firms.
  • Resilience you can point to. You will have been told no, in practice, before it happens with a real client and a real number attached.

JOB TITLE: ESOP Administrator

DEPARTMENT: ESOP Services

REPORTS TO: Director of ESOP Services

About ESOP Partners, Inc.

ESOP Partners, Inc. is a third-party administration and consulting firm dedicated to providing a liquid business transition solution for owners of closely held businesses through the establishment, maintenance, and sustainability of Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs). Our mission is to maximize the financial and cultural benefits of employee ownership by helping ESOP companies build strong, informed, and engaged employee ownership cultures.

We aspire to be nationally recognized as the leading ESOP firm in the country. We pursue this vision through our Core Values:

  • Seek to Understand – We identify the underlying reasons behind questions and actions and take ownership of continuous learning and improvement.
  • Manage Expectations – We proactively communicate clear, specific, and achievable objectives to create alignment and accountability.
  • Collaborate – We work together through constructive discussion and teamwork to achieve win-win outcomes.
  • Get Things Done – We prioritize, organize, and execute efficiently to deliver accurate and timely results.
  • Practice Professional Skepticism – We apply a questioning mindset to objectively analyze information for quality and accuracy.
  • Exhibit Mental Strength – We manage challenges with professionalism, resilience, and a solutions-oriented attitude.

Position Summary

The ESOP Administrator is responsible for the accurate and timely recordkeeping and administration of ESOP and KSOP plans, including compliance testing and analysis of plan provisions in accordance with individual plan documents. This role manages project work within established deadlines, performs detailed compliance reviews, and prepares high-quality data reports for internal quality review and external product delivery.   • Ensure ERISA regulatory reporting is completed in a timely manner.

  • High level of attention to detail and analytical skills

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

Buscamos um Analista de Ambiente de QA para integrar o time Testes em nosso cliente.

Além de oferecer soluções completas em produtos bancários, ela desempenha um papel essencial em políticas públicas, apoiando programas habitacionais, iniciativas de inclusão financeira e projetos voltados ao bem-estar da população.

O que você vai fazer?

  • Elaborar e manter atualizada a estratégia de testes dos sistemas;
  • Construir e manter scripts, artefatos e cenários de testes;
  • Acompanhar o desenvolvimento das demandas desde a concepção até a entrega;
  • Antecipar ações necessárias para garantir a correta execução dos testes;
  • Apoiar a implementação de práticas de qualidade durante todo o ciclo de desenvolvimento;
  • Validar entregas realizadas pelos times de desenvolvimento;
  • Planejar e executar testes funcionais e não funcionais conforme a necessidade de cada demanda;
  • Mapear e atualizar o caminho crítico das aplicações;
  • Apoiar atividades de homologação e aceite junto aos usuários gestores;
  • Atuar na melhoria contínua da qualidade das aplicações em parceria com a equipe de Certificação;
  • Garantir a rastreabilidade entre requisitos, testes, código-fonte e demais artefatos;
  • Gerenciar e gerar massa de testes garantindo disponibilidade dos dados necessários;
  • Realizar a gestão de ambientes, incluindo criação, configuração, manutenção e equalização dos ambientes de desenvolvimento e testes;
  • Contribuir para entregas de TI com mais qualidade, segurança e eficiência.

CONHECIMENTO/ATIVIDADES

🧪 Gestão e Execução de Testes

  • Gestão e planejamento de testes, com capacidade para geração de documentação básica de testes como estratégia, planos, casos, scripts, roteiros, evidências e massa de testes;
  • Planejar e executar testes alinhando o escopo da disciplina ao prazo disponível;
  • Criar scripts automatizados e não automatizados em ferramentas específicas, executando-os e analisando os resultados;
  • Executar testes de aceitação, compatibilidade, regressão, integração, funcionais e não funcionais;
  • Realizar testes exploratórios, conectividade, vulnerabilidade, estresse e carga conforme necessidade da demanda;
  • Avaliar os resultados de cada ciclo de testes;
  • Identificar os itens de teste-alvo a serem avaliados pelo esforço de testes;
  • Elaborar cenários de testes de software;
  • Criar testes baseados em cenários de negócio, experiência e defeitos;
  • Registrar erros encontrados durante a execução dos testes, relacionando-os aos produtos de trabalho pertinentes;
  • Monitorar e acompanhar os níveis de cobertura de testes, promovendo aumento de cobertura sempre que necessário.

⚙️ Automação, Ambientes e Ferramentas

  • Manter em execução toda a estrutura que compõe os testes dos sistemas envolvidos, incluindo massa, scripts, artefatos, simuladores, rotinas e processos negociais;
  • Construir mocks, stubs e simuladores para viabilizar a execução de testes;
  • Manutenção dos ciclos dos sistemas em ambientes definidos e laboratório;
  • Manutenção de rotinas diárias, mensais, batch e interfaces;
  • Conhecimento em ferramentas de gestão de testes, gestão de defeitos, bug tracking, automação, performance, planejamento e execução de testes;
  • Utilização de ferramentas especializadas para automatização, performance, virtualização de interfaces e geração de massa;
  • Trabalhar com execução automatizada utilizando massa de dados variável (datapool).

🚀 Performance e Segurança

  • Avaliar requisitos não funcionais de desempenho utilizando ferramentas específicas e monitores;
  • Realizar testes e validações de segurança, identificando vulnerabilidades e propondo melhorias;
  • Conhecimento das principais falhas e técnicas de testes em software;
  • Avaliar aspectos de segurança indicados pelo OWASP.

🤝 Atuação em Produto e Desenvolvimento

  • Compreender o funcionamento dos sistemas em teste;
  • Compreender negócio, requisitos, programação e testes, atuando como co-responsável por todo o ciclo de desenvolvimento;
  • Conhecer notações de requisitos em modelos ágeis e tradicionais;
  • Apoiar gestores e equipes na homologação de demandas;
  • Auxiliar o Product Owner na escrita de critérios de aceite das histórias do backlog;
  • Apoiar o Product Owner no aceite das histórias da sprint;
  • Auxiliar na escrita de testes unitários automatizados;
  • Realizar práticas de ATDD, BDD e/ou Specification by Example.

📌 Experiência Esperada

  • Experiência em Gestão e Planejamento de Testes;
  • Experiência com documentação de testes;
  • Experiência com automação, performance e execução de testes;
  • Conhecimento em identificação de falhas e erros comuns em software.

CERTIFICAÇÃO OBRIGATÓRIA

Pelo menos uma das certificações abaixo, ou equivalente:

• ATC – Analista de Teste Certificado do IBQTS - Instituto Brasileiro de Qualidade em Testes de Software;

• CBTS - Certificação Brasileira de Teste de Software da ALATS - Associação Latino Americana de Teste de Software ou equivalente ou certificações similares;

• CTFL - Certified Tester Foundation Level

• CTFL-AT - Certificação Certified Tester Foundation Level - Agile Tester do BSTQB ou ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation Level - Agile Tester

Job Title

Program Integrity Director

Job Summary

The Program Integrity Lead defines and leads Noridian's enterprise Program Integrity strategy, with a primary focus on Medicare programs and initiatives that advance fraud, waste, and abuse prevention, payment integrity, medical review, provider audits, data analytics, and compliance operations. Serving as Noridian's strategic authority in Program Integrity, this leader identifies opportunities to strengthen Medicare contracts, expand service capabilities, drive innovation for Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and other federal customers, and improve operational performance. The role is accountable for developing and executing a multi-year strategy that enhances contract value, supports revenue growth, advances CMS objectives, and positions Noridian as an industry leader in Program Integrity.

Essential Functions

(Key Duties/Responsibilities/Accountabilities)

Organizational Impact:

• Develops and maintains Noridian's enterprise Program Integrity strategy and roadmap.

• Establishes a future-state vision for Program Integrity capabilities across Medicare operations.

• Creates executive recommendations regarding investments, technology, partnerships, staffing models, and operational enhancements.

• Develops and executes a growth strategy focused on expanding Program Integrity work within Noridian's existing Medicare and Medicaid contracts as well as new bid opportunities..

• Identifies opportunities to increase contract value through additional CMS scope, new demonstrations and pilots, Program Integrity authorities, provider audit services, advanced analytics capabilities, automation and AI solutions, and medical review modernization.

• Builds business cases supporting additional Medicare work and contract modifications.

• Translates approved strategies into executable operational plans.

• Establishes performance metrics and dashboards to monitor financial impact, quality outcomes, operational performance, customer satisfaction, compliance effectiveness, and program return on investment.

• Ensures alignment between Program Integrity initiatives, quality strategy, compliance requirements, and enterprise objectives.

Communications & Influence:

• Partners with Business Development, Government Affairs, Customer Relations, and Operations leaders to position Noridian as a trusted CMS advisor.

• Supports customer engagement efforts by preparing thought leadership materials, CMS presentations, concept papers, and value propositions.

• Builds relationships with CMS leaders, Medicare stakeholders, industry partners, vendors, and professional organizations.

• Represents Noridian in industry forums, conferences, customer discussions, and strategic planning sessions.

• Advises senior leadership regarding investment decisions, emerging technologies, and future Program Integrity opportunities.

• Fosters collaboration between operational, technical, clinical, compliance, and business development teams.

Innovation & Complexity:

• Identifies emerging CMS priorities, regulatory trends, fraud schemes, payment integrity initiatives, and policy changes that may create risks or opportunities.

• Evaluates and recommends opportunities involving medical review, provider audits, data analytics, prior authorization, fraud prevention, predictive analytics, payment integrity, and AI-enabled Program Integrity solutions.

• Evaluates external partnership opportunities that strengthen Noridian's Program Integrity capabilities and competitive position.

• Defines implementation roadmaps, timelines, business cases, success measures, and governance models.

• Oversees pilot programs and innovation efforts from concept through operational deployment.

• Champions innovation and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance Program Integrity outcomes.

Leadership & Talent Management:

• Leads cross-functional teams responsible for execution.

• Partners with Operations, Technology, Continuous Improvement and Quality, Data and Analytics, Customer Relations, Clinical Services, and Business Development teams to implement initiatives.

Knowledge & Experience:

• Serves as the primary internal consultant and subject matter expert on Program Integrity strategy.

Non-Essential Duties and Functions:

• Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, Public Administration, Data Analytics, Nursing, Health Information Management, or related field OR equivalent work experience.

  • Demonstrated experience developing enterprise strategies and translating them into operational execution plans.
  • Strong knowledge of Medicare operations, CMS programs, and federal healthcare contracting.
  • Experience presenting to senior executives and external stakeholders.
  • Exceptional communication, relationship management, and strategic planning skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree, such as MBA, MHA, MPH, or related field.
  • Experience with Medicare Administrative Contractor, Supplemental Medicare Review Contractor (SMRC), Unified Program Integrity Contractor (UPIC), RAC, or other CMS Program Integrity programs.
  • Experience leading or managing a Program Integrity function within a federal or state government agency, with demonstrated responsibility for oversight of fraud, waste, and abuse prevention, compliance activities, investigative operations, audit programs, and/or payment integrity initiatives in a publicly funded program environment.
  • Experience with AI, predictive analytics, fraud detection technologies, or healthcare data platforms.

Description

Join Intellect and help shape the future of workplace mental health in Australia

Intellect is a modern mental health company on a mission to make high quality mental healthcare more accessible, effective, and measurable.

We partner with organisations to deliver evidence based mental health support, and we are helping redefine workplace mental health in Australia through strong clinical governance, psychosocial risk capability, and outcomes focused care.

We are now hiring a CISP - Required, (AHPRA - preferred but not mandatory) registered Clinical Psychologist for a full time, freelance remote role based in Kalgoorlie-Boulder .

This is a unique opportunity for a psychologist who wants more than a traditional therapy role. You will combine direct clinical care with workplace assessments, psychosocial risk work, stakeholder partnership, crisis response support, and research collaboration.

You will be a practitioner on our telehealth platform 'Intellect', where your role is to support our clients' mental health and personal growth based on the individual needs and goals. This is delivered primarily through scheduled 60-minute video sessions on our platform.

This is a freelance remote role with the flexibility to decide your business hours. Local candidates are preferred but others can still be considered. This role is a great opportunity to supplement your current job or private practice.


Why join Intellect

  • Full time, remote, freelance role based in Kalgoorlie-Boulder
  • Varied scope across therapy, assessments, workplace mental health, and crisis support
  • Clinical supervision provided
  • Admin support provided
  • No need to build your own referral pipeline
  • Be part of the broader Clinical team, in a role with both direct client impact and systems level influence
  • Join a clinically led team focused on quality, governance, and measurable outcomes

About the role

This role is ideal for a clinician who:

  • enjoys variety in their work
  • wants to apply their skills beyond a therapy room only
  • is confident engaging both clients and non clinical stakeholders
  • is motivated by evidence based practice and systems level impact

Team and support

You will be part of Intellect’s broader Clinical team, working in a collaborative environment with clinical, operational, and cross functional partners.

This role is designed to support high quality clinical work, with supervision, CPD support, and admin support in place, so psychologists can focus on care quality and impact.

You will play an important role in delivering high quality care, supporting workplace mental health initiatives, and helping build Intellect’s clinical and research presence in Australia.

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Care and Psychological Assessments

  • Provide evidence based psychological therapy, both in person and virtually, in line with AHPRA requirements and Intellect clinical governance standards

  • Conduct psychological and workplace related assessments, including return to work assessments and other psychosocial or functional assessments
  • Provide case management and care coordination where required, including risk monitoring and escalation

Workplace Mental Health and Psychosocial Risk

  • Contribute to psychosocial risk assessments and workplace mental health initiatives across client organisations
  • Support the development of clinically sound recommendations and reports

Stakeholder partnership and Clinical Account Support

  • Liaise with client representatives and internal stakeholders to uphold clinical quality, service standards, and reporting integrity
  • Act as a trusted clinical voice in programme discussions, helping ensure delivery remains evidence based, safe, and fit for purpose

Crisis and Critical Incident Support

  • Support on site crisis response deployments when required, including psychological first aid, group briefings, and individual stabilisation sessions

Research and Evidence Generation

  • Contribute to Intellect’s research and evaluation efforts in Australia, including partnerships with universities and applied workplace mental health studies
  • Support clinically grounded data collection, interpretation, and programme improvement initiatives
  • Help strengthen Intellect’s evidence base and thought leadership in workplace mental health and psychosocial safety

Requirements

  • CISP - Required, (AHPRA - preferred but not mandatory) registered Clinical Psychologist

  • Minimum 3 years of clinical experience in psychological therapy and assessment
  • Experience in case management and workplace related assessments, including return to work and workplace reports, is highly regarded
  • Experience in psychosocial risk assessment or workplace mental health programmes is highly regarded
  • Strong clinical judgement and communication skills
  • Comfortable working across individual care, organisational contexts, and stakeholder engagement
  • Experience supporting complex, high risk, or safety critical populations is advantageous

Benefits

Why You’ll Love Working With Us:

  • Global company – work in a diverse environment with people from nearly 20 countries
  • Flexible work arrangements – work in a way that suits your lifestyle and goals
  • Work-life balance – a culture that values personal time and long-term wellness

Job Title: Specialist Editor, Asia-Pacific

Department: Programs, Asia-Pacific

Compensation: Determined based on skills and experience and local market ranges. See below for more information.

Location/Workspace Designation: Remote, based in the Asia-Pacific region. Country/city is flexible.

Reports to Title: Regional Director, Asia-Pacific

Closing Date: September 20, 2026

Organization Overview:

Founded in 1981, the Committee to Protect Journalists (“CPJ”) is an independent, non-profit organization defending journalists worldwide without regard to their political ideology. Through its work to safeguard journalists, CPJ protects the rights of all people to have access to diverse and independent sources of information. For over four decades, CPJ has helped win the early release of imprisoned journalists, secure convictions in journalist murders, and enable legal reform in countries where free expression has deteriorated. CPJ’s widely cited database and reports have raised global awareness of attacks on press freedom. Learn more about CPJ’s fight to defend freedom of the press here

At CPJ, we are dedicated to upholding values of equity and free expression in both our internal operations and external endeavors. As a global organization headquartered in the United States, we aspire to build a diverse workplace and foster an inclusive and welcoming environment. We strive for our people to be representative of the global community on which we report and to equip them with the opportunities and resources they need to learn and succeed.

Job Summary:

The Specialist Editor - Asia-Pacific is responsible for executing CPJ’s regional editorial strategy. This includes commissioning, writing, editing, and publishing stories, statements, reports, and other editorial products as needed for CPJ’s various publishing platforms, including the CPJ website and social media.

The Specialist Editor - Asia-Pacific will be embedded within the regional program, reporting directly to the Regional Director and working closely with CPJ’s Research & Analysis team. This role is designed to ensure that editorial output aligns with local priorities and effectively supports CPJ’s mission. This role is responsible for writing, editing, and publishing a range of content—including news alerts, statements, reports, and social media posts—aligned with CPJ’s press freedom mission and regional priorities.

The editor will commission, edit, and publish daily content on CPJ’s various publishing platforms in a timely manner with a focus on content relative to the Asia-Pacific region.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Commission, write, edit and publish daily content, including news alerts, statements, letters, reports, and other materials that align with regional needs and priorities
  • Publish content on CPJ’s website, including selecting photos and writing captions
  • Manage and publish regional social media content in real-time, ensuring timely, accurate, and engaging posts that adhere to CPJ’s communications strategy
  • Disseminate regional content via email or other communication channels according to the regional editorial and communications strategy
  • Ensure content production and publication align with regional time zones and audience requirements
  • Edit research on journalists who have been killed, imprisoned, or attacked for their work, ensuring accuracy and adherence to CPJ’s editorial standards
  • Utilize CPJ’s internal knowledge management system (Carta) for research purposes
  • Identify thematic issues and integrate them into the research and analysis strategy

Please note that YLC does not provide direct legal representation to individual youth and families.

Our summer interns will contribute to a variety of YLC's ongoing and emerging advocacy projects, based on their particular interests and strengths, with a specific goal of developing at least one strong writing sample for use in future job and funding applications. Interns will enjoy the benefits of working with multiple attorneys in our highly collaborative, welcoming, and dedicated team, and can look forward to a rich summer program including:

  • Training through our annual summer seminar series, providing overviews of the child welfare and juvenile justice systems, different strategic approaches to youth and child advocacy, opportunities in public interest law, and key systemic issues informing YLC's advocacy work today;
  • Participation in YLC team meetings, strategic advocacy meetings, and other workgroups on areas of interest;
  • Close one-on-one supervisory support and feedback from one or more YLC attorneys;
  • Opportunities to meet with YLC staff to discuss career interests and opportunities in the field in greater depth;
  • Completion of one or more substantial research and writing projects;
  • Potential opportunities to observe legislative hearings and to visit juvenile facilities (as available and depending on your location); and
  • Invitations to YLC and other summer intern events.

Examples of recent intern projects include:

  • A youth-facing written resource on the rights of pregnant and parenting foster youth;
  • A research memo providing a national overview of foster care transitions policies;
  • A handbook on prudent parent standards for foster youth participation in social justice and activism;
  • A research memo on civil claims available for mistreatment in juvenile facilities; and
  • Comments to promulgated regulations in multiple states regarding licensing of child welfare and juvenile justice facilities.

Qualified candidates will have excellent research and writing skills, be able to stay directed and focused in a fully remote work environment, have experience and/or interest in child and youth advocacy, and want to explore nonprofit legal aid and systemic advocacy environments as a possible career path. We are particularly interested in hearing from students with personal, lived experience in child welfare and juvenile justice systems and people from historically marginalized identities that are disproportionately represented in the child welfare and juvenile justice systems. YLC believes that those who have experienced these systems are best positioned to understand the impacts of systems change, and we're committed to developing youth advocates with lived experience through our hiring practices.

Position Details

The summer intern position is a full-time (37.5 hours/week), 10-week internship position. The position may begin as early as the final week of May 2027, with some flexibility for a later start date if needed.

This position will be completed on a fully remote basis and can be performed from anywhere within the contiguous United States—you are not required to live in or be willing to relocate to the San Francisco Bay Area to apply for this role. Though this position is remote, interns are expected to work a set schedule from 9am – 5pm in their local time zone and to be fully available during those hours. The option to attend in-person meetings or to reserve individual or group workspace may be available to summer interns living locally in the Bay Area.

Funding - This position will be an unpaid, volunteer position. We expect interns to apply for summer funding through their school's public interest funding program and/or other funding programs, as available, in order to participate. After those funding options have been exhausted, YLC will provide supplementary equity funding as needed to ensure that all of our interns receive the same total summer funding amount.

To Apply

You will be required to submit the following documents as your application:

  • A cover letter, explaining your interest in working with YLC and in our advocacy for systems-involved young people, including any relevant personal, educational, or professional background that motivates you to pursue this opportunity. If possible, let us know in your cover letter if you believe you will need YLC funding for the summer (this information will not affect hiring decisions).
    • If you have personal lived experience in the child welfare and/or juvenile justice systems, we strongly encourage you to explain in your cover letter your how your experience motivates you to pursue a legal advocacy career.
  • Resume, with a list of three professional/academic references
  • A legal writing sample

Law school transcripts are not required for this application and will not be factored into our hiring decisions.

Please contact with any questions about the position or application process, but do not send your application materials to this address. Applications sent via email instead of being submitted through the application form will not be considered.

The final deadline for applications is March 5th, 2027, though we strongly recommend applying sooner, no later than mid-January as positions may be filled in advance of this deadline.

Equal Opportunity Employer

YLC values a diverse, inclusive workforce, and we provide equal employment opportunity for all applicants and employees. All qualified applicants for employment will be considered without regard to an individual’s actual or perceived race, color, sex, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, body size, hair style, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, physical or mental disability, neurotypicality, medical condition, family care status, marital status, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local laws.

jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world, processing 25+ trillion data points annually across thousands of connected devices. The Samsara Application Security team protects this vast footprint end-to-end, spanning cloud services, internal systems, and firmware running on IoT hardware in the field.

As a Staff Application Security Engineer, you’ll drive the overarching technical direction for our application security and vulnerability management programs. This is a high-visibility role where you'll influence a broad surface area while retaining the flexibility to dive deep into critical domain focus areas as security priorities evolve.

This is a remote position, open to candidates residing in the UK. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, and countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper-growth environment.
  • You're energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead the ongoing strategy, operation, and continuous improvement of Samsara's vulnerability management program, along with other core application security programs — not just execute against an existing process, but define what the process should be.
  • Own and drive down mean time to remediate (MTTR) across the vulnerability backlog, as SLAs tighten.
  • Build and champion automation and tooling that scale vulnerability detection and response across cloud, firmware/IoT, and corporate systems, rather than relying on manual, one-by-one review.
  • Set technical and architectural direction for the program, translating leadership's strategic priorities into a concrete execution plan for the team.
  • Drive remediation by building trust with engineering teams and providing clear, actionable guidance — partnering with technical program management on reporting rather than owning it directly.
  • Mentor and level up other engineers on secure design and remediation practices, and be a technical voice other teams look to when priorities are unclear.
  • Communicate risk and remediation tradeoffs to engineering leadership in terms they can act on, without owning the relationship end to end.
  • Participate in security incident investigations involving high-profile vulnerabilities, assessing potential impact on Samsara's infrastructure.
  • Be regularly on call to support critical vulnerability response.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 10+ years of relevant experience as a cloud engineer or security engineer, including hands-on vulnerability management across a broad, multi-product enterprise environment — not a single product or team's slice of it.
  • Proficiency in Go, Python, and JavaScript.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently set technical and architectural direction for a security program, and to drive remediation across a broad, multi-surface environment without direct authority over the teams doing the fixing.
  • Significant experience with modern vulnerability management tooling (e.g., Wiz, Semgrep) and deep familiarity with vulnerability scoring frameworks such as CVSS and EPSS.
  • Strong AWS cloud services background.
  • Deep understanding of Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), and Software Composition Analysis (SCA).
  • Hands-on use of AI/LLM tooling in your own security workflow — triage, detection logic, remediation drafting — plus credibility speaking to how AI is changing the threat landscape and the tooling available to address it.
  • Location: must be based in central or eastern timezones.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience with C/C++, relevant to firmware and embedded systems.
  • Background at a cloud-native, AI-forward company actively building agentic or AI-driven products.
  • Experience with security automation platforms (e.g., Tines) and serverless frameworks (e.g., AWS Lambda).
  • Experience integrating vulnerability management into modern CI/CD pipelines with a "shift-left" mentality.
  • Experience spanning SaaS, firmware, and corporate IT security programs — not just one product line.
  • Experience managing vulnerabilities within a FedRAMP-certified environment.
  • Experience building, extending, or wiring up AI copilots/agents for security workflows (e.g., automated triage, remediation drafting).

This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
£138,800—£173,500 GBP

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. jobs.description:
About Us

Snappy Shopper is the UK’s fastest‑growing quick commerce (Q‑commerce) platform powering rapid grocery delivery from local convenience stores. We enable independent retailers and major partners, including SPAR, Nisa, Premier, Co‑op and others, to digitally transform their business by offering same‑day and rapid delivery of food, drink and everyday essentials within as little as 30‑60 minutes. Customers on our platform typically spend significantly more online than in‑store, helping retailers grow revenue and deepen community engagement.

We’re more than a delivery app, we’re a technology partner for local high streets, providing tools for digital sales, marketing solutions, and integrations that help retailers compete with larger online players.

At Snappy Shopper, we’re committed toinnovation, retail empowerment and community impact, helping stores thrive digitally, offering exceptional local convenience to customers, and shaping the future of on‑demand retail in the UK.

Our location

We are a UK company with colleagues across the country and offices in Dundee and Edinburgh. This is a UK-based remote role, with occasional opportunities to connect with colleagues in person.

About the team

You'll join our Infrastructure team, working closely with Software Engineers and other technical teams to keep the systems behind Snappy secure, reliable and performing at their best.

We're looking for someone with strong, hands-on systems administration experience who has also developed modern cloud and DevOps capability.

You'll be equally comfortable getting under the hood of a Linux production environment as you are working with AWS, Terraform, automation and CI/CD.

About the role

As a Senior Linux Systems & DevOps Engineer, you'll take a hands-on responsibility for running, troubleshooting and improving the infrastructure our platform depends on.

This isn't a role focused solely on cloud provisioning and deployment pipelines. You'll work across Linux systems, web and application infrastructure, databases, networking, AWS and automation, and you'll be expected to investigate problems through the full technology stack when something isn't behaving as expected.

Day-to-day, you will:

  • Manage, monitor and improve our production AWS and Linux infrastructure.

  • Run and maintain the services our platform depends on, including nginx, Apache, Redis, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch and relational databases.

  • Maintain and improve our infrastructure as code, configuration management and CI/CD environment using Terraform, Ansible and Bitbucket Pipelines.

  • Manage our CDN and WAF layer across Akamai and Cloudflare.

  • Monitor platform health and performance, responding to alerts and identifying opportunities to improve resilience.

  • Take ownership of production incidents, troubleshooting across systems, networking, databases and infrastructure to identify root cause and restore service.

  • Automate repetitive operational work using Python and Bash.

  • Participate in our shared 24/7 on-call rota once fully onboarded.

To be successful, you'll have:

We're looking for someone with genuine systems administration depth alongside modern DevOps capability.

You'll bring solid experience in DevOps, Systems Administration or a similar infrastructure role, with strong hands-on Linux experience in business-critical production environments.

You'll be confident troubleshooting beyond the cloud or deployment layer, working across operating systems, networking, web infrastructure and databases to understand what's actually causing a problem.

You'll also have strong AWS and infrastructure-as-code experience, an automation-first mindset, and the ability to take ownership when production issues arise. You'll be comfortable working independently, making sound decisions under pressure and knowing when to involve others.

Experience across our wider technology stack, including nginx, Apache, Redis, MariaDB/RDS/Postgres, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, Terraform and CDN/WAF technologies will be important, although we're equally interested in your underlying technical depth and ability to pick up the specifics of our environment.

You'll also need to be comfortable participating in a 24/7 on-call rota.

Experience with Bitbucket Pipelines, Ansible and monitoring tools such as Zabbix, CloudWatch, Pingdom or New Relic would be useful, as would working knowledge of PHP or Node.js and experience within PCI DSS or ISO 27001 environments.

Who you are

  • Community: You collaborate and share success with colleagues and partners.

SENIOR PAID MEDIA STRATEGIST

ROLE OVERVIEW

A Senior Paid Media Strategist at CTC is a full-funnel expert across both paid search and paid social. This place isn't for everyone, but it might be for you if…

YOU SET THE STANDARD

  • Your decisions are research-backed, every time
  • Your client service is the bar others aspire to
  • You arrive at meetings prepared, with data, insight, and a point of view

YOU ARE DRIVEN TO INCREASE VALUE

  • You're passionate about building brands for the next generation

  • You seek opportunities to sharpen your skills without being prompted
  • You resist the temptation to play victim; you own outcomes 100%
  • You're willing to put in the reps to be a domain expert
  • You inspire others through the standard you hold for yourself

WHAT YOU'LL DO

INNOVATE

You stay on the frontier of paid media strategy and technology across both search and social. You combine data analysis and client feedback to develop strategic plans spanning Google Ads and Meta. You make tactical recommendations for targeting, messaging, and campaign optimization across platforms. You test constantly, investigate relentlessly, and adapt strategy based on statistical outcomes. When it's time to pivot, you're among the first. You bring early insights to the team and lead the way.

CREATE

Creative problems take creative solutions. You write compelling direct-response copy for both search and social, build out campaigns in Google Ads and Meta Ads Manager, and ensure every initiative is launched on time, on budget, and built to win. You use historical data to guide decisions and find the hidden solution others miss. Attention to detail, proactive problem-solving, and data-driven decision-making are non-negotiables.

OWN

KPIs are your bread and butter. Google Sheets is your jam. "Count on Me" is your mantra. You see things through to the end. You project monthly budgets for each account, back every recommendation with data, and communicate results clearly to clients and teammates. You hold yourself to a high standard and share your learnings to elevate the buyers around you. People know: if you're involved, it gets done.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

SUCCESS IN YOUR DAY-TO-DAY

  • Optimize ad accounts across Google and Meta, building, testing, and iterating on campaign types, ad copy, creative, budgets, and bids to hit spend and ROAS targets
  • Monitor active campaigns and adjust budgets and strategy in real time for the best results
  • Forecast future budgets and performance using historical data and industry trends
  • Run multivariate tests to determine the best-performing creative, copy, and audiences
  • Pull and sort data tables to guide creative teams on top-performing elements
  • Troubleshoot accounts for errors and warnings across Google Ads, Google Merchant Center, and Meta Ads Manager
  • Communicate meaningful results to clients in weekly meetings, reports, and team debriefs
  • Coach and assist junior buyers, sharing knowledge to uplift the full team

SUCCESS IN YOUR FIRST THREE TO SIX MONTHS

Ownership of Ad Accounts

Actively running client accounts across paid search and paid social without regular assistance from other buyers.

Accurate Reporting and Projecting

You've learned the ropes, you can accurately project a client's spend and ROAS across both Google and Meta.

Assisting Wherever Possible

You share your knowledge freely, assist accounts owned by non-Sr. buyers, and operate palms-down to help wherever you can.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TABLE

  • Significant experience creating and optimizing Google Ads accounts at scale. This is a top requirement; if you haven't done this, this role isn't for you
  • 2–4+ years of paid media experience managing budgets of $350,000+ across search and/or social
  • Expert-level knowledge of: Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, Google Merchant Center, Google Analytics, Shopify, and copywriting
  • Experience building, connecting, optimizing, and troubleshooting data feeds in Google Merchant Center
  • Experience integrating Product Ratings from various aggregators into Google Merchant Center
  • Ability to forecast budgets across channels based on historical data and client goals
  • Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills. You analyze data, make decisions, and build recs from it
  • Familiarity with Google Ads Desktop Editor
  • Ability to think about a brand's 360° digital approach from acquisition through retention
  • Confident interpersonal communicator. You can hold people accountable and lead difficult conversations
  • Insatiable curiosity. You can't leave a problem alone until you've found a solution
  • A desire to take calculated risks after carefully examining the calculus
  • A unique combination of humility (willing to do the dirty work) and ambition (vision for what's ahead)
  • Skilled in Asana or relevant project management software, preferred
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to organize, prioritize, and manage multiple tasks with great attention to detail
  • Ability to adapt to new processes, strategies, and goals

COMPENSATION

  • Bonus Structure: 10% of base salary

At CTC, we are fixated on building the next generation of legendary brands and the people who will lead them.

To give ourselves our best shot at accomplishing this mission, we organize all of our decisions — from recruiting, to hiring, to raises, to promotions, to how we spend our time and money — in the direction of three committed values.

Tutor Schedule:

Pay Rate: $45/hour for group sessions 1:4 - $32/hour for individual sessions 1:1
To be considered, interested applicants must be available for the entire 12-14 weeks

More specifics, depending on engagement, will be shared during the selection process.

Braintrust Tutors has a multi-step onboarding process requiring approximately 3–4 hours to complete. Summit’s team is inspired to touch and help change lives through Summit’s clinical studies in the field of oncology. Summit has multiple global Phase 3 clinical studies, including:

Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)

  • HARMONi: Phase 3 clinical study which was intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a 3rd generation EGFR TKI.

  • HARMONi-3: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

Colorectal Cancer (CRC)

Job Summary

The Admin Correspondence II agent provides knowledgeable written responses to Federal Student Loan (FSA) inquiries in a courteous and professional manner.

Job Duties and Responsibilities:
  • Work on assignments that are semi-routine in nature but recognize the need for occasional deviation from accepted practice.
  • Provide administrative support to project and operations management, which may include identifying, anticipating, and meeting needs of all departments.
  • Perform repetitive clerical steps.
  • Perform clerical duties requiring general knowledge and the application of various work methods and procedures.
  • Insert customer and account data by inputting text based and numerical information from source documents within specific time limits.
  • Interpret paperwork and make sound judgements based on information received.
  • Compile, verify accuracy, and sort information according to priorities to prepare source data for computer entry.
  • Review data for deficiencies and errors, correct any incompatibility and check output for accuracy.
  • Outreach to various sources via oral and written communication in order to make appropriate determination on a variety of tasks.
  • Must be able to effectively read a prepared/written script out loud.
  • Apply data program techniques and procedures to daily tasks.
  • Generate reports, store completed work in designated locations and perform backup operations.
  • Requires the review and examination of numerous source original documents from both image and hard copy which require keying of alphanumeric loan data into core system.
  • Interpretation of OMB structured, and unstructured forms based on processing procedures to properly classify and label forms into organized work lists.
  • Applicant will be required by contract to undergo program training as student financial assistance programs change.
Additional Requirements:
  • Must reside in the U.S.
  • Must be a U.S. Citizen.
  • Must be able to pass a criminal background check.
  • Must not be delinquent or in default on any federal student loans.
  • May be required to work scheduled holidays, overtime, and Saturdays.
  • Adhere to policies as they relate to protecting personally identifiable information
  • Must have the ability to write using proper grammar and punctuation.
  • Must have the ability to type a minimum of 23 WPM required.
  • Must have the ability to work independently and in a team environment.
  • Must have excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to organize simultaneous tasks.
  • Must be able to navigate Microsoft Excel spreadsheets.
  • Must have the ability to identify new scenarios and ask for guidance when none is available.
  • Must have a logical thought process.
  • Must be organized, take accurate notes, and refer to notes during processing.
  • Must welcome and can accept constructive/constant feedback.
  • Must have the ability to use resources and tools to effectively communicate: IM Chat, helpful guides/best practices, training material, SUM.
  • Preferred NSLDS usage experience (benefit but not required).
Security

Information and Physical Security is the responsibility of every employee. In your position you are required to safeguard the computer systems by following proper username and password management which includes selecting challenging passwords and committing them to memory, they should not be written down or stored where others can freely have access. This also includes securing your desk and workstation when you are not there. This includes locking your session and putting sensitive paperwork away when not physically at your desk. You are not to share your username or password with anyone. The physical security of our offices of are equal importance, never shadow or let someone shadow your entry into a Coast Professional, Inc. facility. If this occurs quickly report this action immediately. You are required to follow all Information Technology policies and procedures regarding the management of your system accounts and equipment. If you witness any security violation you should immediately report it to management.

Qualifications

Education

  • High school diploma or GED required.

Experience

  • At least one (1) year of customer service, administrative or call center experience required.
Clearance

As a federal contractor, this position requires U.S. citizenship and security clearance granting access to classified information. The background investigation is conducted by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and is an evaluation of the whole person to determine suitability. The suitability review begins after a conditional offer of employment has been accepted and will include a review of your employment, education, residences, references, criminal history and credit, as an example. Some of the most important factors in an investigation are the individual’s honesty, candor, and thoroughness in the completion of their security forms. In rare instances, non-U.S. citizens with highly specialized skills and experience may also be considered for the security clearance process.

Working Conditions

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this position, the physical presence in the workplace is essential. The employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Specific vision abilities required by this position include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, and the ability to adjust focus. The employee frequently is required to use hands or finger, handle, or feel objects, tools or controls. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.

Nothing in the herein restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

CAD Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Fully Remote-Open Worldwide

Schedule: 15-20 hrs/week. Fully flexible (Can accomodate after hours + weekends if needed)

In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required, your CAD domain knowledge is what matters.

Scope of Work

  1. Provide expert feedback on manufacturing processes and techniques, drawing on hands-on CAD experience (CAM and CNC workflows especially welcome).
  2. Review, assess, and refine AI-generated content and recommendations relevant to manufacturing workflows.
  3. Develop and validate detailed rubrics for evaluating manufacturing process accuracy and efficiency.

Required Qualifications

  1. Hands-on experience with any CAD platform (e.g. Fusion 360, AutoCAD, SolidWorks, Onshape, Inventor, CATIA, Creo).
  2. Strong written and verbal communication skills with an emphasis on clarity and detail.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Experience with Autodesk tools, particularly Fusion 360 or AutoCAD.
  2. Background in CAM, CNC machining, or digital manufacturing workflows.
  3. Python proficiency — a significant plus for this role.
  4. Familiarity with AI tools (LLMs, generative design, AI-assisted workflows) and comfort evaluating AI output.
  5. Experience developing or applying process evaluation rubrics.

Process:

  1. Apply to the role, filling out the screening questions
  2. Complete AI interview (aprox. 30 minutes)
  3. Hiring Manager review

Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.

Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

Job Type: Contractor (~15 hrs a week)

Location: Remote

Schedule: Flexible, you pick the hours and days (including weekends if desired)

Job Summary: In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.

As an expert you will be creating Reinforcement Learning Environments which test an AI model’s ability to solve complex software engineering problems using Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.   5. Proven ability to optimize software for performance and scalability.
  6. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a keen attention to detail.
  7. Track record of success in collaborative, cross-functional teams, ideally in remote settings.

Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Previous experience working on large-scale, distributed codebases.
  2. Familiarity with modern AI or machine learning systems is a plus, though not required.
  3. Background in participating in rigorous code reviews and contributing to the development of software best practices.
