jobs.title: Associate Director, Product Safety & Compliance
jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityCaraway Home is looking for an experienced Associate Director, Product Safety & Compliance to build our product compliance function from the ground up and own what we call the Caraway Promise, a testing-obsessed, transparency-first approach to product safety that sets the bar for the industry.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Caraway Home is looking for an experienced Associate Director, Product Safety & Compliance to build our product compliance function from the ground up and own what we call the Caraway Promise, a testing-obsessed, transparency-first approach to product safety that sets the bar for the industry. The Caraway Promise exists because we believe in transparency, not because the industry requires transparency.

This is a foundational role, the first dedicated compliance hire at Caraway, responsible for building the frameworks, lab relationships, testing strategy, supply chain diligence, claims substantiation, and regulatory sequencing across a diverse and growing product portfolio.You will own the full compliance lifecycle across Caraway's product categories (cookware, bakeware, electrical items, food contact materials, textiles, and packaging), always meeting or exceeding the most stringent applicable global standard to establish industry-leading Caraway protocols and procedures. You will be US-based, work closely with Asia-based suppliers and third-party labs (particularly in China), and build the internal systems and processes that let Caraway scale compliantly, credibly, and with confidence.

Additionally, an important responsibility of this role is disseminating key information, labels, and results to support marketing initiatives. You need to be a strong communicator, working collaboratively with cross functional teams, to broadcast and showcase the diligence Caraway is taking across its entire product portfolio in regards to compliance, being able to assist with crafting accurate, transparent, educational and understandable language and messaging that resonates with our consumer.

This position reports to our Director, Product Development.

Who You Are

You have ten or more years of product safety and regulatory compliance experience in consumer goods, ideally grounded in chemistry, materials science, or applied laboratory research, with deep expertise in food contact materials, cookware, kitchen appliances, or an adjacent hard goods category. You know FDA, LFGB, EU Framework Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004, REACH, CA Prop 65, CA AB 1200, NSF, FSC, and CPSC requirements not as acronyms on a checklist, but as frameworks you've navigated hands-on, including where global standards diverge. You’ll use this fluency to scale the Caraway Promise internationally: building a testing and compliance framework that anticipates global standards.

You are a builder and a scientist at heart, ready to own a compliance program entirely: selecting labs, building testing matrices, writing material certification requirements, establishing supplier audit cadences, and designing the studies needed to substantiate product claims. You operate comfortably across cultures and time zones, with direct experience working with labs and manufacturers in Asia, particularly China. You communicate complex science and regulatory requirements clearly to internal teams (Product, Marketing, Legal, Supply Chain) and external partners alike, and you see internal education as core to the job.

Responsibilities

  • Own and pioneer the Caraway Promise: define and champion a testing-obsessed, transparency-first approach to product safety that goes beyond what regulation requires, because we believe our customers deserve it.
  • Build Caraway's product safety and compliance program, defining frameworks, documentation standards, testing protocols, regulatory calendars, and governance processes across all product categories (cookware, bakeware, small appliances, food contact materials, textiles, and packaging); integrate compliance across the full product lifecycle, from development and supplier onboarding through market placement, ongoing monitoring, and end-of-life.
  • Own and continuously monitor regulatory compliance across US federal and state requirements (FDA food contact, CPSC, CA Prop 65, CA AB 1200, Colorado PFAS Act, and emerging state chemical legislation) and international standards (EU LFGB, EC No 1935/2004, REACH, RoHS, UK REACH post-Brexit), always applying the most stringent applicable standard; lead regulatory change management as a distinct workstream, assessing impact and briefing stakeholders ahead of deadlines.
  • Lead product component mapping and material disclosure, maintaining a complete picture of every material, coating, pigment, and component across Caraway's supply chain, including Declarations of Compliance, material safety data sheets, and test reports.
  • Design and manage Caraway's testing strategy, selecting and managing third-party labs (particularly in Asia, including NRTLs for small appliances), defining testing scope and frequency by product type and risk level, and sequencing testing within development timelines to avoid launch delays or costly late-stage findings.
  • Own claims substantiation: design and commission the clinical, laboratory, and comparative studies (for example migration testing, coating durability, comparative non-stick performance) needed to support our non-toxic, food-safe, and sustainability claims. Partner with Marketing and Customer Research on which claims to make and how to communicate them, and ensure all claims are legally defensible and compliant with FTC guidelines and retailer requirements (Target, Crate & Barrel, Bloomingdale's, etc.), including CA AB 1200 disclosure obligations.
  • Conduct supply chain compliance diligence, including BSCI and Sedex (SMETA) social compliance audits and material certifications (OEKO-TEX, FSC, GRS, GOTS); embed Caraway's material and safety standards directly into manufacturing quality plans in China so factory teams implement them consistently on the production line, not just on paper; manage supplier CAPA processes and produce performance reporting to inform sourcing decisions.
  • Serve as Caraway's internal subject matter expert on product safety and science, building internal education that embeds our standards into onboarding and cross-functional fluency by year one; act as the primary point of contact for retailers, certifying bodies, and regulatory agencies on compliance matters.
  • Own product incident management, leading investigations into consumer complaints and non-conformances, conducting root cause analysis, implementing CAPAs, and coordinating with Legal, Customer Experience, and Operations on any product withdrawal or CPSC recall process; maintaining documentation and reporting readiness for regulatory inquiries.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • 10+ years of product safety, regulatory compliance, or quality assurance experience in consumer goods, with at least 5 years focused on food contact materials, cookware, kitchen appliances, or closely adjacent hard-goods categories; demonstrated ownership across the full compliance lifecycle, from concept and supplier qualification through launch and incident response. No junior or generalist profiles.
  • Deep, working knowledge of food contact material regulations including FDA 21 CFR, LFGB (Chapters 30/31), EU Framework Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004, REACH, CA Prop 65, CA AB 1200, FSC, NSF, and the Colorado PFAS Chemicals Consumer Protection Act; familiarity with UK REACH and other international frameworks is a strong plus.
  • Background in chemistry, materials science, or applied laboratory and clinical research, with direct experience designing and running studies used to substantiate product safety or performance claims.
  • Demonstrated experience managing third-party lab relationships in Asia (China in particular), including test plan scoping, report interpretation, and navigating discrepancies between lab results and supplier-provided data.
  • Hands-on experience with social compliance and supply chain auditing programs, including BSCI and Sedex/SMETA (2- and 4-pillar); familiarity with material certification schemes (OEKO-TEX Standard 100, FSC, GRS, GOTS); skilled at managing CAPA processes and building supplier performance scorecards.
  • Proven ability to develop and manage product testing strategies, including migration testing, heavy metals (lead, cadmium), PFAS/PFOA screening, sensory evaluation, and applicable electrical safety standards (UL, ETL, IEC 60335) for small appliances.
  • Familiarity with FTC Green Guides and CPSC Section 15(b) reporting obligations, product recall mechanics, and the CPSC Fast Track Recall Program.
  • Ability to build and maintain product component maps and material traceability documentation across a multi-supplier, multi-category portfolio, including Declarations of Compliance, mill certificates, glaze and coating specifications, and batch-level test records.
  • Strong cross-functional communication and risk management skills; able to translate scientific and regulatory findings into clear, prioritized guidance for Product, Marketing, Legal, Sourcing, and Supply Chain, and to present compliance risk and status to senior leadership.
  • Demonstrated experience building compliance programs or functions in an environment with limited existing infrastructure; entrepreneurial by nature, with the ability to prioritize and execute without relying on inherited playbooks.
  • Ability to travel internationally to visit manufacturing partners and labs in Asia, up to 35 to 40% annually; experience working with facilities in China required, with additional familiarity across Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia) a plus.
  • Proficiency in Mandarin (spoken and/or written) is a bonus; at minimum, demonstrated effectiveness working through translation with Mandarin-speaking suppliers, factories, and lab contacts.
  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Food Science, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related field, with hands-on laboratory or clinical research experience a strong plus; advanced degree or professional certification (for example RAPS, ISO Lead Auditor) a plus.
  • Experience with small appliance safety standards (UL 60335-1, IEC 60335-2 series, ETL) preferred; experience managing certification processes with Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratories (NRTLs) a plus.
  • Familiarity with retailer compliance and vendor onboarding requirements (Target, Crate & Barrel, Bloomingdale's, Costco, Amazon) and the documentation standards they require from suppliers.

Please note that the duties and responsibilities outlined in this job description are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by employees assigned to this position. It is not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required for the role. Additional tasks and responsibilities may be assigned as needed to meet business needs.

jobs.excerpt: About The Greenwood ProjectAt Greenwood Project, we open doors in financial services for undergraduate freshmen.
jobs.description:
About The Greenwood Project
At Greenwood Project, we open doors in financial services for undergraduate freshmen. We give our scholars three things: social capital, the network that comes from knowing people inside the industry. Academic and technical capital, the training the work actually requires. And aspirational capital, the belief that the seat belongs to you.
This is not a workshop series. Scholars commit to twelve months of training, deliver real work on real deadlines, and finish knowing whether this industry is for them. Many go on to internships and full time offers at our partner firms. All of them leave with a network they did not have before.
The Fintech Academy
This academy trains the analytical and operational foundation underneath financial services: how markets are structured, how money actually moves through systems, where it breaks, and what the rules require. Financial services now hires analysts, operators, and risk professionals in the same numbers it hires traditional finance roles, and those jobs are open to people who did not start out in finance.
Where this training leads
These are the roles this academy prepares you for, and they hire sophomores and juniors in real numbers. Each one maps directly to what you will study.
• Fintech product and operations analysis. Working alongside product and operations teams to find what is broken, decide what matters most, and make the case for fixing it. This is the role our capstone puts you in.
•Trading operations. Everything that has to happen after a trade is agreed. Confirming it, clearing and settling it, making sure the right money and securities land in the right accounts, and finding the break when they do not. Trading desks cannot function without this, and it is one of the largest entry points into a firm.
• Operations more broadly. The rest of the machinery: onboarding clients, moving payments, reconciling accounts, handling corporate actions. When operations fails, it is expensive and public.
• Risk, compliance, and fraud. Figuring out what could go wrong, how likely it is, and how much it would cost. This includes fraud detection and the checks that confirm who a firm is doing business with.

Program Overview
We are recruiting 100 scholars into the Fintech Academy for the 2029 cohort. Across all three Greenwood academies we will select 325.
You are eligible if you are currently a freshman graduating in 2030. We call this the 2029 cohort because Summer 2029 is the internship you are working toward.
When What happens
  • October 2026 to June 2027: Rolling admissions. Decisions every month. November is the priority round.
  • July 2027: Academy begins.
  • July 2027 to June 2028: Twelve months of training, from the summer after freshman year through your sophomore year.
  • Fall 2028: Junior year internship recruiting season. Greenwood supports you through interviews.
  • Summer 2029: The goal: a 10 week internship with a partner firm, the summer after your junior year.
  • Spring 2030: You graduate.

How rolling admissions works
We review applications and make decisions every month from October 2026 through June 2027. You will hear back within 4 weeks of the round your application lands in. Seats fill as we go, so the earliest rounds have the most of them open. Apply early.
You get one application
You submit one application for this cohort. Not one per academy, and not one per round. Our Talent & Recruitment team may move you to a different academy than the one you selected if your answers point somewhere else, so you do not need to get that choice perfect.
Every application gets one of three outcomes:
  • Accepted. You are in.
  • Deferred. We want to see more before we decide, usually your next term of grades. Your application carries forward automatically and you do not need to submit anything new. You will hear from us about two weeks before the next round of decisions, and again every month until we decide. You will not sit in silence.
  • Declined. Final for this cycle. Because this program only admits freshmen, we cannot reconsider you in a later round.
Deferral is the reason you can apply in an early round without taking a risk. If we are not ready to decide, we hold your application. We will not turn you away for applying before your first semester was finished.
Deadlines in this process are real. Once you apply, we will ask you for things on a schedule: transcripts, forms, sometimes an interview time. If you miss those deadlines, your application is declined rather than delayed. We hold this line because the program itself runs on deadlines, and how you handle ours tells us how you will handle those.
Please read this carefully: Internship placements are not guaranteed. Greenwood trains you, advocates for you, and puts you in front of our partner firms. Those firms make their own hiring decisions. What we guarantee is the preparation, the network, and honest feedback. The offer is something you earn.

What You'll Study

No prior finance or technical experience is required. Real effort is. Each module below builds on the one before it, and you will be working with real deadlines throughout.
  • Basic Market Structure. OTC versus exchange systems, liquidity fundamentals, and the key elements of market structure. OTC means over the counter, where a trade happens directly between two parties instead of on a public exchange. Liquidity is how easily something can be bought or sold without moving its price.
  • Inside the FinTech Stack. [DESCRIPTION NEEDED. Awaiting context from team.]
  • Data-Driven Decision Making. Pre-trade, execution, and post-trade processes, including clearing, settlement, and reconciliation. This is the full life of a trade, from the decision to buy through to confirming that the money and the security actually changed hands.
  • Regulation & Risk. Fraud detection, KYC and AML, data privacy, and consumer protection. KYC means know your customer and AML means anti money laundering, the checks a firm runs to confirm who it is doing business with and where the money came from.
Capstone: AI-Powered Customer Insights Lab: Scholars act as members of a fintech product or operations team, analyzing mock customer feedback to identify pain points, prioritize issues, and present strategic recommendations to a simulated leadership audience.
Building AI Fluency
Fintech is where AI stopped being a pilot project. In a 2026 Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance survey, 21 percent of financial services firms already had AI agents running in production and 52 percent were piloting them. Agents are doing real work today in underwriting, fraud detection, compliance, and operations. That means two things for you. The entry level work that used to be manual is going away. And someone has to test, monitor, and be accountable for the systems doing it instead. That someone is who we are training you to be.
Hands on with real tools. You will not just learn concepts. You will build working skill with the software and AI tools used on the job. Each Greenwood academy trains a different technical toolset, chosen to match the roles that academy actually feeds, so what you build here is specific to the operations, risk, and product side of financial technology rather than a general overview.
The judgment we are after: knowing what should be automated, what should not, and who is responsible when an automated system gets it wrong. Firms are hiring for that question right now and struggling to fill the seats.

What We're Looking For - Ideal Degree Backgrounds

Your major does not decide which academy fits you. Your interest does. Plenty of freshmen have not declared yet, and some schools do not allow it until sophomore year. Neither works against you. Major titles also vary from school to school, so if yours is named differently but covers the same ground, it counts. Tell us what it is called where you are.
Fields of study that line up with this academy
  • Computer Science
  • Computer Engineering or Software Engineering
  • Engineering, any discipline
  • Information Systems, Management Information Systems, or Information Science
  • Data Science or Data Analytics
  • Mathematics or Statistics
  • Finance, Economics, or Business Analytics with a quantitative or technical focus
  • Operations, Supply Chain, or Industrial Engineering
  • Risk Management or Risk Management and Insurance, where your school offers it
  • Product and design adjacent fields, including Human Computer Interaction, Cognitive Science, or Design
If you have not declared a major yet
You can apply as undeclared. What we need to see is that you are seriously pointed toward operations, risk, product, or the technology side of financial services. Undeclared is not a weaker application. An undeclared student who can show us the following is stronger than a declared student who cannot:
  • Courses you have taken or registered for next term, such as intro programming, calculus, statistics, or information systems
  • Clubs and activities that back it up: a hackathon, a coding or robotics club, a data or analytics group, a product or startup club, or a technical campus job
  • Anything you have built or taught yourself, including a project, a script, an app, a dashboard, or a certificate
  • If product management is what you are after, anything where you decided what to build and had to defend the decision counts, including a club project, a small business, or an event you ran
  • A clear answer to why this academy and not the Investment Banking or Sales & Relationship Academy
If your major is not on this list
If you have taught yourself to code, or you are the person people come to when something breaks, apply and tell us about it. Self taught is not a disadvantage here. It is often the strongest signal we get.
Technical skills you will build
You are not expected to arrive with any of these. You are expected to want them.
  • Market structure literacy, meaning how exchanges and OTC markets work and how liquidity is provided
  • Trade lifecycle fluency, from pre-trade decisions through execution, clearing, settlement, and reconciliation
  • Data analysis and presenting numbers honestly, including making a chart that tells the truth
  • Product thinking, meaning writing a clear requirement, prioritizing what matters, and saying no to the rest
  • A working understanding of financial systems and the technology infrastructure underneath them
  • Analytical frameworks for risk assessment and operational efficiency
  • Structured problem solving, meaning breaking a vague problem into parts you can test
  • Excel and data manipulation, which you will use more than you expect
  • Regulatory literacy, including know your customer and anti money laundering checks, data privacy, and consumer protection
  • Working with AI tools and evaluating what they produce
Soft skills and characteristics
Greenwood selects scholars who show grit, resourcefulness, and intellectual curiosity, along with:
  • Strong analytical and logical reasoning
  • A systematic approach to problems, rather than guessing until something works
  • Attention to detail and a commitment to precision
  • The ability to explain something technical to someone who is not technical. This is the skill that gets people promoted.
  • A collaborative mindset, because this work is always cross functional
  • Adaptability, since the tools you learn this year will not be the tools you use in five years
  • A continuous improvement mindset, and the instinct to ask why a process works the way it does.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

What Makes a Strong Fintech Academy Candidate?

The strongest candidates take things apart to see how they work. You should be comfortable not knowing the answer, willing to sit with a problem longer than is comfortable, and interested in systems rather than only outcomes. You do not need a technical background. You do need to be willing to be new at something in front of other people, without quitting.
What this takes
  • Twelve months, from the summer after freshman year through your sophomore year, on top of a full course load.
  • Roughly 6 to 8 hours per week, with heavier weeks around project deadlines.
  • Technical work does not compress well. You cannot cram a project the night before and have it run.
  • Managing your class schedule around program commitments and staying organized without being chased.
Eligibility Requirements
  • Currently enrolled as a freshman (Class of 2030) at an accredited four year institution
  • Minimum 3.2 GPA for standard consideration
  • Students with a GPA between 3.0 and 3.19 may apply with a required personal essay
  • Students below a 3.0 GPA are not eligible for this cycle
  • Your high school transcript, submitted with your application
  • Your first semester or first quarter college transcript, submitted with your application or as soon as grades post if you apply in an early round
  • A demonstrated commitment to excellence, integrity, character, and collaboration
If your GPA falls between 3.0 and 3.19, the essay is not a formality. Tell us what the number does not capture, and be specific about what you changed.
If you apply in an early round before you have a college GPA, we review your high school record first and confirm eligibility once your first term transcript arrives

What You'll Gain

  • Work you can show, not just claim. You will finish the capstone with an analysis you built and can walk someone through in an interview.
  • AI capability most candidates do not have. Working with AI tools inside real operations and risk problems, plus the judgment to know when to override what they produce.
  • Range. These skills travel. Operations, risk, and product analysis exist at banks, exchanges, payments companies, asset managers, startups, and technology firms, and the foundation is the same in all of them. You do not have to know which one you want yet.
  • A real network. One on one coaching, a mentor in the industry, and access to professionals at our partner firms.
  • Proof you can learn hard things fast. That is what this year is really for, and what every future employer is trying to find out about you.

The Assistant Director, Regulatory Affairs, Advertising & Promotion will be the regulatory lead for advertising and promotional activities at Praxis, helping us communicate about our medicines with accuracy, integrity, and urgency as we work to bring high-impact treatments to patients with CNS disorders.

You will own the regulatory review and approval of promotional materials and partner closely with Commercial, Medical Affairs, Legal, Regulatory Strategy, and Regulatory Operations to build an efficient, rigorous, and scalable promotional review capability. This is a highly visible role for someone who brings strong regulatory judgment, communicates directly, and is comfortable making thoughtful decisions in a fast-moving environment.

Success in this role requires more than knowing the regulations. You will anticipate issues, challenge assumptions, find compliant paths forward, and help teams solve problems early rather than simply identifying risk at the end of the process. You will operate with significant autonomy and accountability while building trusted partnerships across Praxis.

jobs.title: Enterprise Sales Executive (Latam Region)
jobs.excerpt: About AlphaPointAlphaPoint is the infrastructure platform behind digital asset businesses worldwide.
jobs.description:
About AlphaPoint

AlphaPoint is the infrastructure platform behind digital asset businesses worldwide. Since 2013, we have powered exchanges, brokerages, banks, and fintechs across dozens of countries, giving them the trading, custody connectivity, tokenization, treasury, and settlement capabilities they need to operate in digital assets at institutional scale.

We are not a collection of products in a box. AlphaPoint is a single platform with many capabilities: one integration that lets a client offer trading, brokerage, treasury, and stablecoin workflows to their end users, connect to the liquidity venues, custodians, and banking partners of their choice, and expand into new use cases without re-platforming. Every super app needs a super platform underneath it. That is what we build.

About the Role

We are hiring a Sales Executive to open new markets for the AlphaPoint platform, with APEX (our trading and brokerage infrastructure) and APEX Treasury (our treasury and settlement layer) as the lead offerings. This is a new-business role. You will build your own pipeline, run complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles from first conversation to signature, and land accounts that grow with us as they add capabilities.

Our buyers fall into two groups. The first are firms launching a new exchange or brokerage and looking for the platform to build it on. The second, and larger, are firms that already have an established base of end users or assets and want to give those users access to digital assets: investment platforms and online brokers, asset managers and trading firms, private wealth and RIA platforms, fintechs adding crypto to an existing product, and the retirement channel, where brokers and IRA providers are bringing bitcoin ETFs and spot crypto to retirement accounts.

This is a builder role for someone with deep domain knowledge. You know how a broker-dealer, an asset manager, or a wealth platform actually works, what they need from a technology partner to launch digital assets, and who inside the building signs off on it. You can hold a first meeting with a CEO and a working session with a head of trading or a CTO in the same day, and you can teach a market what it should be asking for.

What You Will Do

  • Own new-business revenue for the AlphaPoint platform in your territory, selling APEX and APEX Treasury as an integrated platform rather than as standalone products, and consistently meet or exceed quota.
  • Build pipeline from scratch through your own network, targeted outbound, referral and partner channels, industry events, and content, with disciplined territory and account planning behind it.
  • Lead complex sales cycles with multiple stakeholders across business, product, technology, compliance, and legal, from discovery and solution design through commercial negotiation and contract close.
  • Develop and execute go-to-market plays for each target segment: investment platforms and brokers, asset managers and trading firms, private wealth, fintechs entering crypto, and retirement and IRA providers.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to prospects on how to structure a digital asset offering: which capabilities to launch first, how to integrate with existing systems and custodians, and how to stay within the regulatory perimeter in each market.
  • Partner with Solutions Engineers, Product, and Engineering to scope integrations and pilots, and bring structured market and client feedback back into the roadmap.
  • Work with Marketing on segment-specific campaigns, case studies, and events, and represent AlphaPoint at industry conferences and forums to build visibility and credibility in your markets.
  • Maintain an accurate, well-qualified pipeline and forecast in HubSpot, with clear next steps and close plans on every opportunity, and report weekly on pipeline health and progress to target.
  • Resourceful and hands-on: finds a way to move a deal forward regardless of the tools or processes in place, and helps build the playbooks the rest of the team will use.

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of B2B enterprise or institutional sales experience in capital markets technology, fintech, and digital asset infrastructure, with a track record of closing six-figure, multi-year contracts and consistently achieving quota.
  • Deep domain knowledge of at least two of our target segments: online brokerage and investment platforms, asset management and institutional trading, private wealth and RIA platforms, fintech, or the retirement and IRA channel. You understand how these firms are structured, how they make money, and how they buy technology.
  • Working knowledge of the digital asset ecosystem, including trading and execution, qualified custody, stablecoins and settlement, and the regulatory considerations that shape how regulated firms approach crypto.
  • Proven ability to build pipeline independently. You have opened new accounts and new segments before, not only worked inbound or an installed base.
  • An established network among decision-makers at financial institutions, brokers, wealth platforms, fintechs, or custodians, and a demonstrated ability to turn that network into qualified opportunities.
  • Technical fluency to engage credibly with CTOs, heads of trading, and product leaders on integration, APIs, and platform architecture, and to translate that into business outcomes for the C-suite.
  • Strong commercial and negotiation skills across complex, multi-stakeholder deal structures, including partner-dependent deals where a custodian or liquidity provider is part of the solution.
  • Experience navigating regulated environments and a commitment to the highest ethical and compliance standards.
  • A data-driven approach to managing your business: rigorous CRM hygiene, accurate forecasting, and comfort using analytics and AI tools to prioritize and work your territory.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the presence to present to executive audiences and the clarity to write a proposal a CFO will read.

Preferred

  • Experience selling trading, custody, or market infrastructure technology to broker-dealers, asset managers, or wealth platforms (for example, OMS/EMS, execution, clearing, or custody connectivity).
  • Existing relationships with qualified custodians, ETF issuers or distributors, IRA and retirement-account providers, or crypto-native liquidity providers.
  • Experience in a venture-backed or growth-stage fintech where you helped define the sales motion rather than inherit it.
  • Familiarity with white-label and API-first platform models and the economics of platform partnerships.

How We Work

You will report to the VP of Sales and work closely with a small, senior commercial, product, and solutions team. We value people who are direct, curious about how our clients’ businesses actually run, and generous with what they learn. We move quickly, own our outcomes, and treat every client as a long-term partner rather than a transaction.

Highlights:

Location: Turkey

Language: Fluent in Russian and English (C1+)

About Fundraise Up

We’re Fundraise Up - a global fundraising platform built to make donating to nonprofits fast, seamless, and accessible to all. Every month, our technology powers tens of millions of dollars in donations across the globe. We focus on innovation that directly impacts results: faster load times, higher conversion rates, global payment support, and accessibility-first design.

Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading nonprofits, including UNICEF, the Alzheimer’s Association, and a wide range of global NGOs. With a 4.9/5 rating across top software review platforms, we’re recognized not just for our impact - but for the quality of the product we deliver.

A Truly Global Product

We operate in the enterprise segment, serving nonprofit organizations across North America, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Europe.

We’re building a large and complex product ecosystem that serves nonprofits, donors, and partners around the world. The platform includes a modern checkout experience and customizable widgets (each a standalone SPA), donor, organization, and partner portals, admin tools, and several internal apps.

The Team

We are a distributed team of 160+ product professionals. Our team members are mainly based across Spain, Poland, Portugal, Georgia, Armenia, Serbia, Turkey, and Cyprus.

Despite our scale, we operate like a focused team - where every task matters and every voice is heard. We value thoughtful collaboration, strong engineering practices, and a product mindset. You’ll be joining a team where quality, mentorship, and mutual respect come first.

About In-Person Giving at Fundraise Up

In-Person Giving brings the quality and connected data of Fundraise Up’s online donation experience into physical fundraising moments.

The product begins with Tap to Donate and Giving Station: staff-led and self-service experiences that let nonprofits accept contactless donations at events, in public spaces, and through other offline workflows. Every transaction should connect to the same campaigns, donor records, reporting, CRM integrations, and operational controls used across Fundraise Up.

The next product direction is Events & Commerce. It includes ticket sales, check-in, merchandise and food purchases, symbolic purchases, auctions, paddle raises, and additional donations before and during an event. These capabilities must work as one connected fundraising system rather than another isolated event tool.

About the Role

We are hiring a Product Manager to own Events & Commerce within the broader In-Person Giving product line.

This is a hands-on software product role covering discovery, definition, delivery, launch, and iteration. You will turn a large category into a focused product direction grounded in customer workflows, live usage, and commercial evidence.

You will work closely with the PM responsible for the broader In-Person Giving area so that event commerce builds on the same payment, campaign, donor-data, reporting, mobile, and operational foundations as Tap to Donate and Giving Station. You will also partner with the Peer-to-Peer team where ticketing and event capabilities should be shared rather than rebuilt separately.

This is not an event-planning, sales, or internal project-coordination role.

What You’ll Own

Define the product direction

  • Turn customer research, market evidence, and business context into a clear Events & Commerce product thesis and sequenced roadmap.
  • Choose a focused target segment and event scenario rather than trying to replace every event platform at once.
  • Decide which capabilities belong in the shared In-Person Giving foundation and which require an Events-specific model.
  • Make explicit decisions about what Fundraise Up should build, integrate, partner on, or deliberately exclude.
  • Keep assumptions, success metrics, scope, risks, and product decisions visible.

Lead discovery and product definition

  • Work directly with nonprofit fundraising teams, event operators, finance teams, volunteers, attendees, donors, design partners, and internal GTM teams.
  • Map the complete workflow before, during, and after an event—including purchase, donation, check-in, fulfillment, reconciliation, reporting, and follow-up.
  • Validate decisions through interviews, workflow observation, prototypes, and live product usage.
  • Separate true adoption blockers from feature requests and expectations created by incumbent event platforms.
  • Shape problems such as ticket sales, QR-based check-in, guest management, commerce catalogues, FMV and receipts, on-site purchases, auctions, paddle raises, refunds, attribution, reporting, and integrations. These are examples—not a pre-committed feature checklist.

Shape and deliver the product

  • Own the product from problem definition through requirements, delivery, launch, and iteration.
  • Write clear requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases, state transitions, and decision records.
  • Make day-to-day scope and trade-off decisions with Engineering, Design, Analytics, Research, QA, and GTM partners.
  • Design for real event conditions: staff and volunteer operators, self-service flows, mobile devices, optional hardware, unreliable connectivity, high-volume moments, and operational recovery.
  • Ensure that event capabilities reuse Fundraise Up’s existing payments, campaign, donor, reporting, CRM, and identity infrastructure wherever possible.
  • Keep delivery predictable by surfacing dependencies, risks, and unresolved decisions early.

Launch, learn, and drive outcomes

  • Launch through EAPs with clear entry criteria, target workflows, success measures, readiness requirements, and out-of-scope areas.
  • Understand whether organizations can configure and run the target event workflows without heavy manual work or disconnected tools.
  • Measure whether attendees can purchase, check in, donate, and receive the right confirmation or receipt through a clear experience.
  • Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, CSM, Support, Finance, Legal, and Operations on positioning, commitments, enablement, and launch readiness.
  • Connect product evidence to activation, adoption, event completion, GPV, expansion, pipeline, retention, and operational cost.
  • Turn evidence into explicit recommendations: iterate, expand, change direction, partner, or stop.

Work AI-native

  • Use AI for research synthesis, workflow analysis, prototyping, specification quality, data exploration, and operational automation.
  • Build testable artifacts quickly without outsourcing product judgment.

Requirements

  • 4–7 years of Product Management or Product Ownership experience in a software product company.
  • End-to-end ownership of a customer-facing product area with Engineering and Design.
  • Strong judgment in reducing a large problem space to a focused release and explaining the trade-offs.
  • Experience turning customer evidence and product data into decisions.
  • Clear written communication across requirements, edge cases, metrics, and decision records.
  • Ability to work with transactional, multi-actor workflows involving permissions, states, money, and data relationships.
  • High ownership and independence, with fluent written and spoken English.

Strong plus

  • Experience with ticketing, event technology, commerce, POS, payments, marketplaces, registration, auctions, or other transaction-heavy products.
  • Experience with mobile applications, contactless payments, physical devices, or hardware-enabled workflows.
  • Experience with B2B SaaS, fundraising, nonprofits, or other operationally complex customer environments.
  • Experience launching a new product area through beta or EAP.
  • Knowledge of CRM integrations, financial reconciliation, reporting, transaction attribution, analytics, or SQL.
  • Practical use of AI for research, prototyping, analysis, or product operations.

This Role May Not Be a Fit If

  • You are looking for an event-planning or internal project-management role rather than software product ownership.
  • You prefer to receive a fully defined roadmap and requirements instead of helping determine what should be built.
  • You want to work only on strategy and avoid specifications, QA, delivery details, or post-launch iteration.
  • You treat every customer request as a roadmap commitment.
  • You need stable scope and certainty before moving forward.
  • You measure progress mainly by features shipped rather than customer and business outcomes.

Why work with us

  • Build a new product direction from research through live customer use.
  • Work in a large, proven fundraising category with clear customer demand and meaningful commercial potential.
  • Shape ticketing and event commerce as part of a broader fundraising platform rather than an isolated event tool.
  • Work with real nonprofit customers, rich product evidence, and experienced cross-functional partners.
  • Join a small team where product managers have meaningful ownership and direct access to Product leadership.
  • Help define an AI-native approach to product management in practice.
  • Build technology that helps nonprofits engage more supporters and raise more money for their missions.

Compensation

  • The compensation range for this role is $4,600 - $5,000 gross.
  • Final compensation will be determined based on relevant experience, skills, qualifications, alignment with the role’s requirements and location.

Benefits

  • 31 days off

  • Relevant professional education

About Virtru:

While the rest of the security industry obsesses over locking data down to prevent it from being lost or stolen, we're doing something fundamentally different at Virtru. We're setting data free so that you can intentionally share it with others, but without sacrificing security, privacy, or control.

We've created both a suite of powerful data protection applications and an open platform that's sparking an ecosystem of innovation. Through the Trusted Data Format (TDF) open standard, we're not just protecting data; we're creating a new paradigm where security enables sharing rather than preventing it.

Think of us as the Android of data protection: a robust platform with an open core that developers and partners can build upon, coupled with our own best-in-class applications that showcase what's possible when you reimagine security from the ground up.

Backed by Iconiq Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Foundry Capital, and Tiger Global, we're helping Fortune 500 companies and government agencies discover that true data security means having the freedom to share, collaborate, and innovate — without compromise.

Compensation: $180,000-220,000/year

Team & Position Details:

We are seeking a Data Warehouse & Analytics Architect with deep site reliability engineering (SRE) experience, who is dedicated to architectural excellence and technical leadership for Virtru's digital privacy products. The ideal candidate will have a natural passion for digital privacy, data architecture, and delivering exceptional technical solutions. You'll have the opportunity to work with and mentor a stellar team of passionate engineers who are collaborative, cohesive, and dedicated to producing high-quality results. We encourage curiosity and have a culture that encourages growth. As a Technical Architect on this team, you will be on the cutting edge of Zero-Trust - the future of data and service protection!

Technical Health & Quality:

  • Monitor and improve technical debt across all engineering teams, related to data storage, processing and site reliability

Technical Leadership & Mentorship:

  • Coach and mentor engineers on data storage, warehouse, processing, and SRE systems architecture, and best practices
  • Lead by example through high-quality code contributions to critical or complex components
  • Share knowledge of hyperscale data warehouse/lakehouses, data models, and emerging technologies with the team
  • Assist SRE teams with improving stability, automation, and scalability
  • Conduct code reviews with focus on architectural alignment and quality
  • Support hiring processes and technical assessments for engineering candidates

Collaboration & Strategic Partnership:

  • Partner with Engineering Managers through regular 1:1s and team planning sessions
  • Collaborate with product management, UX, and other architects to design and deliver new software solutions
  • Work with other Technical Architects to identify and resolve cross-team dependencies and technical challenges
  • Ensure technical roadmap alignment with product and business priorities
  • Participate in and contribute to platform-wide architectural initiatives

Execution:

  • Take ownership of the entire lifecycle and toolchain of all data components from design through deployment
  • Contribute to critical technical implementations, balancing hands-on coding with architectural responsibilities
  • Work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment touching a variety of projects and products
  • Build software that will meaningfully impact how people approach data privacy

Skills that will help you thrive in this role:

Technical Expertise:

  • Strong knowledge of cloud data warehouses (BigQuery, Redshift, Synapse, and Snowflake)
  • Strong experience with lakehouse platforms (Apache Iceberg, Databricks, Delta Lake, or Hudi)
  • Deep understanding of data modeling techniques (Kimball, Data Vault, or dimensional modeling)
  • Experience with columnar storage formats (Parquet, ORC)
  • Strong knowledge of batch and stream processing architectures
  • Deploying AI analytics at scale
  • SRE principles and practices
  • Experience with infrastructure as code (Terraform)
  • Proficiency in containerization and orchestration (Kubernetes)
  • Knowledge of monitoring and observability tools (Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana, or similar)
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices

Architectural & Leadership Skills:

  • Demonstrated experience leading architectural design and technical direction for engineering teams
  • Proven ability to influence without authority and drive technical decisions across teams
  • Strong technical mentoring and coaching experience
  • Experience creating architectural documentation, design documents, and technical specifications
  • Track record of improving technical health metrics and reducing technical debt
  • Experience with cross-team collaboration and dependency management

Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related technical discipline (or equivalent experience)
  • At least 7 years of data warehouse, database, or data processing and analytics experience
  • Proven experience in architectural or technical leadership roles

Communication & Collaboration:

  • Excellent ability to communicate clearly and concisely, both verbally and in writing
  • Strong presentation skills and ability to articulate complex technical concepts to diverse audiences
  • Experience with stakeholder management and aligning technical decisions with business context
  • Motivated by delivering customer value, team impact, and technical excellence

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience architecting Microsoft 365 add-ins with focus on security, performance, and user experience
  • Knowledge of data privacy, encryption, and zero-trust security models
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and modern DevOps practices
  • Contributions to open-source projects or technical community involvement

Virtruvian qualities that will set you up for success:

  • Comfortable with asynchronous communication including slack, email, zoom, etc.

  • A Flexible PTO policy — we strongly encourage you to take time off (in addition to 14 holidays) to ensure that you are getting the proper time needed to unplug and recharge.

In addition to wellbeing, Virtru places a strong emphasis on diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. Our DB&I Council is dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace and making the psychological safety of each and every one of our teammates a top priority.

  • 401K contribution and stock options

jobs.description:
GHX is seeking a Software Engineer III to join Developer Platform & AI Enablement, the team that builds the tooling, standards, and AI capabilities the rest of GHX core product engineering runs on. Reporting to the Director, Software Engineering, Developer Platform & AI Enablement, you’ll work on a small team whose customers are other engineers: the developers building the healthcare supply chain products that take more than a billion dollars out of the cost of delivering healthcare every year.

The SWE III is responsible for analyzing, design, program, debugging, and modifying software. This role is responsible for interacting with users to define system requirements and/or necessary modifications in an Agile/Scrum environment. You’ll grow into owning a capability end to end: a surface of the GHX agent platform, an MCP server other teams depend on, or the complexity-based router that decides whether a request runs on a local model or a hosted one. This is an embedded role, you’ll spend most weeks inside a product engineering team’s repository proving out a pattern before bringing the reusable version back to the broader engineering teams.

Duties and responsibilities

  • Analyzes, designs, programs, debugs, tests, documents, releases, and supports platform capabilities end to end.
  • Authors technical designs and architectural artifacts, and reviews the designs of peers.
  • Develops, versions, and documents reusable GitHub Actions and composite actions used across the organization.
  • Develops, versions, and documents reusable terraform modules (or other IaC) used across the organization.
  • Builds and operates MCP servers over stdio and remote/HTTP transports, owning tool schema design, transport selection, and authentication.
  • Extends our internal agent platform, including the SDK and the APIs other GHX teams build against, and contributes to local model routing.
  • Reads and safely modifies unfamiliar codebases, including Java and Maven builds, without owning the application code.
  • Drives defects and blockers to resolution, and writes automated tests and system test specifications.
  • Instruments developer-facing tooling to measure adoption and extends the team’s delivery-metrics pipeline.
  • Participates in architectural design spikes, project planning, and estimation in an Agile/Scrum environment.
  • Co-facilitates recorded AI in Automation Office Hours remotely each week.
  • Facilitating live sessions, both remote and in person, is an essential function of this role.
  • Actively uses AI-powered development tools to improve productivity and code quality, and authors the agent configuration artifacts other engineers reuse.
  • Create and maintain documentation as part of development and enablement efforts.
  • Stay up-to-date on industry trends and best practices related to Snowflake, Python, and AWS.
  • May mentor and onboard new team members as needed.

Required Qualifications

  • BS or MS Degree in Computer Science.
  • Requires 3-5 years of software development experience
  • Experience building internal tooling whose users were other engineers, with the ability to explain why a given tool was or was not adopted.
  • Daily use of agentic coding tools — Claude Code (preferred), Copilot, Cursor, or similar.
  • Direct experience authoring GitHub Actions at the reusable workflow or composite action level, or equivalent CI that other people consumed.

  • Technical writing that other engineers act on — design documents, ADRs, runbooks, or documentation you can point to.
  • Willingness to teach live and unscripted, including co-facilitating recorded remote sessions and full-day in-person workshops.
  • Willingness and ability to travel as needed.
  • Must be able to work independently and as part of a team on multiple overlapping projects.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Has measured a non-deterministic system and argued from the numbers — an eval harness, a benchmark, or a rubric.

  • Comfortable deploying and debugging on AWS
  • An agent configuration artifact you authored that another engineer used — a skill, subagent, md/AGENTS.md, or MCP tool.
  • Experience with local or open-weight inference: Ollama, llama.cpp, or MLX, quantization tradeoffs, context and KV-cache sizing, and OpenAI-compatible shims.
  • Experience measuring developer outcomes: adoption instrumentation, DORA-style delivery metrics, and data plumbing behind messy organizational data.
  • Experience with the healthcare supply chain, EDI documents and standards, an added advantage.

jobs.title: Full-Time Telehealth Dietitian (Salary + Benefits) Pacific Time
jobs.excerpt: Simplex Health is seeking a Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) to provide telehealth outpatient medical nutrition therapy using an integrative and functional nutrition approach.
jobs.description:
Simplex Health is seeking a Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) to provide telehealth outpatient medical nutrition therapy using an integrative and functional nutrition approach. This is a fully remote, full-time role offering a consistent schedule and the opportunity to build deep, ongoing relationships with patients.

Unlike many outpatient roles, this position offers a full-time, salaried structure with benefits, providing stability and consistency in your schedule and income—while giving you the flexibility to choose a schedule that fits your lifestyle.

The ideal candidate has experience in clinical or outpatient nutrition counseling, is licensed (or eligible for licensure) in Pennsylvania, and is passionate about delivering personalized, root-cause care to support long-term health outcomes.

Our Mission: Radically improve the health of Humankind—one person, one appointment, one connection at a time.

At Simplex Health, we do things differently. Our insurance-funded medical nutrition therapy goes beyond symptom management to improve — and in many cases reverse — chronic conditions. We partner with hospitals, healthcare practices, and individuals to provide personalized, root-cause nutrition care across a wide range of conditions, including metabolic health, digestive disorders, hormonal imbalances, and chronic disease.

Our approach is grounded in prevention, root-cause resolution, and sustainable lifestyle change, supporting patients throughout their health journey. Through a fully virtual, telehealth model, we meet patients where they are, delivering accessible, high-quality care.

Our evidence-based, progressive nutrition interventions are tailored to each patient’s unique biochemistry. Through nutrition counseling, education, and health coaching, we empower patients to improve their health, build lasting habits, and achieve meaningful, long-term outcomes.

Role details:

  • Location: Telehealth
  • Schedule Options: Choose between a 4-day (32-hour) or 5-day (40-hour) work week, with flexibility to design a schedule that fits both your preferences and your patients’ needs.
  • Reports to: Clinical Manager
  • Compensation:
    • 32 hours/week (4-day work week): $44,000–$59,000 annually
    • 40 hours/week (5-day work week): $55,000–$70,000 annually
    • Final schedule and compensation are aligned based on candidate preference, experience, and availability

You love helping people heal. You just don’t love doing it all alone.

If you’ve ever run (or dreamed of running) your own private practice, you know what it takes — the marketing, the scheduling, the billing, the insurance headaches, the empty calendar days, the tech issues, the isolation…

At Simplex Health, you get the best parts of private practice — the autonomy, the flexibility, the deep 1:1 relationships with patients — without the burnout or business stress.

Here, you get to focus on what you do best: helping patients transform their health through integrative and functional nutrition.

What we are looking for:
We are seeking mission-driven dietitians (RD/RDN) who:

  • Are passionate about integrative and functional nutrition
  • Thrive in a collaborative, growth-minded environment
  • Have at least 2 years of experience in outpatient or clinical care
  • Hold current registration with CDR
  • Are credentialed or open to being credentialed with insurance companies
  • Want to spend more time with patients and less time running a business
  • To avoid conflicts of interest, candidates should not maintain an active private practice or independent nutrition counseling business

Preferred:

  • Availability for evening appointments strongly preferred to meet patient demand, with flexibility based on individual scheduling needs.
  • CDCES (Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist) strongly preferred
  • IFNA Certified (IFNCP credential a plus); candidates actively enrolled in IFNA training welcome

PA license and completion of major insurance credentialing required before start; this process may take 3–6 months.

Role Responsibilities (including but not limited to):

  • Provide telehealth medical nutrition therapy using a functional and integrative approach
  • Implement Simplex Health protocols, tools, and educational materials in patient care
  • Assess the nutritional health of patients/clients and develop personalized, root-cause care plans
  • Create and modify individualized nutrition interventions based on patient needs and goals
  • Document all new and follow-up appointments in the Healthie platform with strong attention to detail
  • Respond to patient communications in a timely, professional, and supportive manner
  • Collaborate with team members through case discussions, meetings, and shared learning opportunities
  • Communicate openly and effectively to resolve work-related issues and support team outcomes
  • Contribute to a positive, collaborative team environment and ongoing clinical initiatives
  • Adhere to all company policies, procedures, and clinical standards
  • Stay current with emerging research and best practices in nutrition and health
  • Manage a full and consistent patient caseload, ensuring timely follow-ups, continuity of care, and optimal patient outcomes

What to expect:

At Simplex Health, you’ll have access to:

  • Structured onboarding and training
  • Regular case reviews and clinical collaboration
  • Real-time support via team chat and peer connection
  • Team meetings and shared learning opportunities
  • Opportunities to contribute to committees, resources, and clinical initiatives
  • Credentialing: If you’re not yet in-network, our team fully manages the insurance credentialing process on your behalf, including covering all associated fees and handling the paperwork.
  • Ramp-Up To Full-Time: This role begins in a ramp-up phase with variable hours as your patient caseload grows, transitioning into a full-time, salaried schedule once full-time metrics are met. Our team provides consistent referrals and support to help you build a full and sustainable schedule as quickly as possible.

Benefits

  • Flexible Scheduling: Choose between 32 or 40 hours per week, with the ability to structure your schedule in a way that works best for you and your patients
  • 4-Day Work Week (32 hours): A condensed schedule option designed to support balance, energy, and sustainability
  • Supplement Commissions: Earn 12.5% of MSRP on supplements purchased through Fullscript, providing additional earning potential.
  • Performance-Based Bonus Opportunities: Earn additional income based on patient retention and face-to-face care time.
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • 401(k) (after 90 days)
  • Discretionary Holiday Break: Office closed between Christmas and New Year’s
  • Fitness Allowance: Partial reimbursement for gym memberships, fitness classes, or wellness activities
  • Simplex Wellness on Demand: Free access to virtual fitness programs

Time Zone & Schedule:

Our operations and patient base are primarily in Eastern Standard Time (EST). Candidates in Pacific or Mountain time zones have the unique advantage of working standard daytime hours in their local time zone while providing essential evening coverage for our East Coast patients. Please note that administrative support is available from 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM EST, and while live attendance at team meetings is encouraged, recordings will be provided for those unable to join due to time zone differences.

Key Intangible Characteristics of the Ideal Candidate:

Called: A passion for our mission and a sense that this role and company are a strong fit for the blessings of your gifts, talents, passions, and experiences.. Must be mission-motivated with a resolve to overcome obstacles, anchored in a sense of purpose in this work.

Servant Leadership: Nobody is above any task, and we are all here to serve others. Every customer—internal or external—needs help, and the most powerful way to lead will be to serve.

Learning and Adaptive: As a startup with a big mission, new systems, technology, and situational adaptability are expected. This person must have an appetite for learning and skill improvement.

Grit, Resourcefulness & Entrepreneurial Spirit: Not everything will have a pre-planned solution. This person will have to be resourceful in figuring things out, resist feeling overwhelmed, and be willing to roll up their sleeves to make things happen. This person will have to have an open mind and good resolve, whether it’s looping in other people, finding answers online, or seeking best practices.

Organizational Skills: Being or becoming a constant organizational force. It will require a capacity for being open to change, discerning better processes, and prioritizing for improved outcomes.

Chemistry Fit: We have a unique and fun culture—we laugh, press in, work hard, and jump in to figure things out. Fitting into the team chemistry is essential.

High Character: We operate with a high trust culture. Personal values must fuel our work. Integrity, honesty, compassion, reconciliation, and diligence are all things this person must possess to flourish.

Energy & Enthusiasm: This person must bring joy and passion for work to the job. Encouraging and spurring on others on the mission while being self-motivated and positive is essential.

Multitasking: This is not a steady-state or static environment. Workflow will cycle, and interruptions are normal, so this person must be able to juggle and adjust on the fly.

Project Management: While multitasking, this person must be able to keep an eye on deadlines and critical dependencies, working to preserve them or source support proactively.

🌟 Why Dietitians Choose Simplex Health

Because great clinicians deserve great support.

🧾 We Handle Credentialing & Licensing
We cover insurance credentialing costs and reimburse for out-of-state license fees.

🎓 CEU Reimbursement
We invest in your professional growth and continued learning.

💻 Technology Reimbursement
Support for the tools you need to work efficiently and effectively.

💲 Recruitment Thank You Bonus
Bonus for any referrals hired by Simplex Health who stay at least 90 days

📋 Consistent Referrals & Quality Resources
A steady patient flow and high-quality patient-facing materials to support your care.

👥 Helpful Support Team & Quick Response Times
From scheduling to tech help, our support staff makes your day run smoother.

🌿 Approachable Leadership & Collaborative Culture
Leaders who listen, and a clinical community that truly supports one another.

🤝 Opportunities Beyond Patient Care
Get involved with social media, engagement projects, or hosting lunch & learns.

🌎 Broad Range of Clients, Deep Skill Development
Grow your counseling skills and confidence across a variety of cases.

💞 Strong Sense of Community
Even in a virtual environment, you’ll feel connected, encouraged, and supported.

If you’ve ever wished you could combine the freedom of private practice with the camaraderie and stability of a larger organization, this is where you belong.

Apply today and rediscover the joy of patient care without the grind of running a business.

Simplex Health Core Values:

Simplex Health strives to embody the following values and to apply them to every aspect of how we run our business, including how we interact with each other as teammates and leaders. These values also apply to how we interact with and continue to inspire our clients and strategic partners:

We Inspire Each Other
You are an important part of our team and together we make a collective intention to uplift and commit to one another. Through cultivating genuine, transparent, relationships, we create an environment that encourages individuals to dream big, take risks, and be bold. We aim to inspire and commit to everyone we touch. This sense of commitment and care sets the stage for a culture of accountability, where we hold ourselves and each other to the same high standards, taking the ownership necessary for achieving our goals.
Therefore encourage one another and build each other up, just as in fact you are doing.
1 Thessalonians 5:11

We Always Learn and Grow
We at Simplex Health strive to be continual learners and to expand our abilities as people and as an organization. We educate ourselves, remain curious, and use evidence-based research to challenge our current understanding. We see mistakes and failure as great teachers and learning opportunities. When we stay engaged in the world with a growth mindset, it creates the right environment for us to thrive and make a meaningful impact on each other and on the world.
Let the wise hear and increase in learning, and the one who understands obtain guidance.
Proverbs 1:5

We Think Big Picture What we do day in, day out, how we do it, and the decisions we make- shape who we are as a people and as a company. The details are super important, AND should always be guided by our wide perspective and an understanding of how we are impacting each other, our clients, and our business. Before making any major decision, ask yourself:

• Does it help us grow? How?

• Does it answer “how are we different and why should you care?”
• Is what I’m working on duplicatable and transferable (ie can I duplicate it and apply to other situations)? How?
• Does it challenge the status quo?
• Does it inspire?
• Does it tightly align with and advance our mission? How?
• Can it be more humanized and relatable?
• Does it unite us? How?
• Does it solve a problem? How?
Now we see things imperfectly, like puzzling reflections in a mirror, but then we will see everything with perfect clarity. All that I know now is partial and incomplete, but then I will know everything completely, just as God now knows me completely.
I Corinthians 13:12

We Challenge the Status Quo:
We are inquisitive by nature. We are courageous! We are not afraid to go against the grain in our search for truth. We always question conventional wisdom- it’s how Simplex Health started- it’s what we do.
Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will. Romans 12:2

We Cultivate Health and Vitality:
Being alive in a body is an incredible, temporary experience. Even though at times we feel pain and face challenges, our next breath is not guaranteed and is a HUGE gift. We experience EVERYTHING through our bodies, including thoughts, emotions, spirit, and our inspiration. We see health and vitality as the foundation for living a life that is happy, fulfilled, present, and productive.
Dear friend, I pray that you may enjoy good health and that all may go well with you, even as your soul is getting along well.
3 John 1:2

We Embody Integrity:
We communicate with transparency and face conflict head-on. We do this with the understanding that we respect each other and recognize that we are on the same team working toward a unified noble mission with shared goals. We don’t compromise our morals or integrity no matter the context. When challenging scenarios arise, we approach them with honesty and trust that we are all holding the highest intentions, are committed to our values, and are making best efforts.
Do to others as you would have them do to you.
Luke 6:31

We Simplify the Complicated:
We believe that complex problems don’t always require complex solutions. By simplifying the complicated and offering digestible, scalable solutions, we can pay more attention to the things that matter most. Every mind is unique. Yet much of the world is still built for what’s considered "normal," leaving too many people behind. At Everway, we change that by creating technology that helps everyone understand and be understood. By understanding and addressing the unique needs of each individual, we're creating a world where differences are recognized and valued.

Our careers fit real life. When you join us, you’re not just taking a job. You’re joining a movement to build a more neuroinclusive world. We’re a global community of over 800 employees spanning North America, UK, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. A career here is purposeful and fast-moving, with clear expectations, modern tools, and the clarity to focus on what matters most.

Our people are supported and encouraged to show up as they are, with different ways of thinking welcomed and valued. We pride ourselves on our core values that are embedded within our culture. These are to be curious, have courage, and commit fully.

Join us at Everway - together, we can unlock the full potential of every mind.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Product Designer to help shape how technology empowers neurodivergent individuals and people with physical, sensory and other disabilities.

You'll work across Everway's portfolio of special education and assistive technology solutions for school and workplace environments, collaborating closely with Product Management, Engineering, Research, Content and other cross-functional partners.

A key focus of this role will be our IEP product portfolio, including Polaris, Embrace Education and Spedtrack. You'll work across interconnected products and experiences, helping create coherent, accessible and scalable solutions that support the needs of educators, administrators and students.

This role offers the opportunity to think beyond individual features and products. You'll help shape shared experiences and interaction patterns across the portfolio, balancing consistency with the unique context and needs of individual products and users.

You'll lead end-to-end design work, from understanding complex problems and synthesising research through ideation, prototyping, validation and delivery. You'll contribute to product strategy, design quality and our design system, while exploring practical applications of AI and emerging technologies.

You'll also work closely with other designers, providing senior design partnership, sharing knowledge and helping raise design quality across the portfolio.

This is an opportunity to have a significant influence on the future of Everway's IEP experiences and help create accessible, coherent and high-quality products that make a meaningful difference to the people who use them.

Main responsibilities

In this role, you will:

  • Collaborate with cross-functional partners across Product, Engineering, Research, Content and Marketing to deliver product experiences that meet user and business needs.
  • Own end-to-end design work within your scope, contributing design expertise to product decisions from early discovery through delivery and iteration.
  • Help frame problems, identify opportunities and contribute design insight to product strategy and planning.
  • Design across interconnected products, workflows and user journeys to create scalable and coherent experiences.
  • Translate user insights, product analytics and business objectives into intuitive, accessible and scalable design solutions.
  • Work closely with Engineering to understand technical constraints and opportunities, ensuring solutions are practical, scalable and effectively implemented.
  • Contribute to and evolve Everway's design system, supporting consistency, scalability and accessibility across products.
  • Explore and apply AI where it creates meaningful value, improving design workflows, accelerating prototyping and supporting new product experiences, while considering usability, accessibility, trust, transparency and user control.
  • Create and present design concepts, prototypes and solutions with clear rationale linked to user, product and business objectives.
  • Advocate for inclusive design and ensure work meets or exceeds relevant accessibility standards.
  • Partner with researchers to integrate user insights into iterative design and validation cycles.
  • Balance qualitative user insights with quantitative product analytics to inform design decisions and measure the success of shipped experiences.
  • Facilitate workshops, design reviews and co-creation sessions with peers and stakeholders.
  • Share knowledge and contribute to design practice, learning and innovation across the UX and Product organisation.

Essential criteria

  • Significant product design experience, including 3+ years operating at Senior Product Designer level, with a strong portfolio demonstrating how design decisions contributed to measurable user, product or business outcomes.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with ambiguity, frame complex problems and influence product direction.
  • Experience applying inclusive and universal design principles, reducing cognitive load, and designing to recognised accessibility standards, including WCAG 2.2
  • Experience designing across interconnected products, complex workflows or end-to-end user journeys while considering the wider product ecosystem.
  • Hands-on experience contributing to and evolving design systems.
  • Strong prototyping and interaction design skills, with the ability to use prototypes to explore, test and communicate ideas.
  • Proficiency in modern design tools such as Figma.
  • Familiarity with AI-enhanced design workflows and an understanding of emerging human-AI interaction patterns, including trust, transparency, uncertainty and user control.
  • Ability to communicate and influence design decisions clearly across a range of stakeholders.
  • Strong collaboration with Product Management and Engineering, balancing user needs, business goals and technical constraints.
  • Understanding of modern product development approaches such as Agile, Lean UX, continuous discovery and iterative delivery, with experience facilitating collaborative design activities.

Desirable criteria

  • Experience designing across Web, iOS and Android in a complex SaaS environment.
  • Experience designing products for education, accessibility, assistive technology or other complex user needs.
  • Experience designing or shipping AI-enabled product experiences.
  • Experience using AI-assisted prototyping or design-to-development workflows.
  • Experience working with product analytics and experimentation to evaluate product outcomes.
  • Familiarity with designing for enterprise, education or multi-user environments with complex permissions, roles or workflows.
